To date, noise characterizations within the MC field have predominantly drawn from methodologies found in wireless communications literature. In this study, we diverge from existing MC research by utilizing a newly developed experimental platform that employs yeast, allowing us to consider more realistic noise characterizations based on the relevant signaling pathways. We propose suitable signal detection mechanisms tailored to this experimental setup, which focuses on yeast cell-to-cell communications. Our analysis identifies gene transcription as the primary source of noise, and we utilize a Markov birth-death process model with Poisson arrivals and departures to characterize it. The noisy expression of the FUS1 gene is best represented using a mixed Gaussian distribution model. This model serves as a foundation for evaluating the performance of Maximum Likelihood Detection mechanisms in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) for both symbol-by-symbol and sequence transmission schemes. Error analysis indicates that appropriate adjustments to the signal threshold can reduce errors to as low as 10%, which is not negligible. In contrast, the detection of symbol sequences demonstrates enhanced error performance, achieving error rates as low as 0.4%, albeit at the cost of increased computational complexity.

papers.title: Enriched nerves, interleaving distances and the multiplicative magnitude-path spectral sequence
papers.abstract: By regarding the nerves of categories enriched over a monoidal poset as persistence simplicial sets, we investigate an upper bound of the interleaving distance in the homotopy category between the nerves in the sense of Lanary and Scoccola. In particular, it holds that the distance between the nerves for $r$-homotopy equivalent generalized metric spaces is less than or equal to the half of $r$. Moreover, a product on the cochain complex associated with a persistence simplicial set is introduced and related to the cup product on the magnitude cochain complex in the sense of Hepworth. As a consequence, the product gives the multiplicative structure to the cohomological magnitude-path spectral sequence (MPSS) whose first term is isomorphic to the magnitude cohomology ring. Furthermore, we discuss at which term the MPSS for a connected finite digraph collapses by using the interleaving of the enriched nerve of the digraph.

papers.title: Normalized solutions for logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equations on graphs
papers.abstract: We study a logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equation with prescribed $L^2$ mass on connected locally finite weighted graphs, with $p > 2$. By minimizing the energy, we obtain a positive solution for every prescribed mass $m > 0$ on finite graphs and, under additional assumptions on the vertex measure and the potential, on infinite graphs. We describe the behavior of positive solutions and their Lagrange multipliers as $m \to 0^+$ or $m \to +\infty$. In particular, as $m \to 0^+$, the minimizers rescaled to unit mass converge along subsequences to functions supported at a single vertex.

papers.title: On the Kissing Number of Craig's Lattice and Spherical List Decoding
papers.abstract: Craig's lattices $A_{p-1}^k$ are a family of lattices with large kissing numbers, i.e., relative to their dimension $n = p-1$, they contain a large number of shortest nonzero vectors. Specifically, for small $k = o(\log p / \log \log p)$, a lower bound of Bacher (2015) shows that $A_{p-1}^k$ has a super-polynomial kissing number of $ω(n^k)$. Craig's lattices are therefore attractive candidates for the construction of spherical codes. In this work, we introduce a polynomial-time list decoder for spherical codes obtained from Craig's lattices for angular distance below $45^\circ$. Our second main result shows that Bacher's lower bound is asymptotically tight for $k = o(\log p / \log \log p)$. Finally, we introduce an efficient algorithm for computing the kissing number of $A_{p-1}^k$. Using this algorithm, we compute their kissing number in dimensions up to 521. Based on this data, we pose the open question whether the kissing number of $A_{p-1}^k$ with $k \approx \sqrt{p}$ grows like $e^{Θ(\sqrt{n})}$ in dimension $n=p-1$. Concurrent work by Laarhoven and Kominers as well as Bennett, Hhan, Li and Stephens-Davidowitz proves such a bound for very closely related lattices.

papers.title: Global phase-plane organization of a toxin-mediated plant-herbivore model
papers.abstract: Plant-herbivore interactions with chemical plant defence mechanisms can generate complex population dynamics through the nonlinear interplay between resource availability, herbivore pressure, and defence-induced feedbacks. In this work, we investigate the dynamical organization of a plant-herbivore model characterized by a non-monotone functional response accounting for inhibitory effects on grazing activity. In particular, we perform a qualitative and geometric analysis of the associated homogeneous system, characterizing the dynamical regimes supported by the model and the transitions between them. The results reveal the emergence of oscillatory behaviour through a Hopf bifurcation and the occurrence of stable periodic solutions. We further characterize the global phase-plane organization, providing a complete classification of equilibrium configurations and heteroclinic structures supported by the model. In addition, we identify the conditions under which homoclinic connections may occur and discuss their role in shaping the global dynamics. The analysis provides a unified description of the phase-plane organization and highlights how nonlinear defence feedbacks generate qualitatively distinct ecological outcomes, including extinction, stable coexistence, persistent oscillations, and global bifurcation scenarios organized by heteroclinic and homoclinic structures.

papers.title: Forward Self-similar Solutions of the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in Dimensions Five and Higher
papers.abstract: We construct forward self-similar solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 5$) for arbitrary $(-1)$-homogeneous, divergence-free initial data $u_0$ smooth on the unit sphere. For $n\ge 6$, the $O(|y|^{-3})$ bound on the nonlinear residual of the linear heat profile no longer yields $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$-integrability, obstructing a direct global energy perturbation around $e^Δu_0$. To overcome this difficulty, we truncate $u_0$ near the origin via a divergence-free cutoff and take the time-one slice of the resulting Navier--Stokes flow as the background profile, whose residual reduces to a parabolic scaling derivative evolving in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ from compactly supported data. Choosing a large cutoff radius yields a global $H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ remainder and a forward self-similar weak solution converging strongly to $u_0$ in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ as $t\downarrow 0$.

papers.title: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,β}$ hypersurfaces with $0<β\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

papers.title: Abelian varieties with homotheties
papers.abstract: In 1980, Bogomolov proved that the $\ell$-adic Galois image of an Abelian variety over a number field contains an open subgroup of the homotheties. In 1986, Serre refined that result, showing that the homotheties coming from the Galois side were uniformly bounded in $\ell$ inside the homotheties of the codomain of the representation. In a 2007 paper, Zarhin shows that Bogomolov's conclusion can fail in non-trivial cases for global function fields. We prove a suitable analogue of Serre's results over finitely generated fields of positive characteristic. As a consequence, we prove a new case of the 1978 conjecture by Geyer and Jarden.

papers.title: A 5/2 Guarantee for Echelon Stock (s,S) Policies in One-Warehouse Multi-Retailer Systems
papers.abstract: We study a periodic-review warehouse serving multiple heterogeneous retailers with stochastic demand and fixed costs and lead times at both echelons. We construct a deterministic echelon stock $(s,S)$ policy whose long-run expected average cost is at most $5/2$ times the optimum over all nonanticipative policies. The guarantee holds when the common backlog penalty and retailer holding rates are at least the warehouse holding rate and retailer setup costs are at most $3/2$ times the supplier's. The retailer-specific setup-cost condition extends beyond supplier setup-cost dominance: a retailer dispatch may cost up to 50 percent more than a supplier order. Demand vectors are i.i.d. over periods with finite positive means, and demands of different retailers may be correlated. Each retailer selects the full cycle of its single-location plan or a shifted cycle of half its width, and the warehouse serves requests in arrival order, allowing partial shipments. The upper bound on the policy's cost includes each retailer's mirror cost, which prices the warehouse imbalance created by its batching. The upper and lower bounds share a pooled supplier problem and add one problem per retailer, giving a factor independent of all lead times and the number of retailers. For arbitrary nonnegative setup costs and associated retailer demands, a consolidation policy holds allocated stock until a dispatch threshold is met and gives a factor below $4.9$. On 864 instances built from Walmart store sales, the simulated cost of an integer-rounded implementation of the FIFO policy averages 1.45 times the lower bound and reaches 1.75, and our analytical upper bound on its cost is below 1.94 times the lower bound. With no simulation search, the policy comes within 8.2 and 12.2 percent, on average over 216 instances, of an echelon batch policy and an integer-ratio policy, both tuned by simulation for each instance.
papers.comments: 70 pages, including a 33-page online appendix; 10 figures

papers.title: Anytime-valid inference for conditional hazard and survival functions with streaming data
papers.abstract: We consider the nonparametric estimation of the conditional hazard, cumulative hazard and survival functions of a time-to-event variable from streaming data subject to censoring, truncation, or a cure fraction. A time-to-event model is a map from the distribution of the latent variables to that of the observed ones. For a large class of models this map has an explicit inverse, and the conditional hazard is the ratio of the density of the exactly observed durations to an at-risk function. Both are estimated by one-pass learners, in which each observation contributes once and is never revised, such as recursive kernel, series and histogram estimators. Our main result is an asymptotic confidence band sequence for the conditional hazard at a fixed covariate value, uniform in time and in the sample size, which allows monitoring after a burn-in, and stopping at a data-dependent time. The band can shrink at the optimal uniform rate up to a logarithmic factor. Bands for the cumulative hazard and the survival function follow. In simulations, a fixed-sample band inspected repeatedly fails in about half of the streams, while the miscoverage of the recommended bands stays below, or close to, the nominal level.

papers.title: On representation-theoretic and homological properties of distance algebras of finite graphs
papers.abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology as bigraded Tor and Ext groups. We study the representation-theoretic and homological properties of the distance algebra $Σ_G$ of a finite connected graph $G$. We characterize the graphs for which $Σ_G$ is representation-finite, multiserial, biserial, or self-injective by an explicit graph-theoretic classification. We also compute the finitistic, self-injective, and dominant dimensions for several natural families of graphs. For a finite modular lattice $L$, we consider the distance algebra $Σ_L$ associated to the Hasse graph of $L$, and show that $Σ_L$ is Auslander--Gorenstein precisely when $L$ is a finite direct product of chains. We also present a family of minimal Auslander--Gorenstein distance algebras, namely, those associated to punctured hypercubes, whose finitistic (equivalently, self-injective; equivalently, dominant) dimension can be arbitrarily large.

papers.title: Equivariant Flow Matching on Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: Flow matching enables the training of networks that can flow samples from an initial to a target distribution. The network is regressed against simple vector fields that are conditioned on end points in the target distribution. In the Euclidean case, these conditional vector fields induce flows along straight lines. Various generalisations have been proposed to perform flow matching on spaces where straight lines are not well-defined, such as Riemannian manifolds and Lie groups. Riemannian flow matching applies to many domains, but typically requires expensive simulation, while flow matching on Lie groups is simulation-free but only works on Lie groups. In this work, we develop equivariant flow matching on homogeneous spaces, which generalises flow matching on Lie groups, while remaining simulation-free. We also derive all generators connecting pairs of position-orientations, generalising, and perform a similar derivation for event-velocity space, the Lorentzian analogue of position-orientation space, so that we can perform flow matching on these spaces.

papers.title: Stability for a multi-frequency inverse source problem in diffusion-based tomography
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse source problem for the time-harmonic diffusion equation arising in optical tomography. In inhomogeneous media, we establish a conditional logarithmic stability estimate by using multi-frequency boundary flux measurements. The proof combines a boundary observability inequality for the associated heat equation with quantitative analytic continuation. For constant coefficients, we further derive an increasing stability estimate with explicit dependence on the frequency bandwidth. In this case, the analysis employs complex polynomial interpolation of the Fourier-Laplace transform of the source. We also implement a multi-frequency Landweber iteration with a discrepancy-based stopping rule to reconstruct the sources. Numerical experiments show an overall improvement in reconstruction accuracy and resolution as the frequency bandwidth increases under the tested noise settings.

papers.title: A sharp minimum degree condition for Hamiltonicity in line graphs of 3-hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the line graph of a $3$-hypergraph, and let $n$ be its order. We prove that if $G$ is $3$-connected, $n\ge4936$, and $δ(G)\ge(n+5)/10$, then $G$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it does not belong to an explicitly described family of exceptional graphs. This extends the sharp minimum degree bound of Lai, Shao, and Zhan for $3$-connected claw-free graphs beyond the claw-free setting, since line graphs of $3$-hypergraphs may contain induced claws. The coefficient $1/10$ cannot be decreased, and the constant $5$ in the numerator cannot be replaced by $4$.

papers.title: Bivariate Renyi Tsallis Divergence
papers.abstract: In this paper, a bivariate extension of the differential Renyi Tsallis divergence is introduced for comparing two absolutely continuous bivariate probability distributions. Fundamental properties of the proposed divergence are studied, including non negativity, pseudo additivity under component wise independence, and invariance under monotone and nonsingular linear transformations. Relationships with Renyi, Tsallis, alpha, Bhattacharyya, and Hellinger divergence measures are also established. A sensitivity analysis is performed to compare the Renyi, Tsallis and Renyi Tsallis divergences under the Marshall Olkin and Gumbel type bivariate exponential models, taking the magnitude of Kendall's rank correlation coefficient as a common scale for dependence. The proposed measure is further developed for bivariate order statistics, with particular emphasis on the joint distribution of the minimum and maximum order statistics for several lifetime distributions, including exponential, Weibull, Pareto, and Rayleigh models. When the underlying distributions are unknown, a nonparametric estimator is constructed using bivariate Gaussian kernel density estimators with plug in bandwidth selection. The proposed estimator is applied to a real life dataset and bootstrap resampling is used to assess estimation uncertainty. The results show the applicability of the proposed divergence for comparing bivariate distributions and indicate that its finite sample performance depends on the order parameter and the distributions being compared.

papers.title: Distance algebras of finite distributive lattices are Gorenstein
papers.abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology of quasi-metric spaces as Tor- and Ext-groups respectively. Let $Σ_L$ be the distance algebra of the Hasse graph of a finite distributive lattice $L$, where the metric is given by the lengths of shortest paths in the graph. We show that $Σ_L$ is Gorenstein over any Gorenstein commutative noetherian ring $R$, and give bound of its self-injective dimension. The proof constructs, for each indecomposable (relative) injective module, a projective resolution that is in general non-minimal. When $R=\Bbbk$ is a field, we use algebraic Morse theory to reduce it to a minimal resolution, so that the Betti numbers can be obtained as the dimensions of homologies of certain order complexes. As a consequence, we show that the self-injective dimension of $Σ_L$ is the maximal Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of certain Stanley--Reisner rings. We also show that the first two terms of these minimal resolutions are multiplicity-free, whereas arbitrarily large multiplicities occur in every higher degree. In the appendix, we include a more abstract formulation of the non-minimal projective resolution, namely, a simplicial replacement of a diagram of projective modules.

papers.title: A Burns-Krantz theorem on convex domains
papers.abstract: We prove two boundary rigidity theorems for holomorphic self-maps of bounded convex domains. Let $Ω\subset\C^n$, $n\geq1$, and suppose that $\partialΩ$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $p\in\partialΩ$ for some $0<α\leq1$. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ satisfies $f(z)=z+o(|z-p|^3)$ as $z\to p$ in one fixed non-tangential approach region at $p$, then $f=\id_Ω$. We also prove a rigidity theorem for bounded convex domains $Ω$ without assuming boundary smoothness. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ of $Ω$ satisfies $f(z)-z=O(|z-p|^m)$ as $z\to p\in\partialΩ$ for some $m>1+2π/θ_p$, where $θ_p$ is the supremum of sector angles in the open tangent cone at $p$, taken over complex lines through its vertex, then $f=\id_Ω$, which proves a conjecture of Zimmer.

papers.title: Subharmonic functions and convexity of the Radon transform, with applications to the Fourier transform
papers.abstract: Integrating a subharmonic function over parallel hyperplanes produces a convex function of the signed distance from the origin, provided that the function is absolutely integrable on bounded slabs. We prove this first for twice continuously differentiable functions and then without any smoothness assumption, and the same argument applies to a function defined only on a slab. Examples on the disk explain why subharmonicity on a bounded convex domain does not imply convexity of the integrals over its chords. We then apply a one-dimensional Fourier representation for convex functions to the Radon transform, which leads to a directional formula for integrable subharmonic functions on slabs. For functions on bounded convex domains whose Radon transforms are convex, we obtain a weighted estimate for the integral of the Fourier transform in terms of boundary layers and the gradient.

papers.title: Remarks on uniqueness and nonuniqueness for the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem with $p<-n$
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness and nonuniqueness for the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem with $p<-n$. For $n\geq3$, we prove uniqueness for $p$ just below $-n$ without any symmetry assumptions. Moreover, for $n\geq8$, we obtain nonuniqueness for $p$ just above $-2n-3$, even under full simplex symmetry. The proofs use the Chou-Wang obstruction and Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

papers.title: Flip Combinatorial Invariance for flipclasses with small residues
papers.abstract: We establish (Normal) Flip Combinatorial Invariance for flipclasses with no residues longer than 8. Actually, we show more generally that all flipclasses of finite type with no residues longer than 8 have only one increasing path. For flipclasses of Weyl type, these are precisely the flipclasses having only one increasing path. This marks a refinement of the classical Combinatorial Invariance of Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.

papers.title: $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$
papers.abstract: We give explicit descriptions of the $m$-harmonic polynomials for dihedral groups via hypergeometric functions. Using these, we compute the parameters $m$ for which the Hilbert series of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ differs from the Hilbert series of $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $0$. We also give explicit descriptions of the generators of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ when this is the case.

papers.title: Asymptotic enumeration of histories and limit laws in two random graph evolution models
papers.abstract: We study growth models for random graphs where the growth is established by vertex or edge creations and where there is no dependence between vertices and edges. Creations are logged by time stamps such that the history of the resulting graph can be reconstructed. We investigate two prototypical models, an undirected and a directed one, called undirected independent growth model (UIG-model) and directed independent growth model (DIG-model). The generating functions for the number of histories have radius of convergence equal to zero. In the UIG-model, we express the asymptotic number of histories as a sum that is amenable to the discrete Laplace method. We derive the asymptotic number of histories, study the number of vertices of a random history, and prove a central limit theorem. In the DIG-model we use a rescaled Borel transform to get an entire function. Then we show that this function is Hayman admissible, which enables us to derive the asymptotic number of histories in this model. The counting sequence is closely related to the framework of generalized Legendre-Stirling numbers. To determine the number of vertices in a random history, we prove that the bivariate generating function is e-admissible and infer that again a normal limit law holds. Finally, we discuss a correspondence to set partitions with even block sizes and present an algorithm based on Boltzmann samplers that generates such graphs uniformly at random.

papers.title: Helicity conservation for compressible barotropic Euler flows: regularity criteria and a momentum-based approach
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study helicity conservation for weak solutions to the compressible barotropic Euler equations. Using generalized Constantin-E-Titi-type commutator estimates that fully exploit the kinetic energy, we derive new sufficient conditions for helicity conservation across a broader range of regularity exponents. These conditions reveal the interplay between temporal, spatial integrability and differentiability of the velocity and density, as well as the influence of velocity-density coupling on helicity conservation. A key feature of our approach is that helicity conservation is established directly from the momentum equation, without invoking the vorticity equation.

papers.title: Scaling-invariant smallness and global strong solutions to the three-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with a non-vacuum far-field density
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with a positive far-field density $ρ_\infty$. We identify the following scaling-invariant quantity associated with the initial data: \begin{align*} ρ_\infty^{\frac{3-γ}{2}} \left( \|\nabla u_0\|_{L^2}^2 +P(ρ_\infty) \Big( \frac12\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}ρ_0|u_0|^2\,dx +\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}G(ρ_0)\,dx \Big) \right), \end{align*} where $G$ denotes the relative potential energy density with respect to $ρ_\infty$. Provided that the scaling-invariant quantity is sufficiently small, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, allowing the initial density to contain interior vacuum and exhibit large oscillations. The smallness criterion depends explicitly on the far-field density through the prefactor $ρ_\infty^{(3-γ)/2}$ and the background pressure $P(ρ_\infty)$. Our result provides a non-vacuum counterpart to Wen's scaling-invariant global existence result for the far-field vacuum case (\textit{Adv. Math.} \textbf{482} (2025), Paper No. 110628).

papers.title: On (Pathwidth, Clique)-boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove that every $(\pw,ω)$-bounded class of graphs has bounded tree-independence number, answering a question of Bešter Štorgel, Dallard, Lozin, Milanič, and Zamaraev. We deduce this from a bound on the tree-independence number of graphs with neither $\B_ρ$ nor $K_{σ,σ}$ as an induced minor, where $\B_ρ$ is the complete binary tree of height $ρ$ and the bound depends only on $ρ$ and $σ$. We then obtain an asymptotically sharp bound on the path-independence number of $n$-vertex graphs in any $(\pw,ω)$-bounded class. The lower-bound examples also give counterexamples to a conjecture of Hickingbotham and Joret. We further prove that, for every forest $F$ and every $\ell\in\N$, there is a constant $k=k(F,\ell)\in\N$ such that every graph $G$ with no induced theta or $\ell$-long prism and no induced subgraph isomorphic to $F$ satisfies tree-independence number at most $k$. This proves a strengthened form of a conjecture of Chudnovsky, Hajebi, and Trotignon. Finally, for every integer $s\ge2$, we characterize the forests $F$ for which excluding $F$ as an induced minor and $K_{s,s}$ as an induced subgraph bounds tree-independence number. This extends the characterization of Bonnet, Duhamel, and Hickingbotham, who considered bounded pathwidth with $K_{s,s}$ excluded as a subgraph.

papers.title: Higher orbifold Euler characteristics of torus representations
papers.abstract: We compute the $Γ$-Euler characteristic of a finite-dimensional representation of the compact torus $\mathbb{T}^k$ where $Γ$ is an arbitrary finitely presented group. We additionally compute the $Γ$-Euler characteristic of the unit sphere in such a representation as well as the corresponding symplectic quotient at a nonzero level of the moment map. In each case, the $Γ$-Euler characteristic is expressed in terms of the weight matrix for the representation as well as a description of the abelianization of $Γ$.

papers.title: Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Constrained Combinatorial Optimization with U(1)-Symmetric Tensor Trains
papers.abstract: Tensor Train (TT) decomposition has emerged as a powerful tool for mitigating the curse of dimensionality in a variety of machine learning and combinatorial optimization tasks. Recent advances show that TT-based generative models can efficiently represent and explore high-dimensional discrete spaces, even when the cost function structure is unknown. However, incorporating hard linear constraints into TT-based optimization remains challenging, as existing interpolation and sampling approaches often fail when feasible points are rare. In this work, we develop a general TT-based framework for constrained combinatorial optimization built upon U(1)-symmetric tensor networks. Our method introduces an expressibility-enhancement mechanism for constructing sparse symmetric tensors and a graph-based diversity measure that guides sample selection during training. On assignment benchmarks, expressibility enhancement and diversity-aware selection improve mean solution quality over their respective baselines. The assignment-selected diversifying strategy also extends to nonpolynomial Set Partitioning, with larger relative gains observed in the higher-tensor-rank data families. Separate runtime benchmarks show substantial speedups over ConstrainTNet and PROTES on non-degenerate assignment workloads; comparisons with simulated annealing depend on constraint information and computational budget, but, overall, support the practicality of the current implementation.
papers.comments: 39 pages, including supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/antientropic-guy/OhMyU1_public. Extends an earlier version presented at the non-archival CoLoRAI workshop at ICML 2026

papers.title: Global existence and semi-classical limit for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global existence and the semi-classical limit of the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation. We first establish the existence and uniqueness of a global weak solution for initial data with finite mass and second velocity moment satisfying the Pauli bound. When the initial datum also has finite spatial second moment and finite free energy, we prove that the solution satisfies the Fermi--Dirac free energy inequality. Next, as the quantum parameter $\hbar$ goes to zero, we prove that the solution of the Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation converges strongly to the classical Fokker--Planck solution in $\mathcal C([0,T];L^1_j(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d))$ for all $j\in[0,2)$. We also obtain a quantitative convergence rate in $\hbar$ when both equations share the same bounded initial datum.

papers.title: Maximal defect $2$-blocks with dihedral defect groups up to splendid Morita equivalence
papers.abstract: We classify, up to splendid Morita equivalence, all maximal defect blocks whose defect groups are dihedral \(2\)-groups of order at least \(8\). The classification holds for blocks over an algebraically closed field as well as for those over a suitable discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero. As a consequence, Puig's conjecture holds for this infinite family of blocks. Beyond the classification result itself, a central feature of the present work is the variety of methods required in its proof. Our arguments combine classical techniques of block theory with a broad range of tools and techniques that have emerged over the past twenty-five years. Amongst others these include in a crucial manner the Gorenstein-Walter classification of finite groups with dihedral Sylow \(2\)-subgroups, Linckelmann's glueing of local Morita equivalences to obtain a stable equivalence of Morita type, the modern versions of Fong's 1st and 2nd reduction theorems in terms of splendid and endo-permutation source Morita equivalences, the structure of the Dade group of endo-permutation modules, Boltje-Perepelitsky's extended theory of Brauer pairs for \(p\)-permutation modules, the fusion systems of the blocks involved, or the concrete knowledge of their decomposition matrices.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for the Hénon parabolic equation
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonnegative classical entire solution of $u_t-Δu=|x|^αu^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero when $n\ge3$, $α\ge0$, and $1 < p < \frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$. The same conclusion holds for weighted parabolic Gross--Pitaevskii systems with nonlinearities of degree $p=2r+1$ and constant coupling coefficients $β_{ij}=β_{ji}\ge0$ and $β_{ii}>0$. Both results include the unweighted case and require no boundedness, radial symmetry, spatial decay, finite-energy, or growth assumptions. The range is optimal for both problems: bounded nonzero nonnegative stationary solutions exist for $p\ge\frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$.

papers.title: Critical heavy traffic and diffusion limits for shortest-of-d dynamic routing
papers.abstract: We study shortest-of-$d$ routing, with fixed $d\ge2$, in $N$ parallel queues with independent finite-state Markov service environments switching at rate $κ_N$. At the critical load $ρ_N=1-1/N$, the empirical measure of the centered queue lengths, under stationarity, converges in distribution to a random probability measure determined by its mean. We identify the mean's density and the conditional independence of fixed finite collections of centered queues in the limit. On time scales of order $N$, the centered empirical mean converges to a diffusion with explicit drift and constant diffusion coefficient. These limits hold when $κ_N/N\to\infty$, along subsequences with convergent lattice phase. The diffusion limit extends to centered initial empirical measures tight in the first Wasserstein topology, with means converging in law. A short initial layer prepares the limiting family while preserving the limiting mean. Empirical approximation holds in time-integrated Wasserstein distance.

papers.title: Maximin Dispersion over Simple Polyhedral Domains: Strong NP-Completeness and Exact Algorithms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the decision version of weighted maximin dispersion over the unit $\ell_1$-ball with rational sites and positive rational weights is strongly NP-complete. The same holds for unweighted dispersion over full-dimensional integer simplices when the sites are exactly their vertices. Both reductions from Exact Cover by 3-Sets rely on a shared quadratic rigidity argument. We also give exact algorithms that run in polynomial time for every fixed dimension. For the simplex problem, a Voronoi decomposition yields rational optimal solutions. For the weighted $\ell_1$-ball problem, an orthant decomposition and a single-paraboloid lifting yield optimal solutions whose coordinates lie in a common real algebraic extension of degree at most two. In both cases, these solutions have polynomial encoding length and provide certificates for NP membership.

papers.title: Locking-free numerical methods for poroelasticity optimal control problems with minimal regularities
papers.abstract: We study distributed optimal control of a linear poroelastic system in a total pressure formulation, with displacement and fluid-pressure tracking and box constraints on the source control. A mechanical Schur complement gives well-posedness at zero storage for each fixed finite Lamé parameter, without estimates that grow like the inverse storage coefficient. We discretize the state and adjoint with conforming finite elements and dG(0) time stepping, and use piecewise constant controls. Under the stated regularity assumptions and a positive lower bound on storage, we prove first-order control and state error estimates uniform as the Lamé parameter increases. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates, examine the dependence on the Lamé and storage coefficients, and demonstrate localized pressure control with active bounds.

papers.title: Constructions of reversible linear and DNA codes through $T_{D,g}^n-$set and $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$right polycyclic codes
papers.abstract: In this paper we give a construction technique of $T_{D,g}^n-$set for reversible linear codes and reversible DNA codes with their code parameters. This technique yields many reversible MDS codes which significantly improves the $T^n-$set construction by Oztas et.al. in terms of obtained code parameters. Concatenation-based constructions are presented for reversible linear codes satisfying self-duality and linear complementary dual (LCD) conditions, giving necessary and sufficient condition for desired dual properties. We introduce a new notion of $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes. Also, a new construction technique is developed to obtain reversible linear $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes with good parameters (MDS codes) over any finite commutative rings.

papers.title: Perturbation results for the Choquard equation in the sublinear case
papers.abstract: We study perturbations of the positive ground state of the Choquard equation $$ -Δu+u=(I_α*|u|^p)|u|^{p-2}u\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N $$ by means of a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. For $p\ge2$ the energy is $C^2$ on $H^1$ and a standard machinery applies. The case $α=2$, $1+2/N<p<2$ is different: the ground state has an algebraic decay and the energy is not twice differentiable on $H^1$. We introduce a weighted space adapted to the tail and we perform a finite-dimensional reduction on it. The outcome is a positive solution of a localized perturbation problem near every critical point of the first-order interaction functional with nonzero local degree. For the singularly perturbed problem with potential $V$ we obtain, under a small relative oscillation assumption, solutions concentrating near every critical point of $V$ with nonzero local degree, and a Lusternik--Schnirelman lower bound near compact sets of local minima. We also consider the variant in which $V$ multiplies both the linear and nonlocal terms, and we construct solutions that concentrate near isolated critical points of nonzero degree.

papers.title: Solution-Set Properties of Absolute Value Equations: Inverse Nonnegativity, Boundedness, and Connectedness
papers.abstract: The solution-set properties of the absolute value equation (AVE) \(Ax+|x|=b\) were systematically investigated by Hladík (\emph{SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl.} \textbf{44}, 175-195, 2023), who also formulated several related open questions. This paper settles and extends some of those questions. A complete converse characterization of inverse nonnegativity is established without restrictions on the matrix order or symmetry. The characterization is accompanied by equivalent criteria involving nonsingular \(M\)-matrices and spectral radii. A diagonal semidefinite certificate is then developed for the uniform boundedness of solution sets. Unlike regularity conditions, this certificate permits infinitely many solutions, as illustrated by a three-dimensional example whose solution set contains a nontrivial line segment. Connectedness of the solution set for an individual right-hand side is characterized through a finite graph formed from its orthant components. A further sufficient condition is obtained from the \(P_0\)-property of the associated complementarity matrix. The inverse-nonnegativity characterization is finally extended to generalized absolute value equations (GAVE) having a nonnegative absolute-value coefficient matrix.

papers.title: Dependence properties between marginals of discrete-time maximum processes
papers.abstract: Consider a discrete time sequence $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ and the corresponding process $(M_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ which, at any time $n\in\mathbb{N}$, takes the maximum value reached by the process $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ up to that time. Clearly, there exists a dependence between the values assumed by the process $(M_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ at two distinct points in time. This paper formally describes such a dependence in terms of the copula of the two random values. Various scenarios with respect to the sequence $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ are considered, e.g., without assuming independence in its components and/or identical distribution. Such explicit expressions of the copula are then used to provide results that describe how the dependence between the maxima reached by the sequence $(X_n,n\in\mathbb{N})$ in different times varies when both the time interval between them and/or their positions in the sequence are increased. In this context, asymptotic results are also provided.

papers.title: Kähler metrics with varying cone angles and Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that the cone angle of a Kähler metric is constant if its Ricci curvature is locally in $L^2$. In particular, a Kähler--Einstein metric cannot have a varying cone angle. The proof is elementary and assumes only uniform comparison with the corresponding model.

papers.title: A Divergence-Free Finite Element Discretization of a Convection-Cooling Optimal Control Problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a finite element discretization for a bilinear optimal control problem governed by a stationary convection-diffusion equation, in which an incompressible velocity field acts as the control through the convective term. Continuous piecewise linear finite elements are employed to approximate the state and adjoint variables, while the Stokes-type optimality equation for the velocity control is discretized by a low-order, pointwise divergence-free ($P_1^c\oplus RT_0-P_0$) finite element. To accommodate the nonconforming velocity space, we construct a discrete cost functional by replacing the continuous $H^1$-seminorm regularization with a suitable discrete velocity bilinear form and derive the corresponding discrete first-order optimality system. Since the bilinear coupling between the velocity control and the state variable renders the underlying optimization problem nonconvex, we establish local strong convexity of the discrete reduced cost functional under a second-order sufficient optimality condition at an isolated strict local minimizer of the continuous problem. Furthermore, by exploiting a divergence-preserving interpolation operator, auxiliary state and adjoint error estimates, and a stability relation between the discrete reduced-gradient residual and the control error, we derive a priori error estimates for the state, adjoint state and velocity control. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the optimized incompressible velocity in redistributing the temperature field and to verify the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: Hardness and Inapproximability of the Covering Radius for LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: Given a binary parity-check matrix $H$ and an integer $r$, the covering-radius decision problem asks whether every attainable syndrome can be represented by an error vector of Hamming weight at most $r$. We study this problem for sparse parity-check matrices with bounded row and column weights. Using a bounded-occurrence quantified-SAT reduction, we prove that the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-complete for matrices with maximum row and column weight three, and remains $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-hard under a constant multiplicative gap. Starting from Vertex Cover on 3-regular graphs, we also obtain an explicit NP-hard approximation factor under the same weight constraints. We remark that weight three is the exact threshold for hardness: if either the maximum row weight or the maximum column weight is at most two, the covering radius can be computed in polynomial time.

papers.title: The Cooperstein conjecture and additive alternating $d$-codes
papers.abstract: Let $\bigwedge^2 V$ be the second exterior power of a vector space $V$ over a finite field. The Cooperstein conjecture asserts a dimension bound for flats external to varieties consisting of points of bounded rank in $\mathrm{PG}(\bigwedge^2 V)$. This geometric problem can be translated into a question about linear spaces of alternating matrices whose nonzero elements have rank at least a prescribed value. For matrices of odd order, the sharp cardinality bound was already established by Delsarte and Goethals (1975). In this paper, we prove the Cooperstein conjecture for matrices of even order and, more generally, we prove its additive analogue by determining, for all admissible parameters, the maximum size of an additive subgroup of alternating matrices in which every nonzero matrix has at least the prescribed rank. Our proof uses Pfaffian equations to characterize alternating matrices of rank below the prescribed minimum. We study the minimal graded free resolutions of the corresponding Pfaffian rings. The Cohen--Macaulay property and the $a$-invariant of each Pfaffian ring determine the largest shift in its resolution. We use trace functions on evaluation quotients to construct polynomial indicators for the matrices of small rank in an additive subgroup. The largest shift controls their degrees, yielding the upper bound by a counting argument. Finally, we give explicit trace constructions attaining the bound.

papers.title: Nonlinear syzygies in ordinary powers of chordal cover ideals
papers.abstract: We construct connected chordal graphs whose cover ideals have ordinary powers that are not componentwise linear over any field, disproving the Herzog--Hibi--Ohsugi conjecture.

papers.title: Almost-Global Coordinates on Matrix Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study global coordinates on smooth manifolds outside some closed subsets of measure zero. We first give an elementary proof that every compact smooth manifold admits such coordinates, allowing the Euclidean parameter domain to be disconnected. We then study parametrizations of classical matrix groups, Stiefel manifolds, Grassmannians and real flag manifolds. For these parametrizations, we describe the inverse maps and compute the codimensions of the omitted subsets. We construct these parametrizations using Cayley transforms, graphs of linear maps and block Gaussian elimination. We also give formulas for Riemannian gradients and Haar integrals in these coordinates.

papers.title: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
papers.abstract: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$. Fixing the order of all differences splits the real problem into finitely many polyhedral chambers. A branch-and-bound over these chambers, with an exact rational certificate at every leaf, proves $G_R(n) = G_Z(n)$ for $n \le 10$. Each proof takes under a minute and is verified by an independent checker that uses only exact arithmetic. An exhaustive exact enumeration of all chamber vertices confirms the result for $n \le 7$, and shows that there the shortest real rulers are exactly the optimal integer rulers and their mirror images. For every $n$ we show $n(\sqrt{n}-1)^2 \le G_R(n) \le G_Z(n)$, so that $G_R(n) \sim G_Z(n) \sim n^2$. Non-integral chamber vertices first appear at $n = 7$: there are 84, all half-integral. Already there, 80 of them are shortest points of their chambers, 40 of them the only one, although the global optimum is integral; a twelve-mark example of the same kind comes from Singer's construction. On the other hand, every Singer ruler with at most 104 marks, cut at the largest gap, is the only shortest point of its own chamber; we conjecture this for all prime powers.
papers.comments: 9 pages, 5 tables. Programs, proof files and exact checkers: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23843508

papers.title: Improved contraction estimates for linear elliptic diffusion-advection-reaction equations
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes contraction estimates for the unique strong solution to a linear elliptic diffusion-advection-reaction equation in a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \geq 3$, where the zero-order coefficient lies in $L^{\frac{d}{2}}$ and the drift coefficient belongs to $L^p$ with $p \in (d, \infty)$. Compared with existing results, we obtain contraction estimates with improved constants in a quantitative sense. In particular, for the $L^\infty$-contraction estimate, the constant is shown to have the explicit form $\frac{1}α$, depending only on the constant $α> 0$ in the zero-order term. The key step is to represent the solution as the image of a weighted resolvent associated with a Dirichlet form.

papers.title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
papers.abstract: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calderón--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

papers.title: Exact and Approximate Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Multivariate Diffusions under High-Frequency Sampling
papers.abstract: We establish the asymptotic theory of the exact maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for discretely observed multivariate ergodic diffusions under high-frequency, long-span sampling, solving an open problem posed by \citet{YCW2019} and \citet{Li2013}. The drift may grow linearly, and the volatility is bounded away from zero and either bounded or proportional to $1+|x|$. When the sampling interval decays polynomially, the exact MLE is consistent, asymptotically normal and efficient, with rates $\sqrt{nΔ_n}$ for drift and $\sqrt n$ for diffusion parameters. Under an additional condition on ergodic averages, and when the time span $nΔ_n$ also grows polynomially, its moments converge as well. The proof never analyzes the exact likelihood directly: it shows that a closed-form density expansion of sufficiently high order is uniformly accurate in relative terms at every observed transition, so that the two log-likelihoods differ by $o_P(1)$ uniformly in the parameter. The same argument yields accuracy conditions under which an approximate likelihood is asymptotically equivalent to the exact one; in particular, the approximate MLE of Yang, Chen and Wan converges to the true parameter. For the delta-expansion estimator of fixed order $K\ge1$, we derive the leading bias explicitly. It shows that $nΔ_n^{K+1}\to0$ cannot be weakened when the bias constant is nonzero, and that the bias falls on the drift parameters for even $K$ and on the diffusion parameters for odd $K$. Monte Carlo experiments confirm the predicted biases.

papers.title: For any wavenumber, the Helmholtz FEM matrix is invertible for almost all meshes
papers.abstract: We study invertibility of the conforming piecewise-linear Galerkin matrix for Helmholtz problems with a Dirichlet obstacle and the radiation condition approximated by \emph{either} impedance boundary condition \emph{or} a complex absorbing potential. We prove that for almost every simplicial mesh, and every fixed wavenumber, the Helmholtz FEM matrix with piecewise-linear elements is invertible.

papers.title: A Quasiconformal Squeezing function and Fridman invariant and applications
papers.abstract: The squeezing function and Fridman invariant are two examples of biholomorphic invariants that have proved to be useful in exploring questions in complex geometry. Motivated by their construction, we define conformal analogues of these invariants by using suitable families of $K$-quasiconformal mappings, and study several basic properties such as continuity, domain dependence and boundary behaviour near spherically extreme points. It is also shown that these conformal invariants are explicitly related. As an application, we propose and prove variants of the Ferrand--Obata theorem in conformal geometry that apply to domains in $\mbb R^n$. This highlights the close analogy that exists between the Ferrand--Obata and Wong--Rosay theorems.

papers.title: Convection--diffusion equations with non-integrable initial data
papers.abstract: We characterize the long-time behaviour of solutions to the convection--diffusion equation $u_t-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, with initial data behaving like a non-integrable power at infinity, $|x|^γu_0(x)\to k_\pm$ as $x\to\pm\infty$, $0<γ\le1$. The decay rate in time and the asymptotic profile depend on the strength of convection as compared to the size of the solution at infinity, leading either to a convective behaviour or to a diffusive one. When the nonlinear convection dominates, we observe an enhanced dissipation effect: the decay rate in time is faster than for the purely diffusive equation with the same initial datum. For $0<γ<1$ we obtain the limit self-similar profile, which, in the convective regime, has one shock, or two when $k_+k_-<0$ and $|k_+|>\eps(γ,q)|k_-|$, where $\eps(γ,q)\in(0,1)$ is an explicit threshold. For $γ=1$ logarithmic corrections appear, and the limit is a multiple of the heat kernel if $q>2$ and an $N$-wave if $1<q\le2$. The convergence takes place in the spaces to which the datum belongs, and not only on expanding sets. The main new ingredients are an Oleĭnik type estimate of Hölder type valid for $q\geq 2$ and a far-field estimate, uniform in time, showing that beyond the self-similar region the solution is still described by its own datum.

papers.title: Potential theory for double phase equations with measure data
papers.abstract: We develop a potential theory for elliptic equations with double phase growth and signed measure data. We establish existence of solutions obtained by approximation, pointwise bounds for the flux in terms of linear Riesz potentials, and nonlinear potential estimates for the solution in terms of generalized Wolff potentials; a quantitative decay estimate for the flux excess is the main ingredient and also yields a potential criterion for gradient continuity. The results cover both singular and degenerate equations, including the range $p>n$.

papers.title: The minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for some k
papers.abstract: A graph on at least 2k+2 vertices is k-extendable if every matching of size k extends to a perfect matching, and it is minimally k-extendable if it is k-extendable but deleting any edge is not. Plummer proved that every k-extendable graph is (k+1)-connected. So its minimum degree is at least k+1. Lou and Yu conjectured that a minimally k-extendable graph on at most 4k vertices has minimum degree in {k+1,2k,2k+1}; the case k=1 and the claw-free case of k=2 have been settled previously. We determine the minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for k=2 and k=3, thereby settling the Lou--Yu conjecture for these two values. For k=2 the minimum degree is in {3,4,5}. For k=3 it is in {4,7} at orders 8 and 10, and in {4,6,7} at order 12. The proofs pass to the complement graph and combine Tutte's perfect matching theorem with a classification of four-vertex and six-vertex obstructions. All predicted values are realized by explicit constructions.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to Graphs and Combinatorics

papers.title: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
papers.abstract: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

papers.title: Hausdorff reflections and obstruction ideals for filter topologies on MV-algebras
papers.abstract: MV-algebras arise in many-valued logic and are closely related to lattice-ordered groups. We characterize Hausdorff separation in filter topologies through their associated ideals. For every proper lattice filter, $T_0$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ are equivalent, and the zero-neighborhood ideal determines a canonical Hausdorff reflection. For a radius filter satisfying a refinement condition, the filter topology agrees with the ambient subspace topology exactly when every radius is a weak order unit. This answers a question of Luan, Zhao and Yang without requiring divisibility of the representing group. These results reveal two successive algebraic obstructions: a polar obstruction controlling compatibility with the ambient topology, followed by a relative infinitesimal obstruction controlling the residual failure of Hausdorff separation. For a unital lattice-ordered subring of $C(X,\mathbb R)$, where $X$ is compact Hausdorff and the unit is $\mathbf1$, the associated exact sequence admits a positive additive section exactly when the relative infinitesimal ideal vanishes.

papers.title: Observability and Domain Shape Design for a Class of Degenerate Schrödinger Equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates boundary observability for a class of two dimensional degenerate Schrodinger equations on the unit square. The diffusion matrix has diagonal entries x1 to the power alpha1 and x2 to the power alpha2, where both parameters lie between zero and one. Since the underlying degenerate elliptic operator lacks global H2 regularity, classical Rellich space time multiplier and hidden regularity arguments cannot be applied directly to weak solutions. We introduce a truncation parameter delta and construct uniformly elliptic problems on nondegenerate subdomains. Weighted Poincare inequalities, Sturm Liouville nodal properties, spectral decomposition, and Hilbert tensor product techniques yield an operator resolvent approximation and strong convergence of the state solutions and their boundary normal derivatives in suitable energy and trace spaces. Passing to the limit in the parameterized multiplier identities gives a boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate system on the nondegenerate active boundaries. When alpha1 is less than or equal to alpha2, the minimal observation time is 4 times the square root of 2 divided by the product of 1 minus alpha1 and 2 minus alpha2. This time tends to infinity as alpha1 tends to one, whereas it tends to 2 times the square root of 2 in the nondegenerate limit.

papers.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
papers.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
papers.abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminusΩ$. For any $α\in(0,1]$ and $x\inΩ$, let \begin{align*} d_{α,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\geα\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $α\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(Ω)$, \begin{align*} \int_Ω\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le Cα^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $α^{-p'}$ as $α\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

papers.title: Transmission Expansion and Energy Storage Planning under Great Britain's Uncertain Energy Transition Pathways
papers.abstract: Long term power system planning must account for uncertainty in electricity demand and generation, while recognising the different investment and commissioning characteristics of transmission and energy storage. This paper develops a multi year stochastic framework for coordinated transmission expansion and energy storage planning and applies it to the Great Britain electricity system to assess investment needs through to 2050. The framework integrates multiple energy transition pathways with an enhanced representation of the GB transmission network and captures the different characteristics of transmission and storage investment over time. The coordinated treatment of transmission and storage is considered as a system level benchmark rather than a centralised investment mechanism. In GB, transmission investment is subject to regulated forward looking planning, while storage is largely developed by market participants in response to market signals. The framework therefore quantifies the potential value of improved coordination and identifies where existing investment signals may not encourage complementary storage deployment. Results across alternative transmission only, storage only and coordinated investment strategies show substantial benefits from joint planning. Compared with transmission only planning, coordinated investment reduces additional transmission capacity by 2%, cumulative expected load shedding by 97%, and total expected system cost by 36%, primarily through avoided unserved energy. Transmission preparation periods affect the timing, but not the final portfolio, of investments. Finally, the energy transition pathway materially influences investment requirements, with Electrification and Efficiency requiring 7% more transmission capacity and 45% more storage energy capacity than Falling Behind.

papers.title: Positivity of Signed Odd-Multiplicity Partitions
papers.abstract: We establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for the signed partition $q$-series \[ A_k(q)= \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k} \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{q^{j_i}}{1+q^{2j_i}} =\sum_{n\ge0}a_k(n)q^n, \qquad k\ge0, \] with $A_0(q)=1$. The coefficient $a_k(n)$ counts, with signs, partitions of $n$ having exactly $k$ distinct part sizes, each occurring with odd multiplicity. A partition with multiplicities $2t_1+1,\ldots,2t_k+1$ is assigned the sign $(-1)^{t_1+\cdots+t_k}$. We prove that $a_k(n)\ge0$ for all $k,n\ge0$, thereby resolving a conjecture on signed odd-multiplicity partitions. Our proof combines a positive theta--MacMahon factorization for the generating functions restricted to odd part sizes with a dyadic product decomposition that extends positivity to arbitrary part sizes. Moreover, we establish strict positivity $a_k(n)>0$ for every $k\ge2$ and $n\ge\binom{k+1}{2}$.

papers.title: Covariate-Indexed Inclusion Probabilities on Unbalanced Panels
papers.abstract: We estimate the probability that an item with given covariates belongs to a set when the cross-section changes over time and items and periods are dependent. We propose two convex models whose fitted probabilities are nonnegative by construction and remain valid whatever the dependence between items, for which we establish consistency, finite-sample bounds and limit distributions for serially dependent panels. One suits events of moderate or high probability, the other rare events, and half the disagreement between their fits estimates a lower bound on the misspecification error of the worse fit, without knowledge of the true probabilities. On monthly US stock failures, the rare-event model predicts better than the ordinary logit and the classical failure logit. With the eight classical predictors, most of the gain comes from basis functions of the rank angle of each predictor and summary.

papers.title: Semisimplicity of Brauer algebras associated with finite Coxeter types
papers.abstract: A finite-dimensional complex algebra is semisimple if its Jacobson radical is zero. In this paper, we determine the complex parameters for which Brauer algebras associated with finite Coxeter types are semisimple. We also determine semisimplicity at zero for the specified polynomial diagram forms and show that it can depend on the choice of polynomial form.

papers.title: Shape design for degenerate elliptic Equation with degenerate boundary and its application to quantitativeweak unique continuation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the unique continuation property (UCP) for a class of degenerate elliptic equations of the form $-\text{div}(A\nabla u) = λu$ in a bounded domain $Ω\s \mathbb{R}^N$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions. While unique continuation is well-established for uniformly elliptic operators via Carleman estimates or frequency-function methods, spatial degeneracy introduces substantial analytical obstacles in higher dimensions, particularly due to the lack of sufficient regularity for weak solutions and the breakdown of classical boundary integration-by-parts identities. To overcome these challenges, we develop an alternative framework based on the shape design (shape optimization) method under suitable structural assumptions. We highlight the fundamental distinction between qualitative and quantitative unique continuation in the degenerate setting. While qualitative UCP can sometimes be adapted from classical arguments, quantitative UCP requires explicit estimates that control the behavior of the solution throughout the domain by its behavior on a sub-domain. By integrating the shape design approach with a compatible weighted Hardy inequality, we establish new quantitative estimates and unique continuation results for higher-dimensional degenerate elliptic operators, bypassing the stringent regularity requirements of traditional methods.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I γ_{Σ_i}(K_i)^{\tilde λ_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}γ_Γ\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,Σ_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $γ_{Σ_i}$ is zero, where $λ_i, \tilde λ_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde λ_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $Γ, Σ_1,\cdots,Σ_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I λ_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

papers.title: Maximum number of cells in a matroid subdivision of hypersimplex
papers.abstract: David Speyer proved that the maximum number of cells in a regular matroid subdivision of the hypersimplex $Δ(m,t)$ is $\binom{t-2}{m-1}$ , using the language of tropical geometry and properties of the Tutte polynomial of a matroid \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Speyer}. In this paper, we prove this result in general, i.e. for arbitrary matroid subdivisions including the non-regular ones. We perform a different combinatorial way using our results in \cite{HHH} and independent of tropical language.

papers.title: Sharp lower bounds for weighted bisections of graphs with bounded maximum degree
papers.abstract: A bisection of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two parts the sizes of which differ by at most one. We prove that every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most an odd positive integer $k$, with arbitrary nonnegative real edge weights, has a bisection of weight at least $(k+1)/(2k)$ times its total edge weight. The corresponding bound $(k+2)/(2(k+1))$ for even $k$ follows immediately. Both coefficients are best possible. Somewhat surprisingly, these are exactly the sharp coefficients known for maximum weighted cuts, despite the additional balance requirement.

papers.title: The Koebe radius for univalent cubics
papers.abstract: Let \(p(z)=z+a_2z^2+a_3z^3\) be a polynomial univalent in the unit disk \(Δ\). We determine the largest disk centered at the origin that is contained in the image \(p(Δ)\) of every such polynomial. Its squared radius is the unique real root of \[ 27q^3-54q^2+63q-8=0. \] We also find the extremal polynomial \(p_*\).

papers.title: Edge behavior of the KPZ fixed point under upper-tail conditioning
papers.abstract: We consider the KPZ fixed point $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(x,t)$ with the narrow-wedge initial profile, conditioned on $\{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(0,1)\ge L\}$ as $L\to\infty$. Our main result describes its fluctuations near the boundary of the region affected by the conditioning. More precisely, in the spatial window $x=t\sqrt L+O(1)$, the centered field converges in finite-dimensional distributions to the KPZ fixed point with a half-Brownian initial profile. The convergence holds jointly at arbitrary positive times, including times before and after the conditioning time. The proof is based on an asymptotic correspondence between conditional narrow-wedge multipoint formulas and those for the half-Brownian KPZ fixed point.

papers.title: Fine spectral analysis of concentrating solutions to Brezis--Nirenberg problem in dimension $4$
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the qualitative properties and Morse indices of concentrating solutions to the Brezis--Nirenberg problem \[ -Δu=u^3+εu, \quad u>0, \quad\text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partialΩ, \] where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^4$ is a smooth bounded domain, $ε>0$ is small parameter. For a family of $m$-bubble solutions with distinct interior concentration points and comparable concentration scales, we establish precise asymptotic expansions for the first $6m$ eigenvalues of the associated linearized eigenvalue problem and determine the corresponding eigenfunction profiles.

papers.title: Heap-type permutation generation with a prescribed final arrangement
papers.abstract: Heap's algorithm generates all permutations of an array of n items, obtaining each one from its predecessor by a single swap. We determine the net permutation applied to the array by every complete recursive call: a transposition when the number of items is odd and at least three, and a cycle through all items when it is even. We show that the output of each call is a concatenation of right cosets of the symmetric group on one item fewer, and we prove a general formula: the order in which the items are parked at the last position may be chosen freely, every such order corresponds to exactly one valid schedule, and it determines the net permutation of the call. Two variants follow. In the cyclic variant a complete sweep over an even number of items rotates the array by one position. In the extremal variant, for even n, a sweep started from the identity ends in the lexicographically largest arrangement that any single-swap enumeration can leave; by a parity argument this is the reversal exactly when n is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The construction of the extremal variant is proved correct when n is divisible by 4 and verified by computer for all even n up to 10000.

papers.title: Extended Hamiltonian formalism for multicontact field theories
papers.abstract: We develop an extended Hamiltonian formalism for action-dependent (Herglotz-type) classical field theories within the framework of multicontact geometry. While the standard Hamiltonian description of these theories is formulated on the restricted multimomentum bundle, we work instead on the extended multimomentum bundle, which carries an additional energy-type coordinate together with a canonical multicontact structure. In this setting, an extended Hamiltonian multicontact system is governed by a Hamiltonian density and its associated Hamiltonian one-form, and the submanifold they determine recovers the restricted formalism. We characterise the admissible one-forms and prove that the associated Hamilton-de Donder-Weyl field equations, stated equivalently for sections, multivector fields, and Ehresmann connections, are mutually equivalent. We then establish the precise relation between the extended and restricted formalisms in both the regular (multicontact) and the almost-regular (premulticontact) settings, the latter requiring a constraint algorithm. The formalism is illustrated with two examples: the action-dependent Klein-Gordon equation, which includes the telegrapher equation as a particular case, and the heat equation, whose contactification yields Burgers' equation.

papers.title: The totient bound and extremal gaps in cyclotomic polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $m>1$ be odd and squarefree, and let $p\nmid m$ be prime. If $p<m$, every gap in $Φ_{mp}$ has length strictly less than $\varphi(m)$. If $p>m$, the maximum gap has length $\varphi(m)$ and occurs exactly $2\lfloor p/m\rfloor$ times. We determine its positions and endpoint coefficients. These results prove the equality criterion of Ambrosino, Hong and Lee and the multiplicity formula of Zhang. We also treat repeated prime factors, even cofactors and extremal zero runs in periodic coefficient blocks.

papers.title: Global rigidity and the Hessian energy identity for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
papers.abstract: We prove that every entire classical stable solution of the one-phase Bernoulli problem in dimension five or six is one-dimensional. In dimensions three through six, we establish an exact interior identity for the scale-invariant Hessian energy of sequences with bounded Morse index. Hence, the global stability conjecture is solved.

papers.title: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. We also make an explicit conjecture about the ideal of possible denominators (the description is using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and involves working with endoscopic subgroups of $G$). We prove this for products of general linear groups; in this case the above idea is much more explicit and Langlands correspondence is not needed for its description (it is a principle ideal, where the generator is given by some version of the discriminant function). We also prove our general conjecture for $G=\mathrm{SL}(2)$.

papers.title: Commutants of diagonal operators
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is devoted to the profound and comprehensive characterization when diagonal operators having the minimal or double commutant property on a separable Hilbert space, in terms of the topological and geometric properties of their spectra.

papers.title: Nonlinear Stability of Spiky Patterns for a Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Consumption Model with Signal-Dependent Motilities
papers.abstract: We prove the nonlinear asymptotic stability of one-dimensional spiky steady states for a three-dimensional chemotaxis--consumption system with signal-dependent motility $w^p$ ($p>0$, $α\ge2$) in the half-cylinder $Ω=\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathbb{T}^2$. The cell density satisfies a no-flux boundary condition at $x_1=0$, while the chemical concentration satisfies $w(0,x',t)=b>0$ and vanishes as $x_1\to+\infty$. For any prescribed steady-state cell mass $λ>0$, we show that any sufficiently small compatible initial perturbation with zero mass generates a unique global strong solution that converges to the spiky steady state in $L^\infty(Ω)$, with the chemical concentration converging uniformly relative to the steady profile, namely $\|w(\cdot,t)/W-1\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\to0$ as $t\to\infty$. The stability analysis for an arbitrarily large steady mass $λ>0$ in three dimensions involves four main difficulties: the algebraic degeneracy of the diffusion coefficient $W^p(x_1)\sim (1+x_1)^{-2/(α-1)}$ as $x_1\to\infty$, the $O(λ)$ linear coupling between the density perturbation and the chemical logarithmic gradient on the transversal nonzero modes, the nonlinear boundary conditions at $x_1=0$ produced by the Hopf--Cole transformation, and the different spatial weights required across derivative orders. We resolve these difficulties by introducing the algebraic weights $(ω_1,ω_2,ω_3)=(W^{-p}U^{-1},U^{-1},W^pU^{-1})$, coupling a weighted Neumann inverse on the transversal nonzero modes with the scalar logarithmic potential $Ψ+q$ to cancel the $O(λ)$ linear coupling terms exactly, performing tangential and time-differentiated weighted energy estimates whose boundary traces vanish identically at $x_1=0$, and closing the time-derivative energy before recovering the full weighted Hessian dissipation from the parabolic system.

papers.title: The random Riesz's lemma in random normed modules
papers.abstract: Riesz's lemma states that a normed space is finite-dimensional if and only if its closed unit ball is sequentially compact. The purpose of this paper is to establish a random counterpart of this lemma in a random normed module. Precisely speaking, based on the two recent developments in random functional analysis: one is the dimensional decomposition of a regular $σ$-stable $L^0$-module, and the other is the theory of random sequential compactness in a random normed module, we can finally establish the random Riesz's lemma, which states that a $σ$-stable random normed module is proper if and only if its random closed unit ball is random sequentially compact.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions II
papers.abstract: This is the second of two papers on isolated boundary singularities of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We construct positive solutions that violate the critical upper bound, proving that the dimension ranges in Part I are sharp. For general smooth metrics, the conformal metric can be incomplete near the singularity in every dimension $n\ge18$, and complete in every dimension $n\ge19$. For Euclidean domains with smooth boundary, both types exist for $n\ge23$. We also construct both types for metrics with totally geodesic boundary in dimensions $n\ge35$.

papers.title: Anderson Acceleration of SCF Iteration and Newton's Method for Solving Nonlinear Eigenvector Problems
papers.abstract: The self-consistent field (SCF) iteration is a gateway method for solving nonlinear eigenvector problems, also known as nonlinear eigenvalue problems with eigenvector dependency (NEPv).
