This is deduced as a consequence of a description, in terms of certain norm equations in finite extensions of $L$, of the semilinear Schur indices for the group $\mathbb{Z}$ acting on $L$ via $σ$. As an application, we give an explicit description of the category of isocrystals over a finite field.

papers.title: Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from infinitesimal gradings
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of infinitesimal gradings for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded $A_\infty$-categories and use it to detect Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from quantum cohomology. The dimensions we find agree with predictions from Serre functors of Kuznetsov components, such as $2$ for Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds and the fractional value $\frac{n-2}{n}$ for the symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{IG}(2,2n)$. An infinitesimal grading induces endomorphisms on cohomological morphism spaces, and we prove a straightening theorem that realizes its weights as an actual grading compatible with the $A_\infty$-structure. We use this grading to show that Dehn twists give faithful braid group representations in the symplectic mapping class groups of Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds.

papers.title: Determining Compatible Groups in $Γ$-Zonal Labelings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a plane graph with vertex, edge, and region sets $V(G),$ $E(G),$ and $F(G)$ respectively, and let $Γ$ be a nontrivial abelian group with identity element $0$. A $Γ$-zonal labeling of a plane graph $G$ is a labeling $\ell: V(G)\rightarrow Γ\setminus\{0\}$ such that for every region $f\in F(G)$, the sum of labels on the boundary of $f$ is $0$ in $Γ$. We say a $Γ$-zonal labeling is generative if the labels used generate $Γ$, and strong if the additive order of each label matches the degree of the corresponding vertex. Given a graph $G$ or a family of graphs $\mathcal{G}$, we explore restrictions on the groups $Γ$ for which there can exist a $Γ$-zonal labeling. Here we specifically determine restrictions on compatible groups when $\mathcal{G}$ is the family of $2$-connected multigraphs or $2$-connected simple graphs. We also demonstrate how the Smith normal form decomposition of the face incidence matrix of a plane graph $G$ can help characterize the groups $Γ$ for which there exists a generative $Γ$-zonal labeling.

papers.title: A bordism perspective on ends of manifolds
papers.abstract: We refine the classical pro-homotopy type of the end of a manifold by recording the boundaries of a compact exhaustion together with the bordisms between them. We show that this assignment, the bordism-end, is functorial in embeddings, and independent of the choice of exhaustion. Its target is the free sequential colimit completion of the bordism $\infty$-category. Along the way of defining the bordism-end, we show that the category of all smooth $d$-dimensional manifolds and embeddings is formally obtained from the analogous category of compact manifolds. Through the formalism of the bordism-end, it follows that a manifold is diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold if and only if its bordism-end is representable. Moreover, this formalism yields a fibre sequence relating the classifying spaces of the compactly supported diffeomorphism group of a manifold and its full diffeomorphism group, and a space of bordism-ends. Finally, we set up the pro-end functorially in embeddings, with target the cospan $\infty$-category of pro-spaces, and show that it factors through the bordism-end.

papers.title: Congruence Patterns in Spectral Gaps of mod $p$ Markoff Graphs
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the second-largest eigenvalue of mod $p$ Markoff graphs for three infinite, positive-density families of primes $p$, each defined by congruence conditions. These lower bounds arise from the structure of integral orbits on Markoff-type surfaces over certain number fields, and are strong enough to establish that $$\liminf_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv1\pmod{4}}}λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.875> 2\sqrt{2},$$ partially proving a conjecture of de Courcy-Ireland and Lee, and that $$\limsup_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv 3\pmod{4}}}(λ_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.835 > 2\sqrt{2},$$ disproving another conjecture of the same.
papers.comments: 22 pages, 8 figures. Early draft of a working paper, but contains complete proofs

papers.title: On the V-toothpick sequence
papers.abstract: We give a generating function for the V-toothpick sequence and an algorithm that computes any term in time polynomial in the number of binary digits of its index. We determine its quadratic growth and periodic fluctuations, and give convergent series for the constants in its asymptotic bounds.
papers.comments: 33 pages, 6 figures. Python code and numerical data included as ancillary files

papers.title: Cutoff on abelian groups
papers.abstract: We prove the long-predicted equivalence between the cutoff phenomenon and the product condition along any sequence of abelian random walks whose inverse transition probabilities grow at most logarithmically with the size of the group. Our result does not require reversibility, and comes with a sharp quantitative estimate on the mixing window. Moreover, we show that our sparsity restriction is optimal by constructing abelian Cayley graphs which satisfy the product condition but fail to exhibit cutoff, and whose degrees are arbitrarily close to being logarithmic in the volume.

papers.title: Second-class particle in ASEP. Rarefaction fan
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a second class particle in ASEP on the integer lattice. We prove a general formula for the distribution of its position at any fixed time for arbitrary initial conditions. As a first application, we obtain its limiting distribution for arbitrary initial conditions in the rarefaction fan case, generalizing the result of Cator--Pimentel from TASEP to ASEP.

papers.title: Global genetic inference at the scale of mass disasters
papers.abstract: DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. Joint analysis avoids this dependence on decision order, but combinatorial growth has historically made it prohibitive in large cases. In this paper, we show that the general joint identification problem is NP-hard and develop a local-to-global framework for joint genetic inference at scale. We reduce the search using genetic compatibility tests, likelihood-based pruning of unlikely assignments, and symmetry reductions. We represent pedigree likelihoods as polynomials and reformulate the Elston-Stewart algorithm for efficient parallel likelihood evaluation on GPUs. Together, these advances yield a manageable set of candidate assignments and their likelihoods, from which we construct an integer linear program that resolves competing identifications and determines the global maximum-likelihood assignment. In small benchmarks, the method recovers the exhaustive-search optimum with up to 99.96% fewer likelihood evaluations. We also apply it to simulated disasters involving up to 10 thousand victims and missing persons. The framework is not limited to a single global optimum but yields a list of probable alternative assignments, thus providing a flexible tool to be used alongside other forensic evidence.

papers.title: Multifractal analysis of Takagi-type functions built from beta-expansion cylinders
papers.abstract: We study a family of Takagi functions obtained by placing a normalized tent on each beta-expansion cylinder, with amplitude $β^{-αn}$ at order $n$, where $β>1$ and $0<α\le1$. We characterize their pointwise Hölder regularity in terms of cylinder lengths and distances from the point under consideration. The characterization holds more generally for nested interval partitions with exponentially decreasing mesh, without requiring interval lengths at a given order to be comparable. For beta-expansion cylinders, we compute the full multifractal spectrum whenever the remainders of the expansion of $1$ have a finite upper exponential decay rate. The functions are monofractal when this rate vanishes, as it does for Parry, Pisot and Salem bases. When it is positive, the spectrum is affine on a nondegenerate interval. The bases defined by $\sum_{k\ge0}β_\ell^{-\ell^k}=1$, for integers $\ell\ge2$, give explicit non-monofractal examples. We also prove that every function in the family is nowhere differentiable.

papers.title: Circular Vector Tomography with Partial Radial Data
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce and study several generalized circular Radon transforms acting on smooth vector fields compactly supported in a planar annulus, with centers restricted to the outer acquisition circle and truncated measurement radii. The operators of interest are the longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transforms and their weighted analogues. We characterize the kernels of the individual unweighted transforms. Then we establish the reconstruction of a vector field from the combined longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transform data. We further show that the pairs formed by each transform and its weighted analogue is not sufficient for the complete recovery of a vector field. However, we demonstrate that full reconstruction is possible with suitable additional data. Finally, we numerically implement and validate the derived inversion formulas.

papers.title: Non-homogeneous parabolic conormal boundary problem with singular-degenerate coefficients
papers.abstract: We study non-homogeneous conormal boundary value problems for a class of divergence-form parabolic equations whose volumetric heat-capacity coefficients belong to a Muckenhoupt class of weights. Consequently, the equations exhibit singular, degenerate, or simultaneously singular-degenerate behavior. Under smallness conditions on the partial mean oscillation of the diffusion coefficients and the weighted mean oscillation of the volumetric heat-capacity coefficient, we establish regularity estimates, existence, and uniqueness results in appropriate weighted Sobolev spaces. To obtain these results, we employ the level-set argument introduced by Caffarelli and Peral. We also establish weighted parabolic cylinders, weighted inequalities, and a weighted Aubin-Lions compactness theorem, which are essential tools in our analysis.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Gibbs Posterior Measures on Infinite-Dimensional Hypothesis Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove almost sure contraction rates and consistency for Gibbs posterior measures on arbitrary hypothesis spaces, in general infinite dimensional, under dependent data, nonadditive and time-dependent losses and learning rates, misspecified models, and unattainable minimisers of the limiting objective. In particular, we develop a novel proof approach in contraction rate theory by studying the asymptotics of Gibbs measures through Lorentz spaces, real interpolation theory, and Laplace transforms dispensing with testing or variational formulations which are unavailable in the considered generality. As a consequence we obtain almost sure contraction rates for dominated Bayes and fractional Bayes posterior measures in the same generality, extending existing theory on misspecified Bayesian inference. Furthermore, we demonstrate our theoretical results on novel applications to Gibbs posteriors for Dirichlet process priors with a nonadditive Wasserstein metric loss function under ergodic, non-Markovian observables.

papers.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$. To narrow this gap, we propose an inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient (SVRG) method that significantly improves the previously best-known first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Furthermore, when the objective consists of a single function, the proposed method reduces to a novel deterministic first-order method for solving standard convex conic optimization. It achieves a significantly lower gradient evaluation complexity with respect to the objective function compared to existing methods, and can outperform them when computing constraint gradients and projections onto the associated cone is cheaper than evaluating the objective gradient. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.
papers.comments: Accepted by SIAM Journal on Optimization

papers.title: Sidorenko Inequalities in Oriented Graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce relative Sidorenko and relative anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs, strengthening the corresponding well-studied notions for tournaments by allowing arbitrary host graphs. An orientation $\vec H$ of a graph $H$ is relatively Sidorenko if $\hom(\vec H,\vec G) \ge 2^{-e(H)}\hom(H,G)$ for every oriented graph $\vec G$ with underlying graph $G$, and relatively anti-Sidorenko if the reverse inequality holds. We provide a complete characterisation of the class of connected relatively Sidorenko graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs, and exhibit several families of relatively Sidorenko and relatively anti-Sidorenko oriented graphs. Despite the substantially stronger definitions, many known tournament Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko examples satisfy the relative inequalities, suggesting a broader theory of these phenomena in arbitrary host graphs and motivating several new structural and classification problems.

papers.title: On the multiplicity of crossing limit cycles of double diagonalizable piecewise linear vector fields
papers.abstract: We consider planar piecewise linear vector fields with two zones separated by a straight line and having two diagonalizable components, which we call the \emph{double diagonalizable configuration}. In this configuration, the Poincaré half-maps correspond to separatrices of saddle points in the foliations of symmetric differential forms $ω_r(x)-ω_r(y)$, where $ω_r$ is a rational $1$-form with exactly three simple poles. Limit cycles correspond to non-diagonal intersections of two such separatrices, and the multiplicity of a limit cycle is precisely the order of contact at the intersection point. We prove that two distinct separatrices which are not nested segments of the same straight line have a contact of order at most $4$ at a diagonal point and at most $2$ at a non-diagonal point. As a consequence, we obtain that the multiplicity of limit cycles in the double diagonalizable configuration is at most two, this bound being sharp.

papers.title: Robust feedback control of collisional plasma dynamics in presence of uncertainties
papers.abstract: Magnetic fusion aims to confine high-temperature plasma within a device, enabling the fusion of deuterium and tritium nuclei to release energy. Due to the very large temperatures involved, it is essential to isolate the plasma from the device walls to prevent structural damage and the external magnetic fields play a fundamental role in achieving this confinement. In realistic settings, the physical mechanisms governing plasma behavior are highly complex, involving numerous uncertain parameters and intricate particle interactions, such as collisions, that significantly affect both confinement efficiency and overall stability. In this work, we address particularly these challenges by proposing a robust feedback control strategy designed to steer the plasma towards a desired spatial region, despite the presence of uncertainties. From a modeling perspective, we consider a collisional plasma described by a Vlasov-Poisson-BGK system, which accounts for a self-consistent electric field and a strong external magnetic field, while incorporating uncertainty in the model. A key feature of the proposed control strategy is its independence from the random parameter, making it particularly suitable for practical applications. A series of numerical simulations confirms the effectiveness of our approach and demonstrates the ability of external magnetic fields to successfully confine plasma away from the device boundaries, even in the presence of uncertain conditions.

papers.title: Control strategies for magnetized plasma: a polar coordinates framework
papers.abstract: In this work, we provide an overview of various control strategies aimed at steering plasma toward desired configurations using an external magnetic field. From a modeling perspective, we focus on the Vlasov equation in a two-dimensional bounded domain, accounting for both a self-induced electric field and a strong external magnetic field. The results are presented in a polar coordinate framework, which is particularly well-suited for simulating toroidal devices such as Tokamaks and Stellarators. A key feature of the proposed control strategies is their feedback mechanism, which is based on an instantaneous prediction of the discretized system. Finally, different numerical experiments in the two-dimensional polar coordinate setting demonstrate the effectiveness of the approaches.

papers.title: Micro-Macro Tensor Neural Surrogates for Uncertainty Quantification in Collisional Plasma
papers.abstract: Plasma kinetic equations exhibit pronounced sensitivity to microscopic perturbations in model parameters and data, making reliable and efficient uncertainty quantification (UQ) essential for predictive simulations. However, the cost of uncertainty sampling, the high-dimensional phase space, and multiscale stiffness pose severe challenges to both computational efficiency and error control in traditional numerical methods. These aspects are further emphasized in presence of collisions where the high-dimensional nonlocal collision integrations and conservation properties pose severe constraints. To overcome this, we present a variance-reduced Monte Carlo framework for UQ in the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau (VPL) system, in which neural network surrogates replace the multiple costly evaluations of the Landau collision term. The method couples a high-fidelity, asymptotic-preserving VPL solver with inexpensive, strongly correlated surrogates based on the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Euler--Poisson (EP) equations. For the surrogate models, we introduce a generalization of the separable physics-informed neural network (SPINN), developing a class of tensor neural networks based on an anisotropic micro-macro decomposition, to reduce velocity-moment costs, model complexity, and the curse of dimensionality. To further increase correlation with VPL, we calibrate the VPFP model and design an asymptotic-preserving SPINN whose small- and large-Knudsen limits recover the EP and VP systems, respectively. Numerical experiments show substantial variance reduction over standard Monte Carlo, accurate statistics with far fewer high-fidelity samples, and lower wall-clock time, while maintaining robustness to stochastic dimension.

papers.title: Finite-size Entanglement Certification via Third-Order Local Randomized Measurements
papers.abstract: Certifying entanglement in high-dimensional systems usually requires full state tomography, whose cost grows rapidly with the system dimension. Local randomized measurements offer a scalable alternative, but existing tests based on second-order correlations access only limited information about the state. Here, we derive a finite-size entanglement certificate that extends local randomized measurements to third order. The additional third-order information reveals entanglement that remains undetected at second order, while a dimension-independent concentration bound provides rigorous control of finite-sample errors. Our result opens a practical route to extracting stronger entanglement information from experimental platforms without the dimension-dependent overhead of state tomography.
papers.comments: Previously this version appeared as arXiv:2604.13165 which was submitted as a new work by accident. Any subsequent updates will appear there

papers.title: Full-horizon magnetic control of the Vlasov--Poisson system for plasma confinement
papers.abstract: We study the full-horizon control of a two-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system through an externally imposed magnetic field. The control is represented by time-dependent coefficients associated with smooth, spatially localized basis functions, and is designed to steer selected position and velocity moments of the distribution function while limiting particle dispersion and the control effort. Starting from the kinetic constrained optimization problem, we derive the continuous first-order optimality conditions, including a backward Vlasov equation, an elliptic adjoint equation, and the variational inequality associated with bounded controls. We then project this system onto a particle--grid representation and identify the resulting particle adjoints and control gradient. The full-horizon field is then computed on a reduced particle ensemble, initialized by an instantaneous control, and subsequently applied to a larger set of particles. Numerical experiments indicate that the instantaneous control field already provides an effective baseline, while the full-horizon correction can further reduce the relative thermal energy near the boundaries and improve confinement over the prescribed time interval.

papers.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

papers.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

papers.title: Complexity and symmetry: The asymmetry factor approach
papers.abstract: We study the influence of the instantaneous appearance of a time-like Killing vector (TKV) in self-gravitating fluid spheres during their evolution. For doing so we resort to the concept of asymmetry factor which allows the existence of any specific type of symmetry (e.g. a TKV), exclusively, for a given value of the time-like coordinate. We consider adiabatic and dissipative fluids. The analysis of different relevant physical variables in this process shows the imprints of the emergence of TKV at some point of the evolution. Particular attention is paid to the relationship appearing between the TKV, and the complexity factor describing the degree of complexity of the fluid, bringing out for the first time a link between complexity and symmetry.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 4 figures. Revtex-4. Invited contribution published in AIMS Mathematics (Special Issue: Statistical Complexity in Natural Systems and Artificial Intelligence)
papers.journal_ref: AIMS Mathematics 11, 35737, (2026)

papers.title: A singular minimizer of a uniformly convex Hessian-dependent functional
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth, uniformly convex Hessian-dependent energy functional, which admits a singular $C^{1,1}$ minimizer on $\mathbb{R}^5$ that is a two-homogeneous normalization of Cartan's five-dimensional cubic. Our construction relies on constructing a quadratic null Lagrangian for the Hessian that is suitably non-degenerate on the image of the Hessian for the candidate minimizer. This complements a partial regularity result previously obtained by the authors in this setting, and demonstrates that one cannot hope for a fourth-order version of classical second-order elliptic regularity theory à la De Giorgi-Nash-Moser.

papers.title: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
papers.abstract: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.

papers.title: Lifting asymptotic symmetries from metric to tetrad formulation
papers.abstract: Metric solution spaces defined by gauge and boundary conditions are associated with a residual symmetry algebra, consisting of the diffeomorphism generators whose action preserves these conditions. Describing a metric solution space in terms of tetrad variables adds a local Lorentz freedom. When part of this freedom is fixed by additional tetrad gauge and boundary conditions, metric residual symmetries must be supplemented by compensating Lorentz transformations. If a residual Lorentz freedom remains, there is an ambiguity in these compensating transformations. The most direct choices generally fail to realize the metric residual symmetry algebra as a subalgebra of the tetrad one, because of a field-dependent cocycle. We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.

papers.title: Cycles of Arbitrary Period in Multidimensional Heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study periodic behavior in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause opinion dynamics with multidimensional opinions and norm-defined confidence neighborhoods. We prove that, for every dimension $d\ge3$, every $\ell_q$ norm with $q\in[1,\infty]\setminus\{2\}$, and every integer $m\ge2$, a system of five agents admits a periodic trajectory of minimal period $m$; moreover, different periods can coexist for fixed confidence radii. Four agents remain stationary, while the fifth moves along a line segment contained in their convex hull. The stationary agents may share a common strictly positive confidence radius, and all confidence inequalities are strict. A geometric criterion underlying the construction extends these results to further classes of norms. However, this criterion cannot be satisfied in dimensions one and two, regardless of the confidence norm. We also prove that no heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause system with less than five agents admits a nonconstant periodic trajectory, under any norm and in any dimension; every trajectory with at most three agents converges exponentially.

papers.title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.

papers.title: Covariance Cells And Star Products
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, a localized preparation is described not only by a point in phase space but also by a covariance cell specifying its finite resolution. We study balanced Gaussian cells on a linear symplectic space and show that they are equivalent to compatible complex structures and positive Lagrangian polarizations. Their parameter space is the Siegel symmetric space. Using the Koopman-von Neumann representation of classical mechanics, we describe the linearized transport of Gaussian amplitudes along a reference motion. Each covariance cell determines a separated star product whose antisymmetric part is fixed by the symplectic form and whose symmetric part is fixed by the covariance. This product is related to the Moyal product by Gaussian smoothing. Quadratic Hamiltonians act through their classical Poisson derivations within a fixed cell algebra exactly when they preserve the cell; squeezing transformations instead relate the algebras associated with different cells. Fronsdal's star-polarization construction yields a module whose cyclic element is the Gaussian density of the cell. Its completion is the corresponding Bargmann-Fock space, naturally embedded in the space of classical Koopman amplitudes. Koopman transport carries this Fock space to that of the transported cell. No Planck constant is introduced: the deformation parameter is a classical resolution scale, and physical observables remain commuting multiplication operators.

papers.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
papers.abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
papers.abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlevé V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.

papers.title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
papers.abstract: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topological quantum order across the multiscale hierarchy using a linearly dilated relaxation of the usual Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis criteria. In the companion paper, we combine the tools developed here with finite-temperature worldline cluster expansions to establish passive self-correction throughout the phase diagram's positive-temperature perturbed interior.

papers.title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
papers.abstract: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm iβ/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.

papers.title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.

papers.title: Boxes in Infinite Words: Complexity, Automata, and Point Modules
papers.abstract: Motivated by the geometry of point modules over monomial algebras, we introduce a box-counting function associated to a right-infinite word over a finite alphabet. An extendable box is a family of finite words obtained by choosing letters independently at each position, subject to the condition that all choices admit a common infinite right continuation in the associated subshift. We prove several results for these functions for words of linearly bounded complexity. For $k$-automatic words, we show using techniques from first-order logic that the total box-counting function is $k$-regular. Finally, we apply our results to prove eventual affine growth of the number of positive-dimensional irreducible components in finite projections of point-module spaces associated to semiprime monomial algebras of at most quadratic growth.

papers.title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
papers.abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $ρ_n=\sin^2θ_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $γ$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 2 figures. Companion to "Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures" (D. Rens, submitted). Lean 4 formalization of the finite-dimensional core and the numerical study are in the ancillary files

papers.title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
papers.abstract: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

papers.title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
papers.abstract: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-ε)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

papers.title: Optimal Network Design under Node Failures
papers.abstract: Networks are frequently constructed before it is determined which nodes will persist. We address the design problem in scenarios where nodes fail independently, links are costly and must be established in advance, and the benefits to surviving nodes diminish with distance. Examples include supplier, interbank, and infrastructure networks. Among all possible networks, the complete, star, and empty configurations are each welfare-optimal within specific ranges of link costs. However, with four or more nodes, failures introduce a range of costs in which every optimal network contains more links than the star but fewer than the complete network. At the lower end of this range, we show that the optimal networks are exactly those obtained by removing a matching from the complete network. We develop an exact algorithm for complete multipartite networks. It finds an optimal network by dynamic programming in a number of operations that grows with the fourth power of the number of nodes, although the class itself grows superpolynomially. For networks with up to six nodes, restricting the design to this class results in no loss under explicit conditions. We also characterize pairwise-stable networks within this class and establish their existence for every level of link cost. Finally, we quantify the cost of misjudging failure risk. Overestimating node survival leads to overbuilding and can yield lower welfare than building nothing, whereas underestimating it never does. Under uncertain failure risk, design should therefore favor conservative reliability estimates.

papers.title: A Geometric Framework for Local-to-Global Symmetry: Global Constraints on Local Dynamics
papers.abstract: Aggregate molecular systems are routinely understood by decomposing them into local structural units, such as monomers in J/H-aggregates, chemical moieties, motifs, and functional groups. Implicit in such decompositions is the assumption that these local structures remain meaningful within the aggregate. Here, we ask how the symmetries of constituent structures relate to aggregate symmetry, and how this relation determines the constraints that global symmetry imposes on transitions between local symmetry sectors. We construct a covariant local-to-global representation from framed local symmetry data and show that its reconstruction map intertwines with a global quantum representation. By identifying which global symmetry sectors overlap each local symmetry sector, we resolve symmetry-enforced dynamical exclusions into site-resolved pathways. Through Frobenius reciprocity, these exclusions can be determined from standard character tables of the local and global symmetry groups, with the character values in the inner product paired according to the relative positions and orientations of local structures within the aggregate. Although motivated by molecular aggregates, the construction is formulated for arbitrary geometries modeled by a homogeneous space of an ambient transformation group.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
papers.abstract: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side. To explain, we derive reduced-order models: the softmax is a Boltzmann distribution, gradient descent an Euler step on a nonlinear spring, a loss spike a ball thrown out of a stiff valley, attention on the circle a Kuramoto model, and a repetition loop a well that deepens while it is occupied. We then test these explanations on open language models, on a laptop CPU. Escape from repetition loops in GPT-2 and Pythia follows the Arrhenius law with the logit gap as the barrier, and the barrier deepens and then saturates, so the temperature needed to leave a loop falls like $1/\ln N$ with the generation length $N$ and rises with model size. Coherent text lives in a narrow window of temperatures, which a small reasoning model shares at its recommended temperature. Training makes each Pythia layer more expansive, and a small transformer trains at a multi-mode edge of stability. The third step, solving problems of language models, is still ahead: controllers derived from the escape analysis remove loops but do not yet beat the best fixed temperature. We state twelve open problems where nonlinear dynamics could get there.

papers.title: First-Order Model-Free Policy Gradient for Undiscounted LQR with Global Optimality and Convergence Guarantees
papers.abstract: We provide a first-order model-free policy gradient (PG) framework for learning undiscounted infinite-horizon linear quadratic regulator (LQR) policies with global optimality and convergence guarantees. We first construct a stochastic wrapper policy class parameterized by the LQR gain to enable exploration around a deterministic linear control law. We analyze the additional cost induced by exploration over infinite-horizon, and establish a weak gradient dominance condition that characterizes global optimality under exploration. We then construct a model-free first-order PG algorithm using sampled trajectory information, without identifying the dynamics or approximating a value function. Finally, we establish finite-time convergence guarantees, providing the sufficient number of samples required for near-global optimality with our proposed PG algorithms.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints: Policy Gradient Methods with Intersample Guarantees
papers.abstract: We develop a policy-gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework with hard inter-sample control barrier function (CBF)-based safety constraints for nonlinear sampled-data systems. We first design a class of stochastic policies with support truncated to sampling-period-dependent safe control sets, that guarantee safety-by-construction at sampling instants. We then propose a model-free PG algorithm that searches over the class of safe-by-design policies and establish sufficient conditions on sampling-period such that any action sampled from safe control sets remains safe throughout the sampling interval, providing inter-sample guarantees. We further establish finite-time convergence and sample complexity guarantees for the proposed PG algorithm and characterize its global optimality under gradient dominance. Finally, we illustrate inter-sample safety guarantees on a safe quadrotor navigation environment.

papers.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation
papers.abstract: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes remains largely unexplored. A general closed-form SWT generator and a clear physical principle for gauge fixing remain elusive, obscuring the transformation's underlying structure. We introduce the dual SWT to deal with the strong-coupling problems. The generalized SWT (gSWT) is formulated for any Hermitian operator and block partition. We establish the geodesic principle for its canonical gauge. Furthermore, we derive an exact closed-form solution of the gSWT generator at every order as a finite nested-commutator sum whose only input is the active gap set. Both the geometric and algebraic aspects of the SWT physics are revealed. The gSWT framework is illustrated in two quantum many-body models, the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.

papers.title: A mechanistic characterization of missingness at random
papers.abstract: The missingness-at-random (MAR) assumption underlying many missing-data methods describes abstract statistical independences, whereas practitioners reason more naturally about the causal mechanisms that generate missingness. To bridge this gap, we provide a mechanistic characterization of MAR in terms of paths in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) modified to allow certain edges to cease to operate when an incomplete variable is missing, a property termed "context-specific causal irrelevance (CSCI)". Under a faithfulness condition, MAR holds if and only if the modified DAG contains no MAR-violating paths. Without CSCI, this condition reduces to a previously established d-separation condition, VMAR; thus, MAR without VMAR requires specific kinds of CSCI, as can occur with monotone dropout. These results shift the burden on investigators from passively invoking MAR to justifying, on substantive grounds, the specific mechanisms it requires. We then consider identification of a target law p(v) of variables V by a MAR-assuming analysis, e.g., multiple imputation, that includes complete auxiliary variables Z (variables not in V). Barring a perfect cancellation, such an analysis recovers p(v) if and only if MAR holds with respect to V and Z jointly. We show that if there exists any set of auxiliaries such that (V, Z) obeys MAR, then the complete candidate auxiliaries that are ancestors of the target variables or their missingness indicators form a sufficient set. Contrary to standard recommendations, not all candidate auxiliaries should be used: even complete auxiliaries can introduce MAR violations that would not otherwise occur. We illustrate these results with simulations and an analysis of sexual identity change in the Stockholm Public Health Cohort, where our results indicate that a candidate auxiliary, income, should be excluded; including it attenuated estimates toward the null.
papers.comments: 70 pages: 34-page main text followed by 36-page supplement

papers.title: Single-Vertex Metropolis on Minor-Free Graphs: A General EPTAS
papers.abstract: We consider a class of combinatorial optimization problems where the goal is to find a largest induced subgraph with a prescribed property. We assume that the property is preserved by taking induced subgraphs and disjoint unions, holds for all edgeless graphs, and can be tested in polynomial time. We study the single-vertex Metropolis process for this class of problems. We show that on graphs excluding an arbitrary fixed minor $H$, this process is a randomized efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme. Starting from any feasible solution on a graph with $n$ vertices, it finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation within $\exp(O_H(\varepsilon^{-2})) n(n+\log(1/δ))$ steps with probability at least $1-δ$. This includes maximum independent set, maximum induced forest, maximum induced bipartite subgraph, and maximum induced subgraph of degree at most one. The proof uses improving exchanges on one fixed division of the input graph into regions. A recursive separator construction performs each exchange inside a region of size $r$ in at most $2r$ moves, with temporary loss $O_H(\sqrt r)$. We count move sequences through each transition and bound the probability of avoiding all near-optimal states. The general theorem bounds the number of Metropolis steps in terms of the temporary loss along improvement paths. We extend the result to bounded weight imbalance and give a weighted-star obstruction for unrestricted weights.

papers.title: Cantor correlations II. Synchronicity and bisynchronicity
papers.abstract: We study synchronous and bisynchronous no-signalling correlations, defined over Cantor topological spaces, from the perspectives of both continuous variable quantum information and operator algebra theories. We focus on strategies, satisfying a natural no-signalling condition across the Cantor space levels, called graded, identifying a universal C*-algebra, whose tracial states of different types characterise synchronous correlations of respective types. The universal C*-algebra for bisynchronous graded correlations is shown to coincide with the C*-algebra of a projective limit of free wreath products of quantum permutation groups, introduced by Bhowmick, Goswami and Skalski, and a type description, analogous to the one in the synchronous case, is provided. Extending results in the finite case, we show that bisynchronous graded correlations canonically give rise to factorisable maps on type I factors, defined via Cantor permutation matrices. We examine non-local games over Cantor topological spaces, with inputs/outputs that are finite words of equal length, define corresponding game algebras, and characterise the perfect strategies of the games via the respective game algebras. In the case of the Cantor graph isomorphism game, we provide equivalent descriptions of the existence of perfect strategies of quantum commuting type, in terms of bigalois correspondences, factorisable maps, Cantor permutation intertwiners and game algebra non-triviality. Our results supply a quantum information interpretation of a notion of a quantum isomorphism of locally finite graphs, introduced by Rollier and Vaes, canonically arising from Cantor graphs.

papers.title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
papers.abstract: We develop neural network methods for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations at a small viscosity $\varepsilon > 0$, whose accuracy is uniform in $\varepsilon$ and whose residual is evaluated on a grid that does not resolve the vorticity boundary layer. In the vorticity-stream function formulation with the slip boundary conditions, a vorticity layer of width $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ forms along the walls. The trial function of the singular layer Physics-Informed Neural Network (sl-PINN) contains the corrector of the asymptotic analysis, together with the law that fixes its amplitude at the wall. The amplitude is tied to the wall trace of the network itself, so that the method requires no a priori knowledge of the limit solution. The sl-PINN keeps the error uniform in $\varepsilon$ over six decades, for the Stokes and the Navier-Stokes equations alike, although in the latter the wall trace travels with the flow and is not known in advance. An enrichment that uses the thin scale but leaves the profile and the amplitude of the layer free deteriorates as $\varepsilon\to0$. Since the corrector carries the layer analytically, the Laplacian in the residual can be discretized by a finite volume flux difference on a coarse grid. The resulting singular layer Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) attains the same uniform accuracy as the sl-PINN, to within the scatter of the random seed, at about half the cost of a training step. The combination of the asymptotic corrector with the coarse-grid finite volume discretization is the main result of this article.

papers.title: COSI: A Framework for Robustly Valid Inference
papers.abstract: We introduce COSI (COnfidence from Scale Invariance), a framework for constructing confidence sets for statistical functionals. COSI builds on the HulC (Hull-based Confidence), which uses median unbiasedness to construct confidence sets from batch estimates. COSI uses scale-invariance properties shared by many common estimators. We divide the data into batches, compute an estimate in each batch, and retain each candidate parameter value for which the batch estimates pass a test of scale invariance. The resulting confidence sets are asymptotically valid under weaker assumptions than classical Wald and bootstrap procedures require, and their coverage can be closer to the nominal level in small samples. Applications include robust inference for the mean, regression coefficients in misspecified linear models, tensor norms, and Fréchet means.
papers.comments: Slides based on this paper can be found at https://arun-kuchibhotla.github.io/docs/talk/ (These slides includes more examples and sometime more simulations. The discussion in some of these slides is also informal.)

papers.title: Semantic Communication via Analog RF Computing: When the Radio Computes the Meaning
papers.abstract: Semantic communication (SC) systems transmit continuous latent representations of meaning, but computing the semantic encoder at resource-constrained edge devices incurs substantial energy and memory costs. To address this challenge, we propose an end-to-end SC framework that executes the semantic encoder in the client's RF receiver front end using analog RF computing. A base station (BS) broadcasts encoder weights as RF waveforms, while each edge device reuses its receiver's passive mixer to compute semantic latents at ultra-low energy. These latents are transmitted over the uplink for network-side task inference. We show that analog computing noise across encoder layers and channel noise affecting transmitted latents admit a unified mathematical model. We define a task-posterior semantic distortion metric and derive its second-order decomposition into per-client, per-stage semantic sensitivities. Using this decomposition, we obtain a closed-form semantic-aware water-filling allocation of the total client energy budget across clients, encoder layers, and uplinks, assigning tighter accuracy targets to semantically sensitive stages. This allocation induces a broadcast beamforming problem that accounts for client-specific, per-layer accuracy requirements. We further refine the allocation through stochastic optimization and jointly design it with multi-task noise-aware training of the shared semantic model. MNIST simulations show that, at matched total client energy, the proposed allocation reduces network semantic distortion by 9.2\%-19.2\% compared with uniform precision and 5.1\%-13.1\% compared with client-blind allocation. Noise-aware co-design yields a further 46\% reduction.

papers.title: Grid-Responsive Pricing of Dynamic Wireless Charging with Coupled Residential Demand
papers.abstract: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) is an emerging technology that enables electric vehicles (EVs) to recharge while traveling. Its unique operational model creates two revenue streams for DWC operators through lane access tolls and electricity sales. However, these prices influence not only traffic flow and roadway energy delivery but also how much EV charging moves to homes instead, potentially within the same distribution network. Neglecting this coupling can underestimate grid loading and compromise pricing decisions. We develop a coupled traffic, EV energy, driver-response, and AC distribution network model with a model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes DWC tolls and charging prices while explicitly accounting for displaced residential charging and network losses. Using 78 days of I-210 West traffic data, we show that conventional MPC exceeds feeder loading limits on 52 days, whereas the proposed residential load aware controller eliminates these violations with only 0.6% lower operator revenue. Under a more constrained feeder configuration, it eliminates 50 overloaded days with a 0.9% revenue reduction. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of accurate residential demand estimation and feeder loss modeling, while peak-aware pricing further reduces daily peak loading by 3.7% relative to the base load. These results demonstrate the value of coordinated pricing that captures the interaction between roadway and residential charging.
papers.comments: 5 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to the IEEE Power & Energy Society General Meeting (PESGM) 2027

papers.title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
papers.abstract: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. These approaches typically quantify drag reduction as a function of a single geometric parameter, such as spanwise spacing or groove cross-sectional area, evaluated over fixed riblet shapes. As a result, identifying optimal riblet geometries across a broader design space often necessitates exhaustive parametric studies. To address this problem, we propose an optimization framework for the systematic design of optimal riblet shapes. Accordingly, we reformulate the volume penalization term in the linearized dynamics as a structured state-feedback operator. Targeting maximal suppression of turbulence, we pose a composite optimization problem that minimizes the steady-state variance of velocity fluctuations and riblet-induced dynamical augmentations while maintaining a constant bulk-flux. For a fixed spanwise wavelength (riblet spacing), this framework yields optimal wall-normal profiles that achieve maximal turbulence attenuation.

papers.title: A faster algorithm for commutator length in free groups
papers.abstract: We compute the commutator length $\cl(w)$ of a reduced word $w\in[F,F]$ of length $M$ in a free group. Given a target $g\ge1$, a deterministic algorithm decides $\cl(w)\le g$ and, when it holds, returns a decomposition into at most $g$ commutators, in $O(M^{3g})$ steps; trying $g=1,2,\dots$ gives $\cl(w)$ in $O(M^{3\cl(w)})$ steps. For $g=1$ the same test takes $O(M)$ expected steps on a uniformly random reduced input in $[F,F]$. All bounds are in the unit-cost model.

papers.title: Strong Transitivity of Group Cellular Automata: Characterization and Decidability
papers.abstract: A discrete-time dynamical system is strongly transitive if every point can be reached, in finitely many steps, from every non-empty open set. We study this property for group cellular automata, \ie cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism, in every dimension $d\geq1$. We prove that no group cellular automaton over a non-abelian group is strongly transitive, and we develop a decomposition of group cellular automata over abelian groups, via quotients by power subgroups, which preserves strong transitivity. For linear cellular automata over $(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^n$ we use Pontryagin duality to characterize strong transitivity in terms of the characteristic polynomial $χ_A$ of the associated matrix $A$ of Laurent polynomials: the automaton is strongly transitive if and only if $\det(A)\neq0$ and no irreducible factor of $χ_A$ has an invertible constant term. Combining these results, we obtain that strong transitivity is decidable for group cellular automata in every dimension. For every fixed dimension $d$, we give an explicit decision procedure whose running time is polynomial in the group size $N$, the number $k$ of neighbours, and the neighbourhood radius $\varrho$.

papers.title: Multilevel Filtering on Manifolds with Light Schrödinger Bridges
papers.abstract: In this article we consider the filtering of partially observed diffusions when the observations, made at discrete times, are noiseless. Each observation then confines the hidden state to a manifold defined by the data, whose type, for instance a sphere or an affine subspace, may change from one observation time to the next. In practice, the filter is approximated by particle filters, which require the diffusion to be discretized in time. Multilevel Monte Carlo reduces the cost of this discretization only if the particle approximations at consecutive discretization levels stay close, which standard particle filters do not ensure. We develop a new particle filter based on light Schrödinger bridges, which works between changing manifolds and can be coupled across discretization levels. A key insight is that the previous state enters the light Schrödinger bridge only through a few features, so that the bridge only has to be fitted on the new manifold, regardless of the type of the previous one. We bound the bias of this particle filter and the gap between its approximations at consecutive levels, and show numerically, on spheres and on manifolds that change type, that this gap is much smaller than with standard multilevel particle filters, and that, with the cost of the fits included, a hybrid estimator that uses it at the fine levels reduces the cost at small tolerances.

papers.title: The Multivariate Feedback Particle Filter for State-dependent Multiplicative Noises and Its Application to Attitude and Pose Estimations
papers.abstract: Nonlinear filtering with state-dependent multiplicative measurement noise poses a notable challenge for spacecraft attitude determination and robotic pose estimation. This work develops the FPF-DM, a decomposition scheme for feedback particle filters tailored to this family of filtering problems. Extending prior decomposition techniques for additive noise and polynomial measurement models, the proposed method resolves the key difficulty that state-dependent multiplicative noise breaks the polynomial assumption and prevents Hermite spectral backward recursion for the weighted Poisson's equation. By measure transformation and importance reweighting, we incorporate the inverse measurement covariance into particle weights and rescale the feedback gain to restore the polynomial-form Poisson's equation, with the decomposition generalized to non-uniformly weighted mixtures for closed-form gain computation. This general FPF-DM is instantiated on quaternion and dual-quaternion manifolds for attitude tracking and point-cloud registration. Simulations on 4D attitude tracking and 8D point-cloud registration verify that the instantiated filters using only 10 particles achieve superior accuracy and computational performance relative to baseline filters.

papers.title: FAST: Functional Adaptive Sensing and Testing for Quickest Change Detection
papers.abstract: Quickest change detection (QCD) is studied for partially observed functional data streams. At each sampling epoch, a function is realized over a continuous domain, but its values can be observed at only a fixed number of locations. At an unknown change point, the functional mean undergoes a shift that is assumed to admit a sparse representation in a localized basis. We propose Functional Adaptive Sensing and Testing (FAST), which jointly estimates the unknown post-change parameter, selects sensing locations, and performs sequential detection. A minimax lower bound on the worst-case detection delay is derived under an average-run-length constraint. A non-asymptotic estimation-error bound is established for the policy-dependent observations induced by adaptive sensing. Under the stated regularity conditions, FAST is first-order asymptotically optimal when sensing subsets are optimized exactly. Simulations and a wildfire case study demonstrate the performance of the proposed procedure.

papers.title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of neural networks in solving partial differential equations depends not only on their approximation capability but also on the suitability of their representations for the underlying solutions. Motivated by stochastic integral representations of incompressible fluid flows and the associated Biot--Savart kernel, we propose a Biot--Savart-informed (i.e. physics-informed) neural network (BS-PINN) for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations. By extracting a rational profile from a regularized Biot--Savart kernel, we construct a smooth activation function with fixed and learnable kernel scales. Both variants retain the conventional velocity--pressure formulation and physics-informed training framework, allowing the influence of the activation function to be examined independently. We evaluate the method on five benchmarks, including Kovasznay flow, cylinder wake, three-dimensional Beltrami flow, Taylor--Green vortex, and double shear layer. Across 21 benchmark--architecture comparisons, both variants consistently reduce the combined velocity error relative to the conventional $\tanh$-based PINN, achieving mean relative error reductions of 31.7\% and 33.2\%, respectively. Improvements are also observed in reported pressure and vorticity errors. Notably, the double-shear-layer experiments demonstrate improved resolution of localized shear structures and, for BS-PINN-F, qualitatively clearer vortex-roll-up patterns in the long-time simulation. These findings highlight the potential of incorporating analytical flow structures into neural-network representations for incompressible flow simulations.
papers.comments: Physics-informed neural networks; Navier--Stokes equations; Stochastic integral representations; Biot--Savart kernel; Numerical simulation

papers.title: The Price of Hard Coverage Constraints in Online Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction provides distribution-free uncertainty quantification, but in sequential deployment, standard coverage guarantees can still allow substantial fluctuations in the number of miscoverages over time. We study an online setting in which prediction sets are produced one round at a time and the cumulative number of miscoverages must stay within a prescribed budget throughout deployment.Such a hard coverage guarantee can be enforced by enlarging prediction sets, but how much additional prediction-set size is fundamentally necessary remains unclear. We characterize this unavoidable efficiency cost over $T$ prediction rounds. Remarkably, the cost persists even with i.i.d.\ data, a known score distribution, and perfect knowledge of the population-optimal prediction set. Under suitable regularity conditions relating coverage and prediction-set size, we determine the minimum cumulative excess prediction-set size required by any online method satisfying the hard coverage constraint. This minimum cost is $Θ(\log T)$ for expected cost at a fixed time known in advance, $Θ(T^{1/3})$ for the largest expected cost over all fixed times up to $T$, and $Θ(\sqrt{T})$ for the expected worst realized cost when the evaluation time is chosen in hindsight. We further show that these rates can be attained using past scores, without knowing the score distribution. Thus, even perfect statistical knowledge does not make sequential reliability free.

papers.title: Feedback and Resource Competition in Incoherent Feedforward Loops: When Is Cumulative Dose Ordering Preserved?
papers.abstract: Biochemical coupling can change the expression levels and timing predicted by an incoherent feedforward loop (IFFL) model without changing cumulative dose ordering. We derive ordering conditions using shared-production identities and Metzler comparison bounds, with tail guarantees beyond finite computation. A nonlinear example exhibits delayed slope reversal at a fixed dose, on an $O(1/η)$ timescale as pathway mismatch $η$ vanishes. At one fixed joint fit, validated bounds establish decreasing cumulative output across 20-100 ng nominal burden, from zero to full target loading, at every positive finite observation time for a translation-blocking model and an RNA-decay model. Full loading at 20 ng reduces 48-hour cumulative output by 13.35% and 10.18%, respectively, while endpoint concentration in the first model changes by only +0.15%. Preserved ordering therefore does not ensure quantitative agreement.

papers.title: Construction and regularity of lump solutions of the modified KP-I equation
papers.abstract: We express the $τ$-functions of standard and higher-order lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I (mKP-I) equation as Gram determinants in integral form. Unlike the KP-I equation, the mKP-I $τ$-function is complex-valued, and its nonvanishing does not follow from the positive definiteness of a Hermitian Gram matrix. We derive explicit spectral conditions for the regularity of these solutions; for higher-order lumps, the sharp condition depends only on the spectral parameter and the largest entry of the index vector. We also prove that the lump solutions and all their spatial derivatives decay algebraically in every spatial direction, uniformly on compact time intervals.

papers.title: Structured Design of Layered Sparse Unitary Space-Time Modulation for Integrated Noncoherent and Coherent MIMO Communications
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel structured constellation design based on unitary space-time modulation (USTM) for integrated noncoherent and coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Information is encoded into the sparse space-time matrices through two layers: a noncoherent layer that distinguishes points on the Grassmann manifold (subspaces) and a coherent layer that distinguishes among the Stiefel representatives associated with each of those points (bases for the subspaces). We consider sequential decoding of the two layers to reduce computational complexity, while explicitly identifying the matrix structures that favor this decoding strategy. The proposed constellation builds on a previous structured Grassmannian signaling design, which has the remarkable property of producing space-time matrices with a single nonzero entry per row, while introducing a novel systematic design for the second layer corresponding to the Stiefel representatives. The design of the second layer preserves the sparsity of the first layer and significantly reduces the decoding computational complexity, while ensuring reliable performance under sequential decoding and enabling a simple yet effective bit labeling, as validated by numerical results in terms of bit error rate (BER) and symbol error rate (SER). Numerical results also show graceful performance degradation under channel correlation and, for limited coherence intervals where channel state information at the receiver (CSIR) can be estimated only imperfectly, improved performance compared with classical space-time block coding (STBC) schemes based on QAM and PSK.

papers.title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
papers.abstract: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate.
