The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. The method is applied to a two-level model of a polar dye in three different solvents: chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide, each differing in polarity and dielectric relaxation time. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are obtained from dipole-dipole correlation functions, capturing the solvent-induced spectral broadening, the dynamic Stokes shift, and the time evolution of the emission bandwidth. The calculated solvent spectral response agrees well with the experimental relaxation trends of the three solvents.

papers.title: Greedy Empirical Bayes for Density Estimation
papers.abstract: Bayesian nonparametric density estimation is challenging in high dimensions, where traditional approaches like the Dirichlet process (DP) mixture rely on computationally intensive Markov chain Monte Carlo or approximations. We introduce the partition posterior bootstrap (PPB), where a flexible prior is constructed by smoothing a DP over a partition of the sample space. Conditioned on this partition, exact posterior sampling reduces to a simple Bayesian bootstrap-like algorithm. Importantly, we select the partition using a greedy empirical Bayes (GEB) algorithm which scales to high dimensions and large sample sizes. GEB greedily maximizes the closed-form marginal likelihood via local split decisions arising naturally from its factorization, yielding an adaptive binary tree partition. Our key theoretical result is that the GEB tree belongs to an admissible family with high probability, splitting all identifiable signals while avoiding over-splitting noise. As a result, the PPB posterior with the GEB tree attains adaptive contraction rates. Our theory holds under weak, verifiable assumptions, which we demonstrate in numerous examples. Empirically, PPB delivers accurate density estimates and uncertainty quantification at a fraction of the computational cost of other approaches, making it a practical off-the-shelf choice for high-dimensional Bayesian density estimation with theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Pluggable Subband-Decoupled Fusion and Unlabeled Capture Prototype Calibration: Bridging High-SNR Null-Subcarrier Regrowth and Low-SNR Coherent Preambles for Cross-Domain IoT RF Fingerprinting
papers.abstract: Zero-overhead physical-layer authentication at edge wireless access points (APs) is vital for securing resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) transceivers against credential cloning, yet cross-domain IEEE 802.11a/g radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) faces an acute signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) crossover. Power-amplifier spectral regrowth on unpopulated null subcarriers resists indoor multipath at high SNR but decays quadratically below the thermal noise floor, whereas populated active in-band preambles survive low SNR yet degrade under severe multipath, causing static fusion to lose up to 44.7 percentage points (pp). To our knowledge, we propose the first RFFI framework that dynamically modulates active in-band waveforms and unpopulated null-subcarrier regrowth via a blind physical SNR gate: Pluggable Gated Subband-Decoupled Fusion with Unlabeled Capture-Aware Prototype Calibration (GSDF-CAPC). Avoiding the 20-35 dB subband gradient imbalance of joint training, GSDF pairs any frozen pretrained host backbone with a 46.3K null-subcarrier plug-in encoder (NS-Branch), fusing scale-standardized logits and gate-warped spherical embeddings under a source-calibrated lag-64 thermal-SNR gate with exact low-SNR fallback. Over unlabeled target AP captures, forward-only unbalanced optimal-transport calibration (UOT-CAPC) aligns shifted prototypes under packet-arrival skew and recovers parameter-free balanced Sinkhorn (U-CAPC) at equipartition. Across DataPort-WiFi, WiSig, and ORBIT MobRFFI, zero-retrain GSDF wins all 72/72 paired runs across eight backbones with 0.00 pp low-SNR loss, while edge IB-Host + GSDF (92.6K-93.3K active parameters, 1.82 ms single-core CPU latency) and timing-synchronized GSDF-STO / GSDF-Tri reach 57.50%-65.05% three-benchmark Macro-F1 (89.04%-100.00% over 5-10-packet IoT bursts).

papers.title: blaris: Windowless Random-Access LZSS for Constrained Microcontrollers
papers.abstract: Embedded LZ77 decompressors (such as heatshrink and tamp) require an in-RAM sliding window that couples memory usage to compression ratio and incurs high latency on random-access reads. We present blaris, a lightweight, windowless LZSS decompressor for execute-in-place (XIP) random access on constrained microcontrollers. By partitioning tokens into bidirectionally traversable streams with power-of-two checkpoints, blaris resolves back-references directly in the compressed payload, achieving compression ratios comparable to high-window heatshrink and tamp configurations without allocating a RAM window. Targeting compress-on-host, decompress-on-device workflows, blaris assumes trusted build-time payloads and omits runtime error and bounds checks. On RV32IMC, it requires just 548-784 B of Flash and 104-112 B of total RAM, achieving orders-of-magnitude faster small-slice random reads than ratio-matched, block-indexed heatshrink and tamp.
papers.comments: 4 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Source code and benchmark suite available at https://github.com/lis05/blaris

papers.title: Optimising Recruitment and Sample Allocation in Multi-Site Rare Disease Studies
papers.abstract: Clinical research in rare diseases is challenged by the limited availability and broad geographical distribution of eligible patients. This necessitates multi-centre collaboration and strategic selection of analytical laboratories based on capacity, cost, and capability. We present a mathematical framework based on cardinality optimisation to support key operational decisions in study design, balancing clinical relevance, feasibility, budgetary constraints, and logistical factors. The framework was implemented in the Reconstruction and Computational Modelling for Inherited Metabolic Diseases (Recon4IMD) project, aiming to recruit 1,900 diagnosed patients across 24 healthcare centres and eight metabolomic laboratories. Compared to both proportional heuristic and greedy marginal allocation baselines, the proposed optimisation model consistently achieved higher recruitment yields in simulated multi-centre scenarios and reduced metabolomic analysis costs by approximately 30% under unconstrained conditions. Notably, both the heuristic and greedy allocation baselines became infeasible under progressively tighter laboratory capacity constraints, whereas the optimised model maintained feasibility and cost control. These findings highlight the value of integrated optimisation strategies for improving recruitment, platform selection, and sample allocation in complex, resource-limited research settings.

papers.title: Entanglement cost and classical capacity of multimode Gaussian states and channels
papers.abstract: Gaussian states and operations are central to continuous-variable quantum information and communication. For systems with any finite number of modes, we prove that entanglement of formation, Gaussian entanglement of formation, and entanglement cost coincide for every finite-energy bipartite Gaussian state. Their common value is strongly superadditive and lower-bounds entanglement of formation and entanglement cost for arbitrary non-Gaussian states with the same covariance matrix. We then determine the entanglement cost of every multimode Gaussian channel as well as its classical capacity under a mean energy constraint. These quantities reduce to Gaussian covariance optimizations, and the capacity is attained by pure Gaussian signals with Gaussian displacement modulation, independently across channel uses. The proof combines geodesic convexity of entanglement for pure Gaussian states with a relative-entropy inequality for arbitrary states. We also obtain a closed formula for the entanglement cost of a family of four-mode bound entangled states.

papers.title: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries
papers.abstract: We introduce non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving quantum channels that are dualizable and pure. This provides an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries of quantum lattice systems, formulated in terms of their action on local operators. Focusing on quantum spin chains, we motivate these defining conditions and conjecture that every such quantum channel admits a realization by dualizable topological defects or, equivalently, by dualizable sequential quantum circuits. We construct a broad class of examples, including on-site non-invertible symmetries that are anomalous, as well as higher-dimensional examples. In Part II of this work, we reconstruct topological defects whose boundary algebras yield an index theory that classifies non-invertible QCAs up to blend equivalence.

papers.title: Binary Affine Optimization with Nearly-Graphic Constraint Matrices
papers.abstract: We present a polynomial-time algorithm for binary affine optimization with a linear objective when every column of the constraint matrix has Hamming weight at most 2, and prove that the problem is NP-hard when every column of the constraint matrix has Hamming weight exactly 3. We obtain fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms for the unrestricted problem provided that a nearly-graphic certificate is given, where the certificate roughly measures how far the constraint matrix is from having columns of Hamming weight at most 2. We apply our FPT algorithm to Max-Lin$_2$ on graphs and obtain FPT algorithms parameterized by the contraction distance and contraction rank of the graph, utilizing the concept of Eulerian-spanning set. In the case of contraction distance, another FPT algorithm can be used to find the corresponding certificate; that is, we obtain an FPT algorithm that requires no information beyond the problem instance itself.

papers.title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'. We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.

papers.title: Long-Term Quantile Treatment Effects with Combined Experimental and Observational Data
papers.abstract: This paper studies the identification, estimation, and inference of long-term quantile treatment effects (LTQTEs) when short-term experimental data are supplemented with long-term observational data. Under a latent unconfoundedness framework, we establish identification of the LTQTE curve and derive the corresponding efficient influence functions. Building on these influence functions, we propose a semiparametrically efficient estimation procedure and develop a multiplier bootstrap method for uniform inference on the LTQTE curve, yielding valid simultaneous confidence bands over a continuum of quantile indices.

papers.title: On the recursive feasibility and stability of MPC without terminal constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze stability and recursive feasibility of a model predictive control (MPC) scheme that does not rely on terminal ingredients -- such as terminal constraints or a terminal cost based on a terminal controller. In the proposed formulation, we augment the cost function by a weighted finite tail which is optimized online, and we show it plays the role of a stabilizing terminal cost. Under a relaxed, local dynamic programming condition on the tail, we certify a family of regions -- parameterized by the tail's weight coefficient -- on which the problem is recursively feasible and the origin is asymptotically stable. These regions are larger as the weight increases: in particular, we show that any state that can be steered within the control horizon to a predefined neighborhood of the origin is contained in a certified region for a sufficiently large weight. Finally, we characterize the closed-loop performance over the certified region, bounding the suboptimality of the closed loop with respect to the infinite-horizon optimal cost. We conclude the discussion by illustrating these results on a simple numerical example.

papers.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.

papers.title: Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution. We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker parameters. Notably, our result also holds for distributions whose marginals are "locally independent" and "approximately identically" distributed. It is not known whether such distributions fool general DNFs, which makes the derandomization via DNF-fooling techniques unavailable. Our proof of this derandomization is via the method of moments, which might be of independent interest. We apply this result to obtain improved separations between non-monotone arithmetic circuits and the radical of monotone circuits. Specifically, we construct an explicit family of multilinear polynomials $P_n$ that have small non-monotone arithmetic circuits such that any power of $P_n$ cannot be computed by monotone arithmetic circuits of sub-exponential size. This improves on a recent result of Cavalar, Fabris, Mukhopadhyay, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff (STOC 2026), who proved a non-explicit separation that was quasipolynomial. Our construction uses Nisan-Wigderson designs with an additional linear-algebraic expansion property.

papers.title: Dynamics-preserving graph sparsification
papers.abstract: Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes. We first study linear diffusion, where node values evolve according to the graph Laplacian. The dominant network sparsification method, effective resistance sampling, preserves all Laplacian eigenvalues within a uniform multiplicative bound. We show that with a limited edge budget, this is dynamically inefficient: diffusion is dominated by the slowest-decaying modes, so enforcing a uniform guarantee spends edges on fast modes that barely affect long-term dynamics. Based on this observation, we derive Diffusion Spectral Error (DSE), which evaluates in closed form the typical error in trajectories between the original and sparsified graphs over random initial conditions. Minimizing this error, which naturally prioritizes slow modes, yields sparse networks explicitly designed to preserve dynamics. At the same sparsification levels, DSE sparsification often preserves diffusion dynamics with several-fold lower error than effective resistance sampling, and up to two orders of magnitude lower on strongly modular networks. Although derived in a linear context, we empirically find that DSE sparsification gives similar improvements in the Kuramoto model (a nonlinear system of coupled oscillators), where DSE sparsification approximately preserves the synchronization threshold and, at strong coupling, order-parameter trajectories.

papers.title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
papers.abstract: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors. From lattices constructed using ternary quadratic-residue codes, we obtain an infinite family with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(p+1,p+1)$ for primes $p\ge71$ with $p\equiv23\pmod{24}$. From Barnes-Wall lattices, we obtain an infinite family with gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(2^m,2^m)$ for odd $m\ge7$. We also obtain two additional examples, with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(48,48)$ and gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(512,512)$.

papers.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras
papers.abstract: In 1990, Kantor introduced the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e., bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. In the case $n>1$, the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any of the well-known classes of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). We describe the algebra of all derivations of $W(2)$ and the subalgebras of $W(2)$ of codimension one. We also study similar problems for the algebra $W_2$ of all commutative algebras on the two-dimensional vector space and the algebra $S_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace-zero multiplication on the two-dimensional space.
papers.journal_ref: I. Kaygorodov, A. Lopatin, and Yu. Popov, Conservative algebras of 2-dimensional algebras, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 486 (2015), 255--274

papers.title: On The Kantor Product
papers.abstract: We study the algebra of bilinear multiplications of an n-dimensional vector space. In particular, we study the Kantor product of some well-known multiplications (associative, Lie, alternative, Novikov, and some others).
papers.journal_ref: I. Kaygorodov, On the Kantor product, Journal of Algebra and its Applications, 16 (2017), no. 9, 1750167

papers.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, II
papers.abstract: In 1990, Kantor defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e., bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). We describe automorphisms, one-sided ideals, and idempotents of $W(2)$. Similar problems are also solved for the algebra $W_2$ of all commutative algebras on the $2$-dimensional vector space and for the algebra $S_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace-zero multiplication on the $2$-dimensional vector space.
papers.journal_ref: I. Kaygorodov, Yu. Volkov, Conservative algebras of 2-dimensional algebras, II, Communications in Algebra, 45 (2017), no. 8, 3413--3421

papers.title: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
papers.abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.
papers.comments: 59 pages. v3: Part 1 has been edited; Part 2 consists of clarifications of statements

papers.title: The universal conservative superalgebra
papers.abstract: We introduce the class of conservative superalgebras, in particular, the superalgebra $\mathcal{U}(V)$ of bilinear operations on a superspace $V$. Moreover, we show that each conservative superalgebra modulo its maximal Jacobi ideal is embedded into $\mathcal{U}(V)$ for a certain superspace $V$.
papers.journal_ref: I. Kaygorodov, Yu. Popov, and A. Pozhidaev, The universal conservative superalgebra, Communications in Algebra, 47 (2019), no. 10, 4066--4076

papers.title: Long time decay for global solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in the critical Sobolev--Gevrey space $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$, $a>0$. We first prove local well-posedness, together with a global existence criterion and a blow-up criterion for the maximal solution. Our main result is that every global solution $u\in C\big([0,+\infty),\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)\big)$ satisfies $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}}\to0$ as $t\to+\infty$. The proof combines the classical decay of global solutions in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ with an analyticity estimate for small data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ and Fourier-analytic product laws in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces. As consequences, we obtain the decay rate $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^s}=o\big(t^{-\frac{s-1/2}{2}}\big)$ for every $s\ge\frac12$, and the stability of global solutions under small perturbations of the initial data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}$.

papers.title: An application of "Selmer group Chabauty" to arithmetic dynamics
papers.abstract: We describe how one can use the "Selmer group Chabauty" method developed by the author to show that certain hyperelliptic curves of the form $$ C \colon y^2 = x^{2g+1} + h(x)^2 \,, $$ with $h \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $\operatorname{deg} h \le g$ and $h(0)$ is odd, have only the "obvious" rational points $\infty$ (the unique point at infinity on the smooth projective model of the curve) and $(0, \pm h(0))$. Let $c \in \mathbb{Q}$ and write $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$. We denote the iterates of $f_c$ by $f_c^{\circ n}$; i.e., we set $f_c^{\circ 0}(x) = x$ and $f_c^{\circ(n+1)}(x) = f_c(f_c^{\circ n}(x))$. As an application of the method, we prove that if $f_c^{\circ 2}$ is irreducible, then $f_c^{\circ 6}$ is also irreducible. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), it also follows that $f_c^{\circ 10}$ is irreducible.
papers.comments: 17 pages. v2: added reference to Magma code implementing the algorithm from Section 2 and verifying the computations in Section 3. v3 fixes a gap (assumption (A3) needed to be strengthened) and adapts the paper to the fix (the results in Section 3 are not affected, but the statistics in Section 4 get slightly worse), plus a bunch of further minor fixes

papers.title: Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
papers.abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.
papers.comments: One of the announced result is false

papers.title: Multiply Robust Causal Mediation Analysis with Continuous Treatments
papers.abstract: In many applications, researchers are interested in the direct and indirect causal effects of a treatment or exposure on an outcome of interest. Mediation analysis offers a rigorous framework for identifying and estimating these causal effects. For binary treatments, efficient estimators for the direct and indirect effects are presented by Tchetgen Tchetgen and Shpitser (2012) based on the influence function of the parameter of interest. These estimators possess desirable properties such as multiple-robustness and asymptotic normality while allowing for slower than root-n rates of convergence for the nuisance parameters. However, in settings involving continuous treatments, these influence function-based estimators are not readily applicable without making strong parametric assumptions. In this work, utilizing a kernel smoothing approach, we propose an estimator suitable for settings with continuous treatments inspired by the influence function-based estimation strategy. Our proposed approach employs cross-fitting, relaxing the smoothness requirements on the nuisance functions and allowing them to be estimated at slower rates than the target parameter. Additionally, similar to influence function-based estimators, our proposed estimator is multiply robust and asymptotically normal, allowing for inference in settings where parametric assumptions may not be justified.

papers.title: On the Kantor product, II
papers.abstract: We describe the Kantor square (and Kantor product) of multiplications, extending the classification proposed in [I. Kaygorodov, On the Kantor product, Journal of Algebra and Its Applications, 16 (2017), 9, 1750167]. Besides, we explicitly describe the Kantor square of some low dimensional algebras and give constructive methods for obtaining new transposed Poisson algebras and Poisson-Novikov algebras; and for classifying Poisson structures and commutative post-Lie structures on a given algebra.
papers.journal_ref: R.~Fehlberg Júnior, I.~Kaygorodov, On the Kantor product, II, Carpathian Mathematical Publications, 14 (2022), no.~2, 543--563

papers.title: Greatest Common Divisors and an Unlikely Intersection Type Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove inequalities involving greatest common divisors of functions at integral points with respect to numerically parallel divisors, generalizing a result of Wang and Yasufuku (after work of Bugeaud-Corvaja-Zannier, Corvaja-Zannier, and the second author). In addition to proving results in a broader context than previously considered, we also study the exceptional set in this setting, for both the counting function and the proximity function. Based on our study of exceptional sets, we propose new conjectures connected to the topic of unlikely intersections. We prove special cases of the conjectures on abelian varieties and the algebraic torus, including a completely explicit result in the former case, and provide a link between the conjectures and exceptional sets for inequalities involving greatest common divisors.

papers.title: Scattering in the planar restricted $(N+1)$-body problem
papers.abstract: In the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem, as time goes to positive or negative infinity the massless body has four possible final motions: hyperbolic, parabolic, oscillatory and bounded. In the hyperbolic case, the massless body comes from or goes to infinity with a non-zero limiting energy and a limiting direction, and in the parabolic case, it comes from or goes to infinity with a zero limiting energy and possibly a limiting direction. In this paper we study scattering orbits that come from infinity and then go to infinity. It will be proven that for the planar restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with the motions of the primaries being collision-free and periodic, for any two given asymptotic directions, there exists at least one hyperbolic scattering orbit for any positive limiting energy and one parabolic scattering orbit. The orbits are either always collision-free or regularizable with one collision.
papers.comments: 19 pages. The previous version of the paper contains a gap in the proof of a key lemma. This new version is revised based on a recent result in https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22849. The main results now include both hyperbolic and parabolic scattering orbits by adapting recently developed techniques

papers.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, IV
papers.abstract: The notion of conservative algebras appeared in a paper by Kantor in 1972. Later, he defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). It looks like $W(n)$ in the theory of conservative algebras plays a similar role to the role of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the theory of Lie algebras. Namely, an arbitrary conservative algebra can be obtained from a universal algebra $W(n)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ The present paper is a part of a series of papers, dedicated to the study of the algebra $W(2)$ and its principal subalgebras.
papers.journal_ref: A. Fernández Ouaridi, I. Kaygorodov, C. Martín González, Conservative algebras of 2-dimensional algebras, IV, Journal of Algebra and its Applications, 24 (2025), no. 6, 2550143

papers.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, V
papers.abstract: The notion of conservative algebras appeared in a paper by Kantor in 1972. Later, he defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). It looks like $W(n)$ in the theory of conservative algebras plays a similar role to the role of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the theory of Lie algebras. Namely, an arbitrary conservative algebra can be obtained from a universal algebra $W(n)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ The present paper is a part of a series of papers, which dedicated to the study of the algebra $W(2)$ and its principal subalgebras.
papers.journal_ref: I.~Kaygorodov, D.~Martín Barquero, C.~Martín González, Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, V, Siberian Electronic Mathematical Reports, 22 (2025), no.~1, 587--620

papers.title: Adaptive mesh refinement for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
papers.abstract: We propose a new adaptive algorithm for the approximation of the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation via a higher-order tangent plane scheme. We show that the adaptive approximation satisfies an energy inequality and demonstrate numerically that the adaptive algorithm outperforms uniform approaches.

papers.title: A variational Free Boundary Ricci flow on Surfaces with Boundary
papers.abstract: We study a Ricci flow on a compact surface with boundary arising as the L2-gradient flow of the Liouville functional with its natural Neumann boundary condition. Geometrically, this boundary condition preserves the geodesic-curvature density H dσ. In the regime in which the total scalar curvature satisfies 0 < C_0 < 4π, a scale invariant normalised Liouville functional is monotone, and bounded below. In our first result, we use its dissipation to show that every compact blow-up limit is homothetically shrinking with constant positive scalar curvature. We then treat a rotationally symmetric disc with H_0 > 0 and C_0 > 0, in which case every noncompact limit is ruled out via singularity analysis and a noncollapsing theorem. Consequently, the normalised flow fully converges smoothly to the unique spherical cap determined by the initial area and the preserved boundary data, yielding our second result. Additionally, we also study the regime in which C0 is nonpositive. In this case standard PDE arguments prove full smooth convergence of the normalised flow towards a metric with constant nonpositive scalar curvature.

papers.title: Joint Communication and Control: Causal Coordination Coding for Witsenhausen Counterexample
papers.abstract: In decentralized network control, communication plays a crucial role by transforming local observations into shared knowledge, enabling agents to coordinate their actions. This paper investigates how communication facilitates cooperation behavior and therefore improves the overall performance in Witsenhausen counterexample, a canonical toy problem in distributed decision-making. We consider the vector-valued setups where the encoder, i.e., the first decision-maker (DM) acts causally and the decoder, i.e., the second DM, operates noncausally, 1) without and 2) with access to channel feedback. Using a coordination coding framework, we characterize the achievable power-estimation cost regions in single-letter expressions for both scenarios. We show that feedback enlarges the coordination region compared with the no-feedback setup. Building on the characterization of the power-estimation cost region, we propose a hybrid strategy that combines discrete quantization with a continuous Gaussian codebook, the Zero Estimation Cost (ZEC) strategy. This strategy uses coding tools that allow perfect reconstruction of the target symbols, leading to an asymptotic estimation cost equal to zero, while substantially reducing the power cost. Moreover, when channel feedback is available, we propose an analogous ZEC strategy that simultaneously achieves zero power and zero estimation costs in the low-noise regime. Finally, we establish that, when restricted to jointly Gaussian random variables, the performance is identical across all setups featuring at least one causal DM, regardless of the presence of feedback information.
papers.comments: Published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. Date of publication: 12 October 2026

papers.title: A one-dimensional model of catheter aspiration in blood vessels
papers.abstract: Aspiration thrombectomy is a primary endovascular treatment option for acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusions, in which a catheter is navigated to the occlusion site and suction is applied to remove the thrombus. This work introduces a reduced one-dimensional model for aspiration in blood vessels that accounts for the elasticity of both the vessel wall and the catheter. The inclusion of vessel wall visco-elasticity transforms the governing equation for the flow rate into a parabolic form, enabling an accurate resolution of the diffuse pressure gradients near the catheter tip observed in CFD simulations. The numerical treatment is based on a relaxation of the hyperbolic subsystem that facilitates nodal solvers, enabling efficient coupling between catheterized and uncatheterized vessel segments, including bifurcations and the catheter tip. A splitting strategy ensures that the visco-elastic terms incur only negligible additional computational cost relative to the purely hyperbolic model. The model is benchmarked against three-dimensional CFD simulations and reference data from the literature. Numerical experiments investigating the role of catheter elasticity and suction force on the hemodynamics are presented, and an uncertainty quantification study demonstrates the suitability of the framework for efficient parameter studies. The results indicate that the proposed model resolves blood flow comparably accurate to three-dimensional simulations at a fraction of the computational cost. While further in vitro and in vivo validation is required, the framework represents a promising step toward computationally efficient preoperative planning and uncertainty-aware decision support in aspiration thrombectomy.

papers.title: Absence of ground states for anions
papers.abstract: We show that the $N$-electron Hamiltonian $H(N, Z)$ with the total nuclear charge $Z$ has no normalizable ground state if the ground state energy $E(N, Z)$ satisfies $E(N, Z)= E(N-1, Z)$ for $Z=N-1$. For anions $\mathrm{He}^-, \mathrm{Be}^-, \mathrm{N}^-, \mathrm{Ne}^-$, etc., many numerical results give strong evidence of the condition $E(N, Z)= E(N-1, Z)$.
papers.comments: The author has found a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1, which is needed for the main theorem

papers.title: On non-isomorphic universal sofic groups
papers.abstract: We show that there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ non-isomorphic universal sofic groups. This proves a conjecture of Simon Thomas.

papers.title: On completed homology and a conjecture of Venkatesh
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a CM field and $Π$ a regular algebraic cuspidal cohomological representation of $\mathbf{G}=\operatorname{PGL}_2/F$. A conjecture of Venkatesh describes the structure of the contribution of $Π$ to the homology of the locally symmetric spaces associated to $\mathbf{G}$. We investigate this conjecture in the setting of $p$-adic homology with $p$ a totally split prime. Along the way, we elaborate on the relations between Venkatesh's conjecture and completed homology, the Taylor-Wiles method and the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence. Our main result is a `big $R=T$' theorem in characteristic 0, from which we deduce a variant of the $p$-adic realisation of Venkatesh's conjecture, conditional on various natural conjectures and technical assumptions.
papers.comments: Improved exposition and typesetting from earlier version. 30 pages

papers.title: Exploiting the nonzero diagonal pattern in matrix function computations
papers.abstract: We consider the task of approximating a matrix function $f(A)$, where $A$ is a matrix in which only a relatively small number of (not necessarily consecutive) sub- and superdiagonals contain nonzero entries. Approximating $f$ by a low-degree polynomial $p$ allows us to obtain sparse approximations to $f(A)$, which one can efficiently work with (while, in general, $f(A)$ is a dense matrix, even when $A$ is sparse). Our approach is based on carefully inspecting the locations where nonzeros can occur in $p(A)$, and identifying the entries in $A$ that influence them. In particular, we illustrate how this approach can be used for efficiently approximating the trace of $f(A)$ and identify how this approach is related to established (stochastic) probing methods for trace estimation. Another application area in which our approach works particularly well is the computation of functions of Toeplitz matrices. Here, studying the sparsity pattern of $p(A)$ allows us to reduce the computation of the whole matrix polynomial to that of a single small-scale submatrix, yielding an algorithm that scales exceptionally well to large problem sizes.

papers.title: Picard Groups of Spectral Varieties and Moduli of Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of Higgs sheaves valued in line bundles and the associated Hitchin maps on surfaces. We first work out Picard groups of generic (very general) spectral varieties which holds for dimension of at least 2, i.e., a Noether--Lefschetz type theorem for spectral varieties. We then apply these Picard-group calculations to obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the non-emptiness of generic Hitchin fibers in the range where the spectral Noether--Lefschetz theorem applies. Then we move on to detect the geometry of the moduli spaces of Higgs sheaves as the second Chern class varies.
papers.comments: 37 pages. We have clarified the hypotheses of the spectral Noether-Lefschetz theorem and the scope of the nonemptiness criterion for generic Hitchin fibers. We have also revised the proofs of generic smoothness of the Hitchin map and of the connectedness result in rank two. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: A Classification Theorem on Non-compact Embeddings between Besov Spaces
papers.abstract: We analyze the embedding properties between Besov spaces, defined on the total space $\mathbb R^n$ and on bounded domains. We give a complete classification on whether or not these embedding maps satisfy certain weaker forms of compactness characterized by the so-called strictly and finitely strictly singular conditions. The result extends the recent findings on Sobolev embeddings by offering a refined description of the quality of non-compactness in the setting of Besov spaces.
papers.comments: Final version, 16 pages. Published in Mathematische Annalen
papers.journal_ref: Math. Ann. 396 (2026), no. 4, Paper No. 76, MR 5154984

papers.title: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
papers.abstract: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $ω$-ASD connections (where $ω$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

papers.title: Remarks on nonlinear dispersive PDEs with rough dispersion management
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Cauchy problem for a class of dispersive PDEs where a rough time coefficient is present in front of the dispersion. Under minimal assumptions on the occupation measure of this coefficient, we show that for the large class of semilinear dispersive PDEs whose well-posedness theory relies on linear estimates of Strichartz or local smoothing type, one has the same well-posedness theory with or without the modulation. We also show a regularization by noise type of phenomenon for rough modulations, namely, large data global well-posedness in the focusing mass-critical case for the modulated equation. Under rougher assumptions on the modulation, we show that one can also transfer the well-posedness theory based on multilinear Fourier analysis from the original dispersive PDE to the modulated one. In the case of the NLS equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbb{T}^d$, this covers all the sub-critical and critical regularities, thus completing and extending the various results currently available in the literature. At last, in the case of the periodic Wick-ordered cubic NLS, we show an even stronger form of regularization by noise, namely well-posedness in the critical Fourier-Lebesgue space for rough modulations.
papers.comments: The proof of Theorem 1.4 has been corrected for the local well-posedness, and a globalization argument has been added. Appendix A has also been added to discuss the case where the occupation measure is no longer absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. 54p

papers.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
papers.abstract: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.
papers.comments: 52 pages. To appear: Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal

papers.title: Cohomological VC-density: Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: The concept of Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) density is pivotal across various mathematical fields, including discrete geometry, probability theory and model theory. In this paper, we introduce a topological generalization of VC-density. Let $Y$ be a topological space and $\mathcal{X}$ a family of closed subspaces of $Y$. For each $p \geq 0$, we define a number, $\mathrm{vcd}^{p}_{\mathcal{X}}$, which we refer to as the degree $p$ VC-density of the family $\mathcal{X}$. The classical notion of VC-density within this topological framework can be recovered by setting $p=0$. Our definition of degree $p$ VC-density extends to higher orders as well. For $p \geq 0$, $q \geq 1$, we define the degree $p$, order $q$ VC density $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$ of $\mathcal{X}$, which recovers Shelah's notion of higher order VC-density for $q$-dependent families when $p=0$. Our definition introduces a completely new notion when $p > 0$. We examine the properties of $\mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p$ (as well as $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$) when the families $\mathcal{X}$ are definable in structures with some underlying topology (for instance, the Euclidean topology for o-minimal structures over $\mathbb{R}$, the analytic topology over $\mathbb{C}$, or the étale site for schemes over arbitrary algebraically closed fields). Our main result establishes that in any model of these theories \[ \mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p \leq (p+1) \dim X, \] and more generally for any $q \geq 1$ \[ \mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}} \leq (p+q) \dim X. \] We give examples to show that our bounds are optimal. We also present combinatorial applications of our higher-degree VC-density bounds, deriving higher degree topological analogs of well-known results such as the existence of $\varepsilon$-nets and the fractional Helly theorem.

papers.title: On loops in the complement of dimers
papers.abstract: We consider ergodic translation-invariant Gibbs measures for the dimer model (i.e. perfect matchings) on the hexagonal lattice. The complement of a dimer configuration is a fully-packed loop configuration: each vertex has degree two. This is also known as the loop $O(1)$ model at $x=\infty$. We show that, if the measure is non-frozen, then it exhibits either infinitely many loops around every face or a unique bi-infinite path. Our main tool is the flip (or XOR) operation: if a hexagon contains exactly three dimers, one can replace them by the other three edges. Classical results in dimer theory imply that such hexagons appear with a positive density. To some extent, this replaces the finite-energy property and allows to make use of tools from the percolation theory, in particular the Burton--Keane argument, to exclude existence of more than one bi-infinite path.
papers.journal_ref: Electronic Journal of Probability 31 (2026) 1-26

papers.title: On the Algebraic Independence of $E$- and $G$-Functions, I: A $p$-adic Criterion
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and let $f_1(z),\ldots, f_m(z) \in K[[z]]$ be power series such that, for every $1 \leq i \leq m$, $f_i(z)$ is a solution to a differential operator $\mathcal{L}_i \in E_p[\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}z]$, where $E_p$ denotes the field of analytic elements. Suppose that $K$ is totally ramified over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and that for every $1 \leq i \leq m$, the operator $\mathcal{L}_i$ has a strong Frobenius structure and satisfies the maximal order multiplicity (MOM) condition at zero. Under these assumptions, we show that $f_1(z),\ldots, f_m(z)$ are algebraically dependent over $E_p$ if and only if there exist integers $a_1,\ldots, a_m$, not all zero, such that $f_1(z)^{a_1} \cdots f_m(z)^{a_m} \in E_p.$ The main consequence of this result is that it provides a general criterion for studying the algebraic independence of a broad class of $G$-functions and certain $E$-functions over the field of analytic elements.

papers.title: Exponential mixing for equilibrium states of time changes of hyperbolic geodesic flows
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic manifold of dimension $n\ge2$, let $ψ$ be a smooth positive function on its unit tangent bundle $SM$, and let $f^t_ψ$ be the time change of the geodesic flow with speed $1/ψ$. We prove that $f^t_ψ$ is exponentially mixing, for Hölder observables, with respect to the equilibrium state of every Hölder potential, as asked by Bowen and Ruelle. This includes the smooth invariant measure and the measure of maximal entropy. The proof runs Dolgopyat's cancellation argument at a variable \emph{local frequency} $Λ_b=|b|(1+\|\bY_b\|)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:localfreq}): the scale $1/|b|$ is replaced by a scale that depends on the point, as in the work of Tsujii and Zhang in dimension three, and the argument runs without a smooth contact structure and without $C^1$ strong foliations. Many of the techniques, in particular the reduction to an expanding semiflow by quotienting along the stable foliation, are inspired by the earlier work of Butterley and War \cite{BW20}.

papers.title: A Bourgain-Gromov problem on non-compact Sobolev-Lorentz embeddings
papers.abstract: We study the non-compact Sobolev embeddings into the optimal scale of Lorentz spaces, $W_0^mL^{p,q}(Ω) \to L^{\frac{dp}{d - mp},r}(Ω)$, where $Ω\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $1 \leq m < d$, $0<q<r\le\infty$ with $1<p<\frac dm$ or $p=q=1$. We show that these embeddings are finitely strictly singular with certain upper bounds on the decay rate of the Bernstein numbers. We reduce the Sobolev embeddings to embeddings of Besov spaces and sequence spaces, which simplifies the previous methods by Bourgain-Gromov and Lang-Mihula.
papers.comments: Final version, 6 pages. Published in Constructive Approximation

papers.title: Complexity Framework For Forbidden Subgraphs V: Beyond Simple Graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate how allowing self-loops and multi-edges (i.e. moving from simple graphs to pseudographs) impacts the complexity of graph problems on finitely defined monotone graph classes. We do this by extending the C123-framework beyond simple graphs. We use several testbed problems to illustrate some of the new and varied behaviours introduced by the transition to pseudographs. We show that Pseudograph Matching Cut and Pseudograph d-Cut are C123-problems. Consequently, for every finite set HH of simple graphs, we obtain a complete complexity classification for these problems on HH-subgraph-free graphs. This sharply contrasts with their simple-graph counterparts, which are not C123-problems and their complexity remains open even for classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph H. We also show that Pseudograph Stable Cut is not a C123-problem. Nevertheless, for graph classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph, the problem mirrors the C123 classification; this correspondence already fails for sets of size 2. This gives the first example of a problem that aligns with C123-problems for a single forbidden subgraph but not for larger sets. Motivated by the interpretation of Stable Cut as a surjective homomorphism to a partially reflexive path, we also study surjective homomorphisms to partially reflexive cycles on k vertices with one irreflexive vertex. These problems share structural similarities with Pseudograph Stable Cut. We prove that for k at least 6, they are NP-complete on triangle-free pseudographs. However, unlike Pseudograph Stable Cut, they are polynomial-time solvable on all graph classes with bounded-degree.

papers.title: A remark on the reach and upper bounds on some extrinsic geometry invariants of submanifolds
papers.abstract: We consider a compact submanifold $M$ of a Riemannian manifold $N$ and we use the second variation formula as a tool to drive some geometric results on reach$(M, N)$ the reach of $M$ in $N$, including some useful relations between the extrinsic geometry of $M$ in $N$ and reach$(M, N)$. Our results generalize some theorems previously proved for the special case where $N$ is Euclidean space.
papers.comments: The paper is withdrawn because errors have been identified in some of the proofs. The validity of the main results requires further investigation.

papers.title: Lifting canonical divisors of the form $2G-D$ in towers of function fields
papers.abstract: We present a method for constructing, given a canonical divisor in a function field of the form $2G-D$, another canonical divisor of the form $2G'-D'$ in an extension of the function field that satisfies certain ramification conditions. This method applies in particular to certain recursive towers that yield sequences of canonical divisors of the form $2G_i-D_i$ for each index $i\geq 0$. Using these divisors, we construct sequences of iso-dual AG-codes and establish the existence of asymptotically good sequences among them. Beyond its simplicity, a key advantage of our approach is its flexibility, which allows it to be applied to a wide range of recursive towers of function fields, thereby providing a more explicit way to construct asymptotically good sequences of iso-dual AG-codes.
papers.comments: To appear in Bulletin of the Brazilian Mathematical Society, New Series

papers.title: Low-regularity error estimates of a filtered Lie-Trotter splitting scheme for the Zakharov system in arbitrary dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish low-regularity error estimates for a fully discrete, filtered Lie--Trotter splitting scheme for the Zakharov system on the $d$-dimensional torus. Our analysis relies on multilinear estimates in discrete Bourgain spaces. Specifically, for an exact solution $(E,z,z_t)$ with regularity $H^{s+r+1/2}\times H^{s+r}\times H^{s+r-1}$ on a fixed time interval, we prove an error bound of order $\mathcal{O}(τ^{s/2}+N^{-s})$ in $H^{r+1/2}\times H^r\times H^{r-1}$ for $s\in(0,2]$, where $r=\max\{0,\tfrac d2-1\}$, $τ$ is the time step, and $N$ is the number of spatial grid points in each coordinate direction. The analysis treats the coupled nonlinearities directly, without introducing the time-differentiated auxiliary variables of an Ozawa-type transformation. Under the stated CFL condition, which renders the filter inactive on the Fourier collocation space, the scheme preserves discrete mass exactly in exact arithmetic. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence rates and show small relative energy errors over the tested time intervals.

papers.title: The Betti Numbers of Kunz-Waldi Semigroups
papers.abstract: Given two coprime numbers $p<q$, KW semigroups contain $p,q$ and are contained in $\langle p,q,r \rangle$ where $2r= p,q, p+q$ whichever is even. These semigroups were first introduced by Kunz and Waldi. Kunz and Waldi proved that all $KW$ semigroups of embedding dimension $n\geq 4$ have Cohen-Macaulay type $n-1$ and first Betti number ${n \choose 2}$. In this paper, we characterize KW semigroups whose defining ideal is generated by the $2\times 2$ minors of a $2\times n$ matrix. In addition, we identify all KW semigroups that lie on the interior of the same face of the Kunz cone $\mathcal C_p$ as a KW semigroup with determinantal defining ideal. Thus, we provide an explicit formula for the Betti numbers of all those KW semigroups.
papers.comments: A correction:Prop 2.6, a criterion for KW semigroups to lie in the interior of the same face of the Kunz cone, was integral to our main result, and needed correcting:the Apery set of a KW semigroup isn't always homogeneous. We state when it is homogeneous (Remark 3) and how covering relations change when it isn't. Cor 2.8 retains its statement with a modified proof. All other results unaffected

papers.title: On $(Σ^2_1)^{uB}$ Absoluteness Between V and HOD
papers.abstract: We put together Woodin's $Σ^2_1$ basis theorem of AD$^+$ and Vopěnka's theorem to conclude the following: If there is a proper class of Woodin cardinals, then every $(Σ^2_1)^{\mbox{uB}}$ statement that is true in $V$ is true in $\mbox{HOD}$. Moreover, this is true even if we allow a parameter $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that $C$ and its complement have scales that are $\mbox{OD}$ and universally Baire. We also investigate whether $(Σ^2_1)^{\mbox{uB}}$ statements are upwards absolute from $\mbox{HOD}$ to $V$ under large cardinal hypotheses, observing that this is true if $\mbox{HOD}$ has a proper class of Woodin cardinals. Finally, we discuss $(\forall^{\mathbb{R}})\, (Σ^2_1)^{\mbox{uB}}$ absoluteness and conclude that this much absoluteness between $\mbox{HOD}$ and $V$ cannot be implied by any large cardinal axiom consistent with the axiom ``$V =$ Ultimate $L$''.

papers.title: Finite element spaces of double forms
papers.abstract: The tensor product of two differential forms of degree $p$ and $q$ is a multilinear form that is alternating in its first $p$ arguments and alternating in its last $q$ arguments. These forms, which are known as double forms or $(p,q)$-forms, play a central role in certain differential complexes that arise when studying partial differential equations. We construct piecewise polynomial finite element spaces for all of the natural subspaces of the space of $(p,q)$-forms, excluding one subspace which fails to admit a piecewise constant discretization. As special cases, our construction recovers known finite element spaces for symmetric matrices with tangential-tangential continuity (the Regge finite elements), symmetric matrices with normal-normal continuity, and trace-free matrices with normal-tangential continuity. It also gives rise to new spaces, like a finite element space for tensors possessing the symmetries of the Riemann curvature tensor.

papers.title: The Error in a Smooth Weighted Prime Number Formula and Zero-free Regions for the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We study the error bound for a smooth weighted prime number theorem, and its implication to the zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function using the method of Pintz. We also give an application to the average number of smooth weighted Goldbach representations and generalize the result to the case of smooth weighted average k-Goldbach representations.

papers.title: First-order methods for stochastic and finite-sum convex optimization with deterministic constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of stochastic and finite-sum convex optimization problems with deterministic constraints. Existing methods typically aim to find an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, in which both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are within a prescribed tolerance $ε$. However, in many practical applications, constraints must be nearly satisfied with certainty, rendering such solutions potentially unsuitable due to the risk of substantial violations. To address this issue, we propose stochastic first-order methods for finding an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, where the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$ and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. Our methods apply an accelerated stochastic gradient (ASG) scheme or a modified variance-reduced ASG scheme $only\ once$ to a sequence of quadratic penalty subproblems with appropriately chosen penalty parameters. We establish first-order oracle complexity bounds for the proposed methods in computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed methods.
papers.comments: Accepted by Mathematics of Operations Research

papers.title: Regularity of velocity averages in kinetic equations with heterogeneity
papers.abstract: This study investigates the regularity of kinetic equations with spatial heterogeneity. Recent progress has shown that velocity averages of weak solutions $h$ in $L^p$ ($p>1$) are strongly $L^1_{\text{loc}}$ compact under the natural non-degeneracy condition. We establish regularity estimates for equations with an $\boldsymbol{x}$-dependent drift vector $\mathfrak{f} = \mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbolλ)$, which satisfies a quantitative version of the non-degeneracy condition. We prove that $(t,\boldsymbol{x}) \mapsto \int ρ(\boldsymbolλ) h(t,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbolλ)\, d\boldsymbolλ$, for any sufficiently regular $ρ(\cdot)$, belongs to the fractional Sobolev space $W_{\text{loc}}^{β,r}$, for some regularity $β\in (0,1)$ and integrability $r \geq 1$ exponents. While such estimates have long been known for $\boldsymbol{x}$-independent drift vectors $\mathfrak{f}=\mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbolλ)$, this is the first quantitative regularity estimate in a general heterogeneous setting. As an application, we obtain a regularity estimate for entropy solutions to heterogeneous conservation laws with nonlinear flux and $L^\infty$ initial data.
papers.comments: We have modified the assumptions to accommodate nonsmooth drift throughout the paper. We have included two applications: (1) multidimensional scalar conservation laws with discontinuous flux and (2) a regularity result for the density variable in isentropic gas dynamics, given a regularity assumption on the velocity

papers.title: Approximation of the Lévy-driven stochastic heat equation on the sphere
papers.abstract: The stochastic heat equation on the sphere driven by an additive square-integrable Lévy process is approximated by a spectral method in space and forward and backward Euler-Maruyama schemes in time. New sharp regularity results are proven for its solution. The spectral approximation is based on a truncation of the series expansion with respect to the spherical harmonic functions. For a given regularity of the initial condition and two different settings of regularity for the driving noise, strong convergence rates for the spectral approximation and for the Euler-Maruyama methods are proven. Moreover, weak rates of up to twice the strong rates are shown for Wiener noise and for Lévy noise with independent and up to a deterministic decay rate factor identically distributed components, while for general square-integrable Lévy noise the weak rate depends explicitly on the polynomial order of the test function. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results.

papers.title: Co-periods and central symmetric cube L-values
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the co-period integral attached to an automorphic form on $\GL(2)$ and two exceptional theta series on the cubic Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $\GL(2)$. In the local aspect, we show the $\Hom$-space is always of one dimension and conduct the unramified calculations. In the global aspect, we give the Euler decomposition for the co-period integrals of Eisenstein series and propose an Ichino-Ikeda type conjecture relating the co-period integrals of cuspidal forms to the central critical value of symmetric cube $L$-functions. We also deduce from the local multiplicity one result that there exist cuspidal automorphic forms with prescribed local components and non-vanishing central symmetric cube $L$-values.

papers.title: Frames over finite fields with respect to the Galois inner product and their connections to self-orthogonal and LCD codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize the theory of frames to vector spaces over finite fields equipped with the $\ell$-Galois inner product. We introduce $\ell$-Galois analogues of fundamental concepts in frame theory and investigate extensions of existing results to the $\ell$-Galois setting. In particular, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a given matrix to be the $\ell$-Galois Gram matrix of a frame and show that such frames are unique up to isometry. We also extend Gerzon's bound to $\ell$-Galois equiangular systems and show that equality in this bound yields an $\ell$-Galois equiangular tight frame. Furthermore, we investigate the connections between $\ell$-Galois frames and $\ell$-Galois self-orthogonal and LCD codes over finite fields. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for constructing $\ell$-Galois equiangular tight frames from self-dual codes, generalizing existing results by Shi et al. on the relationship between frames and self-dual codes over finite fields. Beyond self-dual codes, we provide sufficient conditions for constructing $\ell$-Galois equiangular tight frames from linear codes using their automorphism groups, together with explicit examples.

papers.title: Linearity of fundamental groups of graphs of virtually cyclic groups
papers.abstract: We characterize when a generalized Baumslag-Solitar group is linear, and extend the result to the fundamental groups of a graph of groups with infinite virtually cyclic vertex and edge groups.

papers.title: On the Algebraic Independence of $E$- and $G$-Functions, II: An Effective Version
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ that is totally ramified over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. The set $\mathcal{M}\mathcal{F}(K)$ consists of power series in $1+zK[[z]]$ that are solutions of differential operators in $K(z)[d/dz]$ equipped with strong Frobenius structure and satisfying maximal order multiplicty (MOM) condition at zero. It turns out that this set contains an interesting class of $E$- and $G$-functions. In this work, we provide a criterion for determining the algebraic independence, over the field of analytic elements, of elements belonging to $\mathcal{M}\mathcal{F}(K)$. As an illustration of this criterion, we show the algebraic independence of some $E$- and $G$-functions over the field of analytic elements.

papers.title: A Multivariate Generalized Cox Model for Dependent and Simultaneous Default Times
papers.abstract: We propose a framework for dependent default times where each name defaults when an increasing driver crosses an independent unit exponential threshold. As in Gueye and Jeanblanc (2022), the drivers may jump, so defaults may occur at stopping times of the reference filtration, including predictable ones, and a common jump may cause no, one or several simultaneous defaults. For general drivers, we derive the conditional joint survival law by a backward recursion; it is an explicit product of survival functions if and only if, for every set of names, the predictable reduction of the compensator of their first default time is deterministic. If, moreover, defaults avoid predictable stopping times, the law is a fatal shock law with hazards identified from the drivers; predictable default atoms can rule this out. Examples include Lévy subordinators and, with random reductions but explicit laws, Liu's model and shot-noise drivers with memory.

papers.title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
papers.abstract: We study the hardmax limit of self-attention dynamics for token embeddings obtained in the zero-temperature ($β\to+\infty$) regime, and relate it to the finite-$β$ setting. In this limit, the update rule can be viewed as a Frank-Wolfe step for a quadratic objective over the convex hull of the current token embeddings. When the key-query matrix is negative semidefinite, the method linearly contracts all tokens to a single cluster at the origin. When it is positive semidefinite, extending the hardmax rule to the entire convex hull induces a Voronoi diagram: vertices are stationary, interior points remain in their initial cells, and each token moves along a straight line toward its cell's vertex, yielding (super-)exponential convergence. As a byproduct, we also establish well-posedness of the associated ODE limit in this regime. Returning to the finite-$β$ regime, we model self-attention dynamics as a Markov chain and prove dynamic metastability: with high probability, interior tokens reach near-vertex configurations in a constant number of steps and remain within a small neighborhood for times that grow exponentially in the inverse temperature $β$, before ultimately collapsing to the origin. Thus, the hardmax dynamics accurately approximate the finite-$β$ process over exponentially long time horizons.
papers.comments: Accepted at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning: https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/60480 Funded by the European Union's HORIZON-MSCA-2021-DN-01-01, through ModConFlex ("Modelling and control of flexible structures interacting with fluids"; No. 101073558; DOI: 10.3030/101073558). Code: https://github.com/borjanG/2025-transformers-frank-wolfe, code DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23468440

papers.title: Antiferromagnetic Long-Range Order in a Lattice Fermion Model
papers.abstract: We study a lattice fermion model with antiferromagnetic interactions on the three-dimensional cubic lattice. The hopping term of the Hamiltonian has a Weyl-type dispersion. We prove that the model has reflection positivity. Moreover, by relying on the property, we prove the existence of the antiferromagnetic long-range order at low temperatures in a strong coupling regime.
papers.comments: 29 pages, final version to appear in Journal of Statistical Physics
papers.journal_ref: J. Stat. Phys. 193 (2026)

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis on narrow tubes: narrow escape problems and diffusion processes
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a diffusion process in a narrow tubular domain with reflecting boundary conditions, where the geometry serves as a singular perturbation of an underlying graph in $\mathbb{R}^2$ or $\mathbb{R}^3$. The construction incorporates distinct scaling regimes in the neighborhoods of the graph's vertices and edges. We show that, in the limit, the projected process converges weakly to a diffusion process on the graph, with gluing conditions at the vertices that depend on the relative scales of the neighborhoods. Our analysis relies on a detailed understanding of the narrow escape problem in domains with bottlenecks. In particular, we rigorously derive the asymptotic behavior of the expected escape time, establish the asymptotic exponential distribution of escape times and obtain exit place estimates, results that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Cluster Expansion and Decay of Correlations for Multidimensional Long-Range Ising Models
papers.abstract: We develop the cluster expansion for the multidimensional multiscaled contours defined by three of us. These contours are suitable for long-range Ising models with interaction $J_{xy}=J(|x-y|)= J/|x-y|^α$, $J>0$, and $α>d$. As an application of the convergence of the cluster expansion at low temperatures, we study the decay of the truncated two-point correlation functions, showing that the decay is algebraic with coefficient $α$.
papers.comments: 44 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Probability and Mathematical Physics (PMP)

papers.title: Annihilating ideals and Agler--McCarthy spectral varieties in the bidisc
papers.abstract: The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.
papers.comments: Version 3: A missing assumption has been added to Theorem 2.6. The statement of Theorem 2.11 has been reworded. An issue in Theorem 3.12 has been fixed. 26 pages

papers.title: Differentiable-by-design Nonlinear Optimization for Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Nonlinear optimization-based control policies, such as those arising in nonlinear Model Predictive Control, have seen remarkable success in recent years. These policies require solving computationally demanding nonlinear optimization programs online at each time-step. The resulting solution map, viewed as a function of the measured state of the system and design parameters, may not be differentiable, which poses significant challenges if the control policy is embedded in a gradient-based policy optimization scheme. We propose a principled way to regularize the nonlinear optimization problem around the nominal solution, obtaining a surrogate derivative even if the solution map of the original problem is not differentiable. The surrogate problem is differentiable by design and its solution coincides with the solution of the unregularized problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in a free-final-time optimal control problem and a receding-horizon nonlinear MPC example.

papers.title: Boundary Feller-Dynkin processes associated with Laguerre processes and Pickrell diffusions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a Feller-Dynkin boundary process by applying the method of intertwiners to the coherent family, introduced in our previous work, of Laguerre processes with a fixed parameter. The corresponding boundary process is computed explicitly, and it turns out to be a deterministic dynamical system. Since the Pickrell diffusions that leave the Pickrell measure invariant are coherent with respect to the same projective system, we also obtain the stochastic boundary process associated with the coherent family of Pickrell diffusions.

papers.title: Secant sheaves on abelian n-folds with real multiplication and Weil classes on abelian 2n-folds with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: Let K be a CM-field, i.e., a totally complex quadratic extension of a totally real field F. Let X be a g-dimensional abelian variety admitting an algebra embedding of F into the rational endomorphisms End_Q(X) of X. Let A be the product of X and Pic^0(X). We construct an embedding e of K into End_Q(A) associated to a choice of an F-bilinear polarization h on X and a purely imaginary element q in K. We get the [K:Q]-dimensional subspace HW(A,e) of Hodge Weil classes in the d-th cohomology of A, where d:=4g/[K:Q]. Let V be the first cohomology of A. The even cohomology S^+ of X is the half-spin representation of the group Spin(V) and so the projectivization P(S^+) contains the even spinorial variety. The latter is a component of the Grassmannian of maximal isotropic subspaces of V. We associate to (h,q) a rational 2^[F:Q]-dimensional subspace B of S^+ such that P(B) is secant to the spinorial variety. Associated to two coherent sheaves G and G' on X with Chern characters in B we obtain the object E in D^b(A) by applying Orlov's equivalence between D^b(XxX) and D^b(A) to the outer tensor product of G and G'. The flat deformations of a normalized Chern class k(E) of E remain of Hodge type under every deformation of (A,e) as an abelian variety (A',e') of Weil type. We provide a criterion for the tensor product of ch(G) and ch(G') to belong to the open subset in the tensor square of B for which the algebraicity of the flat deformation of k(E) implies the algebraicity of all classes in HW(A',e'). The algebraicity would thus follow if E is semiregular in the appropriate sense. Examples of such secant sheaves G and G' are provided for X the Jacobian with real multiplication by a real quadratic number field F of a genus 4 curve. The search for semiregular such E is left for future work.

papers.title: Critical phenomena in 2D Coulomb gas: Birth of a gap
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of radially symmetric Coulomb gas systems at inverse temperature $β= 2$. The family is characterised by the property that the density of the equilibrium measure vanishes on a ring at radius $r_*$, which lies strictly inside the droplet. The large-$n$ expansion of the logarithm of the partition function is obtained up to the constant term and features a novel term of order $n^{1/4}$. We perform a double scaling limit of the correlation kernel at the $n^{1/4}$ scale and obtain a new limiting kernel in the bulk, which differs from the well-known Ginibre kernel.
