papers.comments: 36 pages, 6 figures. Title changed and minor corrections. Peer reviewed version

papers.title: A polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of block-structured graphs
papers.abstract: The boxicity of a graph $G$ is the minimum dimension $d$ that admits a representation of $G$ as the intersection graph of a family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Boxicity has applications in ecology and operations research, where it models competition for shared resources. Computing boxicity is an NP-hard problem. Despite considerable theoretical interest, few graph classes are known for which the boxicity can be computed in polynomial time. Following the approach of Cozzens and Roberts (1983), we study directly the boxicity of graph complements, which we call co-boxicity. In this setting, the geometric intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ becomes a graph cover problem involving only complements of interval graphs. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that computes the co-boxicity of $G$ from two pieces of information about each block: its co-boxicity, and how the co-boxicity changes when certain subsets of its vertices become cut-vertices. Using this algorithm, we obtain polynomial-time algorithms for the co-boxicity of trees, graphs with bounded block order, block graphs, and cactus graphs. More generally, our method implies the union of these results: for any fixed $k \geq 3$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of $G$ whenever every block of $G$ is complete, a cycle, or has at most $k$ vertices.

papers.title: On the decomposition of the diagonal for n-fold hypersurfaces via cubic n-1-folds
papers.abstract: We study the question of the existence of a decomposition of the diagonal for very general degree $d\geq 4$ and $(2,d\geq 3)$-complete intersection $n$-folds. Using cycle-theoretic techniques of Lange, Pavic and Schreieder we reduce the question to the existence of such a decomposition for $n-1$-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces. This extends results of Nicaise and Ottem from stable rationality to the existence of a decomposition of the diagonal. A key ingredient is the essential dimension of cubic hypersurfaces due to Voisin. As an application, we use a recent result of Engel, de Gaay Fortman and Schreieder on the decomposition of the diagonal for cubic threefolds to give a new proof of the retract irrationality of a very general complex quartic $4$-fold, originally due to Totaro, and of a very general complex $(2,3)$-complete intersection $4$-fold, originally due to Skauli. As another application we show that a very general quintic fourfold containing a three-dimensional linear subspace with multiplicity $2$, which is unirational due to results of Massarenti, does not admit a decomposition of the diagonal and is therefore not retract rational.
papers.comments: 13 pages, final version, to appear in European Journal of Mathematics
papers.journal_ref: Volume 12, article number 54 (2026) Volume 12, article number 54 (2026) European J. of Math., Volume 12, article number 54 (2026)

papers.title: Generalized Centralizers and Polynomial Equivalence of Matrices: Answers to Questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova
papers.abstract:
For $n	imes n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ over a field and a scalar $ω
e0$, let $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\{X:AX=ωXA\}$. If $ω$ is a root of unity of order $q\ge2$, then $\mathcal C_{ω^j}(A)=\mathcal C_{ω^j}(B)$ for all integers $j$ if and only if each of $A$ and $B$ is a polynomial in the other with exponents $\equiv1\pmod q$. Over algebraically closed fields, for $ω
e1$, all $A$, and scalars $\varepsilon
e0$, we describe all $Y$ with $XY=\varepsilon YX$ for all $X\in\mathcal C_ω(A)$. Let $a(μ)$ be the size of the largest Jordan block of $A$ at $μ$, or $0$ if there is none. If $\varepsilon$ is a power of $ω$, all such $Y$ are polynomials in $A$ if and only if $a(ωμ)=a(μ)$ for all $μ
e0$, or this fails only at some $ν$ and at $ω^{-1}ν$, where $A$ has a single largest Jordan block at $ν$ and $a(ων)=a(ω^{-1}ν)=a(ν)-1$. This answers two questions of Dolinar, Guterman, Kuzma, and Markova. If $ω
e1$ has finite order, then for such $A$, $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\mathcal C_ω(B)$ exactly when $A$ and $B$ are polynomials in each other of this form. For all other $A$ some $B$ that is not a polynomial in $A$ satisfies $\mathcal C_ω(A)=\mathcal C_ω(B)$ if the field has more than $n^2+1$ elements. In the $ω$-commuting digraph of Raja and Vaezpour, with an edge from $A$ to $B$ if $AB=ωBA$, vertices with edges to and from the same vertices are twins. Over fields with more than $2n^2+1$ elements we determine the vertices $A$ whose twins are all polynomials in $A$, and describe these twins. We find all $A$, $B$, and $k\ge2$ for which the kernel of $(X\mapsto[A,X])^k$ is the set of $X$ with $[X,[X,\ldots,[X,B]\ldots]]=0$ ($k$ brackets), where $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. Apart from scalar $B$, this happens only in characteristic $
e2$, for $k=2$ and $2	imes2$ matrices that generate the same quadratic extension.
papers.comments: 41 pages, 5 figures. Substantially revised and expanded, with new results, corrections of errors in v2, and extensive changes to the structure and exposition

papers.title: Blow-up rate for the subcritical semilinear heat equation in non-convex domains
papers.abstract: We consider the semilinear heat equation $u_t=Δu+|u|^{p-1} u$ in possibly non-convex and unbounded domains. Our main result shows the nonexistence of type II blow-up for possibly sign-changing solutions in the energy subcritical range $(n-2)p<n+2$. This resolves a long-standing open question dating back to the 1980s and also deduces the blow-up of the scaling critical norm.
papers.comments: 30 pages; revised following referee comments; main results unchanged

papers.title: A Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on non-CMC closed manifolds
papers.abstract: In the paper, we prove the existence of a positive and essentially bounded solution to a Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on a closed manifold with non-constant mean curvature. In particular, the non-constant mean curvature gives rise to supercritical terms in the equation, on top of singular ones. We employ a recent fixed-point argument, which involves sub- and supersolutions. Additionally, we provide several conditions on the coefficients in the equation that prevent the existence of positive classical solutions.
papers.journal_ref: Nonlinear Anal. 276 (2027), Article No. 114326, 10 pp

papers.title: On a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture via categorical representations
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a complex reductive group. For a smooth affine spherical $G$-variety $X$ such that the stabilizer of a point in the $B$-orbit under the $B$-action be connected, assume that the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi-Sakellaridis-Venkatesh (BZSV) for $X$ holds. We establish a spectral description of a full subcategory of Iwahori equivariant coherent D-modules on $LX$ in terms of the relative Langlands dual of $X$, confirming a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture proposed by Devalapurkar.
papers.comments: 47 pages, in comparison to previous version: proof of main theorem is slightly modified, a new supplement result (Theorem 1.3) addressing generation by one element in the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture, and a case study (Section 7) is described in details

papers.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
papers.abstract: We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent. We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

papers.title: Virasoro elements in conformal algebras
papers.abstract: It is well known that Virasoro elements play an extremely important role in the theory of vertex operator algebras, and likewise a very significant role in the field of conformal algebras. In this paper, we introduce the notion of a regular action in the category of conformal modules over Lie conformal algebras with Virasoro elements. We show that a finite conformal module over the general conformal algebra $\mathfrak{gc}_1$ (resp., $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ with $N\ge2$) is semisimple if and only if there exists a pair of different Virasoro elements (resp., canonical Virasoro elements) with regular actions. Along the way to finding semisimplicity criteria, we also discuss the classification of Virasoro elements of $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ in-depth, leading us to construct a huge number of new Virasoro conformal modules.
papers.comments: 24 pages; title changed, Theorem 3.3 updated, added the proof of Lemma 5.2, to appear in Communications in Mathematical Physics

papers.title: Lower Bounds on High Moments of Twisted Fourier coefficients of Modular Forms
papers.abstract: For any large prime $q$, $x \leq 1$ and any real $k\geq 2$, we prove a lower bound for the following $2k$-th moment \begin{equation*} \sum_{\substack{χ\in X_q^*}} \Big| \sum_{n\leq x} χ(n)λ(n)\Big|^{2k}, \end{equation*} where $X_q^*$ denotes the set of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ and $λ(n)$ the Fourier coefficients of a fixed modular form. The bound we obtain is sharp up to a constant factor under the generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
papers.comments: 21 pages, revised according to the referee's comments and suggestions

papers.title: Efficient and rate-optimal list-decoding in the presence of minimal feedback
papers.abstract: Given a channel with length-$n$ inputs and outputs over the alphabet $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$, and of which a fraction $\varrho \in (0,1-1/q)$ of symbols can be arbitrarily corrupted by an adversary, a fundamental problem is that of communicating at rates close to the information-theoretically optimal values, while ensuring the receiver can infer that the transmitter's message is from a ``small" set. While the existence of such codes is known, and constructions with computationally tractable encoding/decoding procedures are known for large $q$, we provide the first schemes that attain this performance for any $q \geq 2$, as long as low-rate feedback (asymptotically negligible relative to the number of transmissions) from the receiver to the transmitter is available. For any sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\varrho \in (1-{1}/{q}-Θ(\sqrt{\varepsilon}))$ our minimal feedback scheme has the following parameters: Rate $1-H_q(\varrho) - \varepsilon$ (i.e., $\varepsilon$-close to information-theoretically optimal -- here $H_q(\varrho)$ is the $q$-ary entropy function), list-size $\exp\left(\mathcal{O}\left(\varepsilon^{-3/2}\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\right)\right)$, computational complexity of encoding/decoding $n^{\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\varepsilon))}$, storage complexity $\mathcal{O}(n^{η+1}\log n)$ for a code design parameter $η>1$ that trades off storage complexity with the probability of error. The error probability is $\mathcal{O}(n^{-η})$, and the (vanishing) feedback rate is $\mathcal{O}({1}/{\sqrt{\log(n)}})$. Our full-feedback scheme has zero probability of error and minimal storage complexity, while the other parameters are the same as the vanishing rate feedback scheme.

papers.title: A kernel method for the learning of Wasserstein geometric flows
papers.abstract: Wasserstein gradient and Hamiltonian flows provide geometric formulations of many partial differential equations. We develop a structure-preserving kernel method for jointly estimating the external potential and interaction kernel governing these flows, assuming a known internal energy. The inverse problem is formulated through a trajectory-dependent observation operator and regularized in a product of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, yielding an explicit finite representation of the estimator. We characterize joint non-identifiability through the null space of the observation operator and derive a Fourier criterion on the torus, distinguishing uniqueness of the regularized estimator from recovery of the underlying physical components. We establish reconstruction error bounds and convergence rates under source conditions and suitable regularization and mesh refinement, together with a stability estimate for Hamiltonian flows with vanishing internal energy. Numerical experiments demonstrate joint reconstruction and illustrate how unobservable interaction modes can prevent accurate potential recovery despite small observation-equation residuals. A comparison with sparse learning illustrates the dependence of reconstruction accuracy on the chosen dictionary.

papers.title: On the $2$-torsion in class groups of number fields
papers.abstract: In $2020$, Bhargava, Shankar, Taniguchi, Thorne, Tsimerman, and Zhao proved that for a finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $n\geq 5$, the size of the $2$-torsion class group is bounded by $\# h_{2}(K)=O_{n,\varepsilon}(D_{K}^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2n}+\varepsilon})$, where $D_{K}$ is the absolute discriminant of $K$. In the present paper, we improve their bound by proving that $\# h_{2}(K)=O_{n,\varepsilon}(D_{K}^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2n}-δ_{K}+\varepsilon})$, for a constant $δ_{K}\geq\frac{1}{28n}-\frac{3}{28n(n-1)}$.

papers.title: Generalized Boltzmann-Gibbs Distributions and the Electronic Partition Function Paradox
papers.abstract: The maximization of the nonadditive entropic functional $S_{q}(p)=k\sum_{i}p_{i}\ln_{q}(1/p_{i})$, $q\in(0,1)$, under a linear mean-energy constraint, i.e., the best-behaved case from Dognini and Tsallis (2026), is used to derive generalizations of the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution for physical systems whose description requires a limiting process over the energy spectrum: the hydrogen atom in free space; an energy spectrum that uniformly approaches a continuous, unbounded limit with a common degeneracy; the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of velocities; the harmonic oscillator; and the one-dimensional box. For the hydrogen atom with mean energy $U\in[0,e_{ion}]$, the limiting optimal distribution is a two-tier one, concentrated on the ground level and on the ionization threshold, with weights $1-U/e_{ion}$ and $U/e_{ion}$ for every $q\in(0,1)$, and the temperature rescaled by $\ln_{q}W$ is finite and given by $T_{q,s}=T_{ion}(U/e_{ion})^{1-q}$, with $T_{ion}=e_{ion}/kq$. This circumvents the Electronic Partition Function Paradox and yields a family of well-defined thermodynamic behaviors.

papers.title: Seaweed algebras with restricted part sizes
papers.abstract: Seaweed algebras are a class of Lie algebras that are naturally characterized by a pair of compositions, which in turn are represented visually as planar graphs called meanders. These meanders provide a straightforward method for computing the index of the associated algebra. The goal of this paper is to enumerate those seaweed algebras with a fixed index and whose associated compositions have restricted part sizes. In particular, we enumerate those with composition part sizes from so-called acyclic sets. We also establish a bijection between sets of indecomposable seaweed algebras with meanders with certain restricted part sizes and sets of permutations with restricted displacements. In certain cases, the index of the algebra can be determined by a simple statistic on the permutation.
papers.comments: 28 pages. v3: added additional exposition, fixed errors in some of generating functions

papers.title: Blown-up singular Riemannian foliations
papers.abstract: We study the effect of projective blow-ups on the leaf closures and basic cohomology of singular Riemannian foliations. For a foliation with smooth Molino sheaf on a compact manifold, we show that the Molino sheaf of the blow-up is the inverse image of the original sheaf under blow-down. In particular, desingularization preserves the Killing property and the structural Lie algebra. We obtain a closedness criterion in terms of the Euler characteristics of the ambient manifold and the blow-up centers, assuming finite fundamental group and singular strata of codimension at least three. For singular Killing foliations on compact manifolds, we approximate the space of leaf closures in Gromov--Hausdorff distance by Riemannian orbifolds whose dimension equals the codimension of the foliation. Finally, relative basic cohomology gives a long exact sequence relating the original foliation, its blow-up, and their restrictions to the center and the exceptional divisor.
papers.comments: Major revisions; results changed. Revised blow-up construction and Molino sheaf comparison; corrected hypotheses for the Euler characteristic criterion; completed the Gromov-Hausdorff approximation proof; expanded basic cohomology results via relative cohomology

papers.title: A Taxonomy of Numerical Differentiation Methods
papers.abstract: Differentiation is a cornerstone of computing and data analysis in every discipline of science and engineering. Indeed, most fundamental physics laws are expressed as relationships between derivatives in space and time. However, derivatives are rarely directly measurable and must instead be computed, often from noisy, potentially corrupt data streams. There is a rich and broad literature of computational differentiation algorithms, but many impose extra constraints to work correctly, e.g. periodic boundary conditions, or are compromised in the presence of noise and corruption. It can therefore be challenging to select the method best-suited to any particular problem. Here we review a broad range of numerical methods for calculating derivatives, present important contextual considerations and choice points, compare relative advantages, and provide basic theory for each algorithm in order to assist users with the mathematical underpinnings. This serves as a practical guide to help scientists and engineers match methods to application domains. We also provide an open-source Python package, PyNumDiff, which contains a broad suite of methods for differentiating noisy data.
papers.comments: Submitted to the Journal of Computational Physics, PyNumDiff package available at https://pypi.org/project/pynumdiff/

papers.title: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
papers.abstract: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $ε$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

papers.title: Composition laws for homogeneous energies and symphonic maps
papers.abstract: For a spectral energy homogeneous of degree $q>1$ in the differential, we characterize the smooth maps which pull back stationary maps into every Riemannian target. If the scalar density is nonzero, these maps are precisely the $q$-harmonic morphisms. The weak statement requires only $C^1$ regularity in the differential variable. It also covers densities which vanish on the identity of the intermediate tangent space. For the energies of the stress tensor $S$ and its trace-free analogue $T$, the source dimension enters the flux. In dimensions at least two we obtain a complete dichotomy: in equal dimensions the preserving maps are the $2p$-harmonic morphisms, and in unequal dimensions only locally constant maps preserve all targets. A hypersurface of dimension $n$ in a target of dimension $n+1$ detects the obstruction when the source dimension exceeds the intermediate dimension $n$.

papers.title: Polynomiality ideals, with applications to polynomial functors over free nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a unital commutative ring. For a monoidal category $C$ whose unit is a zero object, we introduce a descending filtration of the k-linearization of $C$ by two-sided ideals, called the polynomiality ideals: the $d$-th ideal encodes polynomiality of degree at most $d$ for functors from $C$ to $k$-modules. These ideals yield general criteria for the existence of polynomial functors of a given degree and for equivalences between the categories of polynomial functors of degree at most $d$ over different base categories. For Lawvere theories satisfying a mild condition, we identify the polynomiality ideals with powers of augmentation ideals of monoids; this identification makes the criteria computable by means of classical group ring theory. As the main application, we study polynomial functors over finitely generated free nilpotent groups, comparing them across nilpotency classes and polynomial degrees. We obtain refinements of results of Baues and Pirashvili in the case of class at most 2, recover several folklore results for free groups and free abelian groups, and establish a modular analogue formulated with dimension subgroups over a field of positive characteristic in place of the lower central series. Finally, we show that, in contrast to polynomial functors, analytic functors admit no analogous ideal in most cases.

papers.title: Grundy Values of Node-Kayles on Level-Regular Trees
papers.abstract: Node-Kayles is an impartial combinatorial game played on graphs, in which the two players alternately select a vertex and remove it together with all of its neighbours. By the Sprague--Grundy theorem, every position has a Grundy value that determines its outcome under optimal play. In this paper we study the Grundy values of Node-Kayles on level-regular trees $\T{a}$, $a=(a_1,\dots,a_d)$, in which every vertex at level $i-1$ has exactly $a_i$ children. We determine the Grundy values of all level-regular trees of depth at most two, show that $\G(\T{a})\le d+1$, and prove that $\G(\T{a})>0$ whenever $a_1a_2a_3$ is even, using an explicit mirror strategy. We prove a Leaf-Pair Lemma, which shows that the last branching parameter $a_d$ matters only through its parity, and a Twin Lemma for subgraphs that come in isomorphic pairs; as a consequence, $\G(\T{1,2k,s})=1$ for every $k\ge1$ and every finite sequence $s$. For trees containing a long run of ones, we give a general periodicity criterion: if the Grundy values of a tree with a pendant path of length $h$ are $34$-periodic on a finite window, then they are $34$-periodic for all larger $h$. This criterion extends to paths joining two fixed subtrees, and it explains the eventual periodicity of the families $\T{1^k,2}$ and $\T{2,1^k,2}$. We also show that, in this setting, eventual periodicity is equivalent to the boundedness of the Grundy values. Finally, supported by computations, we conjecture that the Grundy values are eventually periodic, with period $2$, in each branching parameter, and eventually periodic in the length of every run of ones.

papers.title: Plane partitions and spin adapted quantum states
papers.abstract: We describe an explicit basis for the $\operatorname{SU}(2)$-invariant space of the exterior power $\wedge_{2k} \mathbb{C}^{2m}$ via the combinatorics of plane partitions. In quantum chemistry, this is the space of spin adapted quantum states of an electronic system with $m$ spin orbitals and $k$ electron pairs. We construct our basis by identifying the invariant space with an Artinian commutative ring called the excitation ring. We compute a Gröbner basis and enumerate its standard monomials via an explicit bijection to Dyck paths counted by the Narayana numbers.
papers.comments: v2: major revisions. The standard monomial basis for $S_{m, k}$ is now obtained via a representation theoretic argument regarding ideals of "generalized permanents" rather than Macaulay2 computations. Additional details and revisions for clarity have been made throughout the paper. We are grateful to the anonymous journal referees whose comments inspired these changes. 15 pages

papers.title: The Inverse Symplectic Eigenvalue Problem of a Graph
papers.abstract: Symplectic geometry plays an increasingly important role in mathematics, physics, and applications. The concept of symplectic eigenvalues, whose existence for positive definite matrices is known as Williamson's Theorem, naturally gives rise to inverse problems. We introduce the inverse symplectic eigenvalue problem for positive definite matrices described by a labeled graph and solve it for several families and all labeled graphs of order four. We develop various tools such as the Strong Symplectic Spectral Property (SSSP) together with its consequences, graph couplings to describe collections of labelings of a graph that produce the same symplectic eigenvalues, and coupled graph zero forcing. We establish numerous results for symplectic positive definite matrices, including a sharp lower bound on the number of nonzero entries of such an irreducible matrix (or equivalently, the number of edges in its graph). This lower bound is a consequence of a lower bound on the sum of the number of nonzero entries in an irreducible positive definite matrix and its inverse.

papers.title: Finite de Finetti for convex bodies and Polynomial Optimization
papers.abstract: We study polynomial optimization over convex bodies with separately affine objectives and local affine equality and inequality constraints. We construct a convergent hierarchy of conic relaxations with explicit finite-level error bounds of order $n^{-1/2}$ at level $n$, complemented by a constructive rounding scheme that produces feasible points. The relaxation bounds and rounded objective values bracket the optimum at the same rate. The analytic ingredient is a finite de Finetti representation theorem for arbitrary proper cones: bipartite marginals of symmetric extensions in maximal tensor products are $O(n^{-1/2})$-close, in base norm, to points of the minimal tensor product. Its proof combines a uniform, monogamy-type bound on a variational mutual information based on Frenkel's relative entropy with classical conditioning and informationally complete measurements. We apply the framework to the assemblage relaxation of two-player non-local games in general probabilistic theories. For polytopic state spaces, the hierarchy consists of linear programs, and experiments on the Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt (CHSH) game provide a numerical proof of concept for the outer approximations and feasible rounding procedure.
papers.comments: Main body and declarations, pp. 1-58. Appendices A-E, pp. 58-68. References, pp. 69-71. Julius A. Zeiss and Gereon Kossmann contributed equally to this work. Changes from v1: Added numerical illustrations and revised proofs, game formulation and exposition

papers.title: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties. We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{χ_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.
papers.comments: eight pictures; v3: Improved Hensley-type theorem, rewrote introduction and abstract and simplified proofs

papers.title: On the distribution of multiplicative energy
papers.abstract: This paper extends the investigation of energy distribution in finite settings, building on results established in our earlier work. We analyze the distribution of multiplicative energies of different orders using Fourier-analytic methods. Our results provide new structural insights into energy phenomena in finite fields, complementing earlier discrete analyses. In the last section, as a corollary, we obtain a 'sum-multiplicative energy'-type result.

papers.title: Optimistic Bilevel Optimization with Composite Lower-Level Problem
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel double regularization scheme for bilevel optimization problems whose lower-level problem is composite and convex, but not necessarily strongly convex, in the lower-level variable. The analysis focuses on the primal-dual solution mapping of the regularized lower-level problem and exploits its properties to derive an almost-everywhere formula for the gradient of the regularized hyper-objective under mild assumptions. The paper then establishes conditions under which the hyper-objective of the actual problem is well defined and shows that its gradient can be approximated by the gradient of the regularized hyper-objective. Building on these results, a gradient sampling-based algorithm computes approximately stationary points of the regularized hyper-objective, and we prove its convergence to stationary points of the actual problem. Three numerical examples from machine learning and transportation engineering demonstrate the proposed approach.
papers.comments: 44 pages. 3 figures. Submitted to Mathematics of Operations Research

papers.title: The Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence between Gaussian distributions
papers.abstract: We study the Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence when both the source and the target are Gaussian distributions. We prove the existence of a flow that stays in the class of Gaussian distributions, and is unique in the larger class of measures with strongly-concave and smooth log-densities. We prove that the flow globally converges toward the target measure when the source's covariance matrix is not singular, and provide counter-examples to global convergence when it is, giving a first answer to an open question raised in [Carlier et al. 2024, \S4.2]. When the covariance matrix of the source distribution commutes with that of the target, we derive more quantitative results that showcase exponential convergence toward the target when the source and the target share their support, but dropping to sublinear rates (O(t^{-1})) if the target is concentrated on a strict subspace of the source's support.

papers.title: Mean-field games with rough common noise: the linear-quadratic case
papers.abstract: Motivated by mean-field games (MFG) with common noise on the one hand and pathwise stochastic control theory on the other, we formulate here a linear-quadratic (LQ) MFG with rough common noise, along with a satisfactory well-posedness theory for the linear-quadratic case. A novel Volterra-type (or mild) formulation allows to keep technical (rough-stochastic) consideration to a minimum. We derive a characterization of the optimal state and optimal control through a rough forward-backward SDE (rough FBSDE), and provide an existence and uniqueness result under the usual assumptions. Our theory is accompanied by stability estimates with respect to initial data and common noise while we also establish continuity of what we call the Itô-Lions-Lyons map for rough mean-field games. Finally, we discuss randomization of the rough common noise under appropriate conditions on the coefficients. When the latter is given by the Stratonovich lift of a Brownian motion independent of the idiosyncratic noise, we show that solutions of the rough LQ MFG coincide with those obtained by conditioning on the common noise.
papers.comments: Remarks were added and typos corrected
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Differential Equations, Volume 490, 15 February 2027, 114932

papers.title: Strong Approximation for the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere
papers.abstract: We study the orbits of solutions to the Markoff-type equation $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + AX + BY + CZ + D$$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ for fixed integers $A,B,C,D$ under the group $Γ$ generated by \[\begin{split}&V_1: (x, y, z)\mapsto (A + yz - x, y, z),\\ &V_2: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, B + xz - y, z),\text{ and}\\ &V_3: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, y, C + xy - z).\end{split}\] This equation defines the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere, with $Γ$ arising from the Pure Mapping Class Group. Outside an explicit degeneracy locus, $Γ$ acts transitively on almost all solutions for a density-one set of primes independent of the parameters; the others split into small orbits reflecting finite orbits over $\mathbb{C}$. For ``degenerate'' parameters, we show there are two large orbits (most cases) or four (the rest, excluding $(0, 0, 0, 4)$) for the same primes. These results strengthen for two subfamilies. The first, $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + k,\,\,\,k\neq 4,$$ arises in the combinatorial group theory of $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. Combined with Chen's work, $Γ$ acts transitively for all large primes, uniformly in $k$, so the $Q$-classification conjecture of McCullough and Wanderley holds over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for $p$ large. By Martin's work, so do their Classification and $T$-Classification Conjectures. The second, $$x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + a_1x_2x_3 + a_2x_1x_3 + a_3x_1x_2 = (3+a_1+a_2+a_3)x_1x_2x_3,$$ arises from generalized cluster algebras. Our degeneracy notion specializes to that of de Courcy-Ireland, Litman, and Mizuno, whose results similarly imply our orbit count (1, 2, or 4) for all large primes for all nondegenerate and some degenerate surfaces in that family.ds for all sufficiently large primes.
papers.comments: 83 pages, 4 figures. v4: Added subsection 9.2, giving uniformity in parameters, and strengthened a special case via a result of Will Chen. v3: Exchanged Sections 6 and 7. Corrections to proof of Theorem 7.1 (in new section numbering), fixed gap in the proof of Proposition 9.1, re-organized and lemmatized the proof of Theorem 11.1, and corrected typos and improved exposition. v2: Added Section 11

papers.title: Circle packing and Riemann uniformization of random planar maps in an ergodic scale-free environment
papers.abstract: We prove that embedded infinite planar maps in ergodic scale-free environments are close to their circle packing and Riemann uniformization embeddings on a large scale, as long as suitable moment and connectivity conditions are satisfied. In subsequent work we use these results to prove convergence of random planar maps to Liouville quantum gravity under circle packing and Riemann uniformization embeddings.

papers.title: The Hofstadter Consecutive-Sum Sequence Omits Infinitely Many Positive Integers
papers.abstract: We study Hofstadter's greedy self-generating sequence, which begins with 1 and 2 and repeatedly chooses the least integer larger than the preceding term that is a sum of at least two consecutive earlier terms. We prove that the excess of its $n$th term over its index is bounded below by a positive constant times $\log\log n$, up to an additive constant, and that the sequence satisfies a polynomial upper bound. In particular, the sequence omits infinitely many positive integers.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 1 figure. Published in the Journal of Integer Sequences. This version incorporates the revisions made for publication
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.6.1

papers.title: Toroidal families and averages of $L$-functions, II: cubic moments
papers.abstract: Generalizing our previous work on ``toroidal averages'', we study the average of special values of $L$-functions of the form $L(1/2,χ^a)L(1/2,χ^b)L(1/2,χ^c)$ for integers $a$, $b$ and $c$, where $χ$ varies over Dirichlet characters of a given prime modulus. We highlight connections with estimates for bilinear forms of trace functions and with bounds for the number of solutions of monoidal equations in three variables in small boxes over finite fields.
papers.comments: 59 pages (to appear in the special volume of QJM dedicated to Roger Heath-Brown)

papers.title: A nonlocal transmission problem on a hybrid continuous-discrete domain
papers.abstract: We study a quadratic nonlocal variational problem on a hybrid domain formed by a compact interval and finitely many discrete points. The associated energy splits into continuous, discrete, and interface contributions. Our main estimate shows that the interface term yields a coercive coupling between the two phases and provides an equivalent hybrid norm. As a consequence, we prove existence and uniqueness of a minimizer for the corresponding variational problem and characterize it as the unique weak solution of the associated hybrid Euler--Lagrange system. The latter combines a nonlocal integral equation on the continuous component with a finite nonlocal algebraic system on the discrete nodes.
papers.comments: The present version has been substantially revised and extended, with additional theoretical developments, spectral investigations, and numerical experiments, and includes G. Rahman and K. Shaib Mohamed as co-authors

papers.title: Pohozaev identities and Liouville theorems for $L$-tension energies on manifolds
papers.abstract: We study autonomous energies $B(φ,e,\|τ_L\|^2/2)$ for a general Lagrangian $L=L(y,r)$. The scaling derivative $\widehat L=2rL'$ determines the trace of the stress tensor and a vector-field identity on Riemannian domains. For homogeneous $L=a(y)(2r)^{p/2}/p$, the divergence term in this trace vanishes when $p=m$. A conformal vector field with a strictly signed conformal factor then gives $L$-harmonicity for positive mixed tension powers, under explicit integrability and flux conditions. This applies, in particular, to hyperbolic space. On complete gradient Ricci solitons with bounded Ricci curvature, a separate cutoff argument gives a global identity for general $L$. On the cigar and on Euclidean space, direct metric variations give second-order boundary criteria that also cover tension powers $1<q<2$. The applications include target weights and the fourth-power case. Examples distinguish the annular condition from global first-derivative integrability and show why scalar growth bounds or finite tension energy alone do not imply vanishing.

papers.title: Regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities via Optimal Transport and Study of Equality Cases
papers.abstract: We consider regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities using the theory of optimal transportation, more precisely an anisotropic version of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. Furthermore, we provide a full picture concerning the issues of finiteness of the Brascamp-Lieb constant and of the existence of Gaussian extremizers, and completely determine all optimizers. The characterization of equality cases requires several new ideas to deal with difficulties, which do not appear for the non-regularized Brascamp-Lieb datum. Finally, we give applications retrieving Brascamp-Lieb-type inequalities with respect to the Gaussian measure and a regularized hypercontractivity inequality.
papers.comments: 64 pages, added a new proof of the fact that dual extremizable Brascamp-Lieb data are Gaussian extremizable, expanded technical details, corrected typos and mistakes, improved the structure of Section 4, added references

papers.title: Motivic local density of isolated surface singularities
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated algebraic surface singularity, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. In this context, we can use an additional data: the inner rate related to the bilipschitz geometry of the singularity, as studied by A. Belotto da Silva, L. Fantini and A. Pichon.

papers.title: Bicyclic graphs with the smallest and largest numbers of connected sets
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ with vertex set $V$, let N(G) denote the number of nonempty subsets of $V$ that induce a connected graph in $G$. In this paper, we focus on determining N(G) for $G$ in the family $\mathbb{B}_n$ of $n$-vertex bicyclic graphs. We find in $\mathbb{B}_n$ the structures of those graphs that possess the smallest, the largest, as well as the second-largest values of N(G). Moreover, we compute the extreme values of N(G) over $ \mathbb{B}_n$.

papers.title: A Geometric Framework for Conditional Stability in Overdetermined Elliptic Problems
papers.abstract: We present a geometric framework for studying stability and symmetry in overdetermined elliptic boundary value problems. The approach is based on a normal radial parametrization of domains with respect to a strictly convex core $C$. We establish unconditional qualitative stability for second and fourth-order problems (Serrin and Bennett--Dalmasso). We then derive conditional quantitative stability estimates assuming a residual estimate for the tangential component. The method does not rely on moving planes or the maximum principle. The quantitative results are conditional upon a sufficient analytical assumption that we carefully formulate, including a control of the tangential gradient; we verify this assumption in two model cases. The quantitative results are stated and proved in the model case $C=\{0\}$; the general strictly convex core is discussed in Remark and left for future work.

papers.title: Non-split sharply 2- and 3-transitive groups in SL_n(\mathbb Z)
papers.abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ contains a non-split sharply 2-transitive subgroup, answering a question of Glasner and Gulko. We also prove that $\mathrm{SL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ contains a non-split sharply 3-transitive subgroup, but that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ does not contain an infinite sharply 3-transitive subgroup.
papers.comments: 10 pages. Final version, incorporating the referee's comments. Published in the Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society. Update: revised a sentence in the introduction to better acknowledge previous work on sharply $3$-transitive groups

papers.title: Self-similar solutions to the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation
papers.abstract: We show the existence of self-similar solutions with constant finite mass to the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation for all spatial dimensions $d \ge 1$ and all exponents $m>m_c=(d-2)_+/d$. This range is optimal. We find two types of solution depending on the exponent: compactly supported solutions in the slow-diffusion range $m > 1$ and positive solutions with heavy tails in the sub-critical fast-diffusion range $m_c < m < 1$. The self-similar solutions in the linear case $m=1$ were already known explicitly obtained by the Fourier transform, and we discuss their properties in our settings and the limit $m \to 1$.

papers.title: Rado's covering problem for cubes and balls: a survey
papers.abstract: What is the largest constant $c\in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of axis-parallel squares in the plane admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $c$ of the area covered by $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T.~Radó in 1928, who was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. R.~Rado later generalized the problem from axis-parallel squares in the plane to homothetic copies of any given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where now we are looking for an optimal constant $F(K)$. In this paper we survey the literature on this problem, with a focus on the case where $K$ is a cube or a ball in the high-dimensional regime $d\rightarrow \infty$. The estimates that we currently have for cubes are much more precise than those for balls: namely if $Q^d$ is a $d$-dimensional cube, then \[ (e^{-1}+o(1))\frac{2^{-d}}{d \log{d}} \leq F(Q^d)\leq 2^{-d}, \] while denoting $B^d$ a $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball, then \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq F(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}.\] Except for the upper bound for cubes, which is classical, the other estimates are due to the authors.

papers.title: The singular set of the superconductivity free boundary problem
papers.abstract: We prove the uniqueness and continuous dependence of blow-ups at singular points of the free boundary for the superconductivity problem. As an application, we show that the free boundary is contained in a countable union of $C^1$ submanifolds of dimension at most $n-1$.
papers.comments: Some of the main ideas in this paper originate from arXiv:2204.11426 and are combined into the present work, which recovers its results. The preprint arXiv:2204.11426 will no longer be updated and will not be submitted for publication

papers.title: A Line-search-free Method for Adaptive Decentralized Optimization
papers.abstract: We study decentralized optimization over networks where agents cooperatively minimize a smooth (strongly) convex sum of local losses while communicating only with immediate neighbors. Prevailing decentralized methods require either centralized knowledge of global problem and network parameters for stepsize tuning--hence impractical, or costly per-iteration line-searches that demand access to local function values. We propose line-search-free, fully decentralized algorithms in which each agent adapts its stepsize using only past local iterates and gradients--with no extra function evaluations and no global tuning. The key technical ingredient is a new Lyapunov function, from which a natural adaptive stepsize rule emerges: at each iteration, each agent selects the largest stepsize that guarantees descent, based solely on a local curvature estimate built from successive gradients. The proposed algorithms enjoy strong theoretical guarantees: sublinear convergence rates for merely convex objectives and linear rates under strong convexity. Numerical experiments on standard benchmarks show consistent improvements over the state of the art, both adaptive and non-adaptive.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 6 figures, appeared at the 60th Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers (Asilomar 2026)

papers.title: Scalar Entropy and Source Terms in Harmonic Ricci Flow on Surfaces
papers.abstract: The modified scalar curvature $S=R-α|\nablaφ|^2$ satisfies a reaction--diffusion equation with a nonnegative source $Q$ under harmonic Ricci flow on a surface. The relative entropy of $|S|$ need not decrease for either sign of $S$. At a nonzero constant initial value its second time derivative is the spatial variance integral of $Q$, divided by $|S|$. We construct closed examples of both signs with spatially varying tension norm. For $S<0$, normalizing by the mass of $-S$ gives an exact covariance threshold for decay and a sufficient bound in terms of the variances of $\frac{Q}{-S}$ and $-S$, the scalar mass and density bounds, and the first positive eigenvalue. On a torus this variance bound gives decay even when the covariance is strictly negative. For $S>0$ we retain the source and boundary flux in the Hamilton square formula. In the fixed harmonic free-boundary disk case the source vanishes, and equality for a nonconstant map forces $S$ to be constant. The appendices give the boundary terms for the coupled Perelman functionals.

papers.title: On Minimal Observation Time for Recovering Latent Hawkes Networks
papers.abstract: Dynamics of interacting systems in engineering, society, and nature often evolve over latent networks that govern which entities can interact. We study the problem of inferring these networks from event-based observations, which arise naturally in finance, seismology, and neuroscience. While there is substantial algorithmic work addressing this important problem, theoretical results are scarce. In this paper we ask the following fundamental question: what is the minimum time that one must observe the dynamics in order to exactly recover the underlying network, as a function of the number $d$ of interacting entities? For a class of stationary Hawkes processes with sparse, weak interactions, we prove that an observation time of order $\log d$ is sufficient and necessary. For the upper bound we construct a two-stage estimator that uses clipped and binned event data for screening, followed by a least-squares refinement, and apply concentration bounds derived from the Poisson cluster representation. For the lower bound we combine Fano's inequality with Jacod's Girsanov formula for point processes on a suitable subclass of networks.
papers.comments: Accepted at 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

papers.title: On a PDE-based material parameter identification problem with contact constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the identification of a scalar coefficient in a PDE-based parameter estimation problem with contact constraints. The considered problem can be used as an idealized model of a membrane under forces, constrained by a barrier or indenter. More generally, it serves as a benchmark for the analysis of more complex contact problems and the development of corresponding reconstruction algorithms. In this paper, we discuss both the forward and inverse parameter estimation problems, as well as uniqueness and non-uniqueness issues caused by the contact constraints. Furthermore, we consider the design and implementation of reconstruction approaches which we test on numerical examples, illustrating both uniqueness and non-uniqueness as well as parameter identifyability.

papers.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
papers.abstract: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(β+1)}/β}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $β^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\logβ$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $β$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.
papers.comments: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Conference: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/loc/paris/poster/149032 Funded by the European Union's HORIZON-MSCA-2021-DN-01-01, through ModConFlex ("Modelling and control of flexible structures interacting with fluids"; No. 101073558; DOI: 10.3030/101073558). Code: https://github.com/albertalcalde/mean-field-transformer-concentration, code DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23726583

papers.title: From Schrodinger Bridge to Optimal Transport over Sub-Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the least-energy way to reshape a probability distribution when motion is constrained to a horizontal subbundle, i.e., optimal transport and distribution steering in sub-Riemannian geometry. It is well-known that the deterministic sub-Riemannian optimal transport problem can be complicated by the non-smooth geometry. To obtain a smooth and numerically tractable formulation, we introduce small noise that aligns with the geometry and study the associated Schrödinger bridge problem. We discuss the case where the given marginals can have compact support or have sub-Gaussian tails. Under bracket-generating hypotheses, we obtain smooth, strictly positive transition densities and a forward--backward characterization of the optimal bridge, which acts as a convex selection principle among potentially many deterministic optima. This leads to a practical Sinkhorn-type algorithm with geometric constraints and we discuss it convergence in both regimes. We show that as the noise level vanishes, the unique Schrödinger bridge minimizers converge to a minimizer of the deterministic sub-Riemannian optimal transport problem. In the case of full support regime, our result illustrates that, the existence and characterization of the unique Schrödinger bridge, Sinkhorn convergence and the convex selection principle is possible only after quantifying the smoothness and positivity of the transition density. We demonstrate with a benchmark Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Stability of Anomalous Dissipation for the Forced Three-Dimensional Navier--Stokes Equations under Geometric Perturbations
papers.abstract: The energy dissipation in the inviscid limit is a central problem in turbulence theory. Kolmogorov's 1941 (K41) theory predicts nonvanishing energy dissipation as viscosity tends to zero, a phenomenon known as anomalous dissipation. Bruè and De Lellis constructed solutions exhibiting this phenomenon, but their construction relies on precise geometric conditions. Based on quasi-self-similar mixing, we prove that anomalous dissipation persists under small pure normal perturbations of the central curves satisfying area-preserving and equal-length conditions. The perturbations vanish near the spatial endpoints and at the initial and terminal times, and smallness is measured in a mixed norm with at most two time derivatives and total order at most six. We establish stability of the area-preserving maps and full local fields, including the mixed derivatives needed for Hölder estimates of the forcing, and obtain high-frequency energy concentration. A comparison estimate and a contradiction argument give a positive dissipation lower bound uniform over the admissible perturbations. Using the $(2+\frac12)$-dimensional framework, we construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional (3D) Navier--Stokes equations with anomalous dissipation for a sequence of viscosities tending to zero.
papers.comments: 38 pages. Revised version with corrected and expanded proofs and clarified assumptions

papers.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a Hilbert space
papers.abstract: The cloud of a metric space $X$ consists of all metric spaces at finite Gromov--Hausdorff distance from $X$, with spaces at zero distance identified. We prove that the cloud of every real Hilbert space $H$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $H$.
papers.comments: 7 pages, v2 generalizes the results from v1

papers.title: Algorithms for experimenting with Zariski dense matrix groups over number fields
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be an algebraic number field. We provide a computational analog of the strong approximation theorem for finitely generated Zariski dense groups $H\leq \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{P})$, $n$ prime. That is, we present algorithms to find the set of congruence quotients of $H$ modulo all maximal ideals of a finitely generated subring $R$ of $\mathbb{P}$ such that $H\leq \mathrm{SL}(n,R)$. The algorithms have been implemented in GAP. Potential applications are illustrated by a range of experiments in degree $2$, with a special focus on Bianchi groups.

papers.title: A counterexample to a basis conjecture of Brualdi, Friedland, and Pothen
papers.abstract: Brualdi, Friedland, and Pothen conjectured that certain rank inequalities characterize bases consisting of elementary vectors in the row space of a matrix whose nonzero entries are algebraically independent. We give a $4\times6$ counterexample: all the inequalities hold, but the four elementary vectors form a minimally dependent family. A construction using two planes in a common three-dimensional subspace explains the dependence and gives a second counterexample pattern with only four prescribed zeros. We also prove that the proposed criterion is valid over every field when the number of columns exceeds the row rank by at most one. A direct-sum extension gives counterexamples of size $m\times(m+2)$ for every $m\ge4$. Thus the minimum column excess permitting a counterexample is exactly two in every such rank.
papers.comments: We replaced the \(4\times8\) example with a \(4\times6\) sparse generic matrix, with complete verification of elementary vectors, rank inequalities, and dependence. We also proved that the four vectors are minimally dependent: every proper subfamily is independent. 6 pages. Comments welcome!

papers.title: Jordan types for pairs of commuting nilpotent matrices: A survey
papers.abstract: The aim of the paper is to survey results on Jordan types for pairs of nilpotent commuting matrices. We also review recent proof of the Box Conjecture on Jordan types that have equal dense orbit in the nilpotent commutator.

papers.title: A Shape-Variational Characterisation of Multi-region Relaxed Magnetohydrodynamic Equilibria
papers.abstract: Let $Λ\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a region admitting a partition into $n$ compact, connected subregions $Λ_1,\dots,Λ_n$, each with smooth boundary such that the interfaces between regions are closed and embedded in the interior $\text{int}(Λ)$. Consider a vector field $B$ on $Λ$ where $B|_{Λ_i}$ is smooth, divergence free, and tangent to $\partial Λ_i$ for all $i$. For each such partition we show that the multi-region relaxed magnetohydrodynamics (MRxMHD) equilibrium equations are necessary and sufficient conditions for the magnetic field, together with the placement of the interfaces, to be a stationary point of the magnetic energy under appropriate constraints. We prescribe the pressure, loop-corrected helicity, and magnetic flux of $B$ through all smooth surfaces in $Λ_i$ whose boundary lies on $\partial Λ_i$. We isolate a gauge condition that is imposed implicitly in the existing toroidal treatments and show that the variation of the loop-corrected helicity cancels the corresponding boundary contribution without restricting the potentials. On toroidal domains this helicity agrees with the familiar loop-corrected expressions. For a single fixed region we give a condition on the Beltrami parameter of a region that is sufficient for a critical point of the magnetic energy to be the strict global minimiser of the energy among all admissible fields of that region. This is a condition for Beltrami fields on fixed domains that is applicable to individual regions $Λ_i$ given a fixed partition and metric.

papers.title: Construction and simulation of a path-valued model of dendrite development
papers.abstract: Neurons receive information through their dendrites. During development, when synaptic connections are forming, dendrites grow, retract, and branch. The resulting dendritic tree shapes the structure of the broader neural network. Crucially, retraction and branching make it necessary to track whole dendritic paths rather than only their endpoints. While this is handled implicitly in some existing simulations, here we construct an explicitly path-valued stochastic process for dendrite growth. Combining this with a branching process, using ideas from measure-valued branching particle systems, we show that the model produces the typical tree structures of real dendrites. To complement this analytical work, we also outline several methods for numerical simulation, including time discretisations at different temporal scales and an approximation using a dynamic graph. This provides both a more rigorous mathematical framework and more structured simulation methods for modelling dendrite development.

papers.title: Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers for Generalized Newtonian Models
papers.abstract: We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems. At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic $λ$-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the $p$-Laplacian and $p$-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for $4/3\le p\le 4$, $p\ne2$, with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range. We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.

papers.title: Beyond the probabilistic scaling for NLS on the ball
papers.abstract: We construct probabilistic strong solutions to the cubic Schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional ball with radial initial data, which is a significant improvement of a result by Bourgain--Bulut. These solutions lie in the supercritical regime with respect to the probabilistic scaling introduced by Deng--Nahmod--Yue. We achieve this result through gauge transformations, without renormalization, combined with a refined modulation analysis using random averaging operators.

papers.title: On the sharp linear convergence rate of the circumcentered--reflection method on subspaces
papers.abstract: For two subspaces $U,V\subseteq\RR^n$, the circumcentered--reflection method (CRM) of Behling, Bello-Cruz, and Santos~\citeyearpar{BBS2018} computes the projection onto $U\cap V$ using only the reflections across $U$ and $V$, with known linear-convergence rate equal to the cosine of the Friedrichs angle. We prove that, when CRM is initialized in $V$, it contracts at the strictly smaller rate $ρ_V=(\sin^2θ_p-\sin^2θ_F)/(\sin^2θ_p+\sin^2θ_F)$, where $θ_F\in(0,π/2]$ is the Friedrichs angle, whose cosine we denote by $c_F\coloneqq\cosθ_F$, and $θ_p\in[θ_F,π/2]$ is the largest principal angle between $U$ and $V$. The bound is sharp, attained on an explicit ray in $V$, and optimal among parameter-free single-step iterations. The constant itself is not new: Bauschke, Bello-Cruz, Nghia, Phan, and Wang~\citeyearpar{BBNPW2016} identified it as the optimal rate of the relaxed alternating-projection family and of their adaptive linesearch map $B_T$. Our contribution is that the parameter-free geometric circumcenter attains it as well, via Kantorovich's inequality applied to a single self-adjoint operator on $V$. Restricted to $V$, CRM coincides pointwise with the linesearch maps $A_T$ and $B_T$ from the Gubin--Polyak--Raik framework~\citep{GPR1967}. We further prove $ρ_V<c_F^2$ whenever $θ_F<π/2$, with one-step convergence exactly when $θ_F=θ_p$. Over-reflecting either or both of $R_U$, $R_V$ inside the circumcenter does not help. Going faster than $ρ_V$ universally requires memory: Chebyshev semi-iteration applied to $P_VP_U$ attains a strictly smaller rate, beating $ρ_V$ by a factor at most $2$, attained in the limit $θ_F\toθ_p$.

papers.title: Bidirectional Random Projections
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes bidirectional random projections for ordinary least squares (OLS) regression under the fixed design setting. Let $(X, Y) \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a sample and $W \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n}$, $R \in \mathbb{R}^{p\times p_1}$ be two random projections. We develop an expected excess loss bound for the OLS estimator built on $(WXR, WY)$, extending an established bound for the OLS estimator built on $(XR, Y)$. Our analysis shows that our bound is larger and the gap between the two bounds decays at a rate of approximately $O(1/n_1)$. These findings are confirmed by numerical results.
papers.comments: v2: correct the sketching constant, update the bound interpretation and numerical results, release source code

papers.title: On concatenation of matrices for reversible linear codes over a finite commutative ring and applications to DNA codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a generalized framework for constructing reversible linear, reversible self dual and reversible DNA codes using a matrix-theoretic approach based on involutory matrices. The proposed concatenation scheme gives a large class of generator matrices and yields codes with good parameters. The construction is carried out at the level of linear codes and then extended to DNA codes. Using a matrix product approach, we provide a unified method for analysis and proof. Further, we resolve an open problem raised by Oztas et.al. and also we correct and improve some results of them.

papers.title: Multi-Stage Stochastic Optimization and Reinforcement Learning Approaches for Dynamic Inspection of Infrastructure Systems
papers.abstract: We study a dynamic inspection problem for infrastructure systems in which we route and schedule multiple vehicles to monitor components that are subject to heterogeneous stochastic failures. Inspection decisions determine which components the vehicles serve first and thus affect how failures propagate to neighboring components. We formulate the problem as a multi-stage stochastic mixed-integer program that jointly optimizes routing and scheduling under exogenous and decision-dependent uncertainty. We develop a stochastic dual dynamic integer programming (SDDiP) algorithm based on a stage decomposition of the multi-stage model and show that it converges finitely to the optimal value. In parallel, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) approach that learns assignment policies from simulated system dynamics. On instances built from the road and storm-sewer networks of Sioux Falls, SDDiP proves optimality where the extended formulation of the same model leaves large gaps. On larger instances, RL with a routable-assignment certificate often finds cheaper policies than SDDiP under a short computational budget, whereas SDDiP finds cheaper policies and bounds on their quality with more time. Moreover, modeling failure propagation and decision-dependent transition probabilities reduces the realized cost when these mechanisms are present. These comparisons guide the choice between optimization and policy learning for inspection planning under failure risk.

papers.title: Super-Arrhenius relaxation of the triangular plaquette model in any dimension
papers.abstract: Consider the following plaquette model from statistical physics: a lamp lies at every vertex of the triangular lattice and a switch lies at every even vertex of the (bipartite) dual hexagonal lattice. Each switch toggles the three lamps on its face. The energy of a configuration is the number of ON lamps. For the Glauber dynamics associated with the Gibbs measure defined by this Hamiltonian at any inverse temperature $β>0$, we show that, in any dimension $d\ge 2$, the infinite volume relaxation time satisfies \[e^{β^2/C}/C \le T_{\mathrm{rel}}\le Ce^{e^{Cβ}}\] for some $C>0$. Our result entails that the Gibbs measure is unique. The $e^{β^2}$ scaling was conjectured by Garrahan and Newman in 2000 and matches the behaviour of supercritical rooted kinetically constrained models such as the East model, thus recovering fragile glass phenomenology in the absence of kinetic constraints. More precisely, we show that, on a torus of side length $2^k$, when $β\to\infty$ and $k/β\to0$, we have $T_{\mathrm{rel}}=e^{2βk(1+o(1))}$, confirming a prediction of Newman and Moore. Quite surprisingly, however, we also prove that, on non-periodic finite domains of size $n\le e^{β/C}$ for large $C>0$, we have the much larger asymptotics $\ln T_{\mathrm{rel}}=βn^{Θ(1)}$. The main ingredients of the proofs are new results in extremal and enumerative combinatorics and rely on renormalisation ideas for the dynamics and its groundstates also known as the Ledrappier subshift. Our combinatorial results also have consequences in geometric group theory (more precisely to the complexity of the word problem for the Baumslag finitely presented group), ergodic theory and linear coding theory.
papers.comments: 49 pages, 8 figures, improved presentation, added Sections 1.3.4 and 6 on linear error-correcting codes

papers.title: The Loss of Tension in an Infinite Membrane with Holes of Decaying Spatial Density
papers.abstract: What is the effect of randomly removing material from an infinite stretched membrane? Under what conditions can the membrane still sustain tension? This problem was introduced by Robert Connelly in connection with applications of rigidity theory in the natural sciences, and was later studied in M. V. Menshikov, K. A. Rybnikov, and S. E. Volkov, "The loss of tension in an infinite membrane with holes distributed according to a Poisson law" (2002); a discrete version was also considered in Robert Connelly, Konstantin Rybnikov, and Stanislav Volkov, "Percolation and the Loss of Tension in an Infinite Triangular Lattice" (2001). We study a mathematical framework based on a non-homogeneous Poisson point process whose intensity $λ$ tends to zero at infinity. The hole shapes are i.i.d.\ and independent of their locations. We show that if the intensity does not decay too quickly, then tension is still lost throughout the whole plane, as in the homogeneous model studied in 2002. Conversely, we give sufficient conditions under which complete loss of tension does not occur. Thus, both destruction and non-destruction regimes are possible even when the intensity tends to zero, indicating a phase transition in the model. The processes studied here are closely related to bootstrap percolation.

papers.title: Subhypergraph counts and proofs of two conjectures of Alon
papers.abstract: For a fixed integer $r\ge2$ and a finite simple $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ without isolated vertices, let $N_r(m,H)$ be the maximum number of unlabelled copies of $H$ among all finite simple $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $m$ edges. Friedgut and Kahn [Isr. J. Math., 1998] proved that $N_r(m,H)=Θ_H(m^{ρ^*(H)})$, where $ρ^*(H)$ is the fractional edge-cover number of $H$. We sharpen this to $N_r(m,H)=(λ_r(H)+o(1))m^{ρ^*(H)}$ as $m\to\infty$, with $λ_r(H)>0$, and characterize the limiting $λ_r(H)$ by a variational problem over finite hypergraphs. We develop a globally rainbow compression argument combining color-coding with successive vertex cloning. In particular, when $r=2$, the asymptotic formula confirms a conjecture of Alon [Isr. J. Math., Conjecture 1, 1986]. Moreover, for graphs we express the limiting constant $λ_2(H)$ as a supremum over finite cores. We also prove that, for every prescribed number of edges, an extremal graph for a star forest can be chosen to be a star forest, confirming another conjecture of Alon [Isr. J. Math., Conjecture 2, 1986].
papers.comments: 24 pages. This version extends the main asymptotic counting result from graphs to uniform hypergraphs. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Learning Locally Stable Neural ODEs and Their Regions of Attraction
papers.abstract: We propose a class of neural ODEs that are hard-constrained to have a locally exponentially stable equilibrium point at the origin, with an exactly characterized region of attraction. The model obtains its dynamics by passing an arbitrary neural vector field through a projection layer defined by a jointly learned Lyapunov function. By design, this function satisfies a variant of the Zubov equation for the projected dynamics and is therefore a maximal Lyapunov function for the projected system. As a result, the projected dynamics are locally exponentially stable at the origin, and the region of attraction is exactly given by the 1-sublevel set of the Lyapunov function. We prove that this model class universally approximates any sufficiently smooth dynamics that are locally exponentially stable at the origin on their region of attraction, and propose an implementation that is consistent with the theory. The approach is validated experimentally on nonlinear systems with nonconvex regions of attraction.

papers.title: Consecutive integers free of certain prime factors
papers.abstract: Let $n_k$ denote the least integer $n>2k$ such that $(n-k)(n-k+1)\cdots(n-1)$ is not divisible by any prime in the interval $(k,2k)$. Confirming a conjecture of Erdős, we prove that, for all sufficiently large $k$, $$ n_k > e^{\frac{\log^2 k}{20 \log \log k}}. $$
papers.comments: 6 pages. Revised version; accepted for publication in Journal of Number Theory

papers.title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For a central division $F$-algebras $L$ of a fixed degree $n$ we identify the double quotients of the homogeneous spaces $L_E^\times/L^\times$ with a topological space $Ξ_E$ which does not depend on a choice of $L$ , define a convolution products $\ast _L$ on the space ${\mathcal M} _E$ compactly supported measures on $Ξ_E$ and conjecture that the product $\ast _L$ on $Ξ_E$ does not depend on a choice of $L$.

papers.title: On the Benign Optimization Landscape and Geometry of Heteroscedastic Probabilistic PCA
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the global optimization landscape and local geometry of heteroscedastic probabilistic principal component analysis (HePPCA). Since the signal strengths and noise variances are often unknown in practice, we analyze a formulation that uses fixed plug-in estimates of these parameters. We first show that the population HePPCA problem is an instance of a homogeneous quadratic program with orthogonality constraints (QPOC). For QPOC, we first derive a necessary and sufficient condition for a critical point to be a global maximizer and explicitly construct a positive-curvature direction at every nonglobal critical point. This establishes a benign optimization landscape of QPOC in which every critical point is either a global maximizer or a strict saddle point. Building on this analysis, we establish quantitative curvature bounds for population HePPCA, yielding local geodesic strong concavity near every global maximizer and uniformly positive curvature in suitable tangent directions at all nonglobal critical points. Combining these results with a deterministic perturbation argument and sample covariance concentration bounds, we derive a sufficient sample-size condition under which empirical HePPCA inherits the benign landscape and local geodesic strong concavity with high probability. Finally, we present numerical experiments to corroborate our theoretical results.

papers.title: The curvature of left-invariant magnetic systems
papers.abstract: We compute the magnetic curvatures (in the sense of Assenza) of left-invariant magnetic systems on Lie groups and explore relations between curvature properties and algebraic properties, extending to the magnetic setting a number of results from Milnor's classic 1976 paper on the geometry of left-invariant metrics. We also discuss the existence of non-trivial bi-invariant magnetic systems and exhibit the resulting curvature formulas in some concrete examples, including the Heisenberg group.
papers.comments: Theorem C improved, and other minor adjustments

papers.title: A sharp inverse theorem for the quadratic large sieve
papers.abstract: We prove that if $A\subseteq[N]$, $|A|\gg\sqrt N$, and $|A_p|\le p/2+O(1)$ for every prime $p\ll\log N$, then $A$ contains at least $\exp(c\sqrt{\log N}/\log\log N)$ elements in the image of a single integral quadratic $m\pm x^2$. A matching construction shows that this is optimal even when the quadratic may be chosen arbitrarily in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
papers.comments: 24 pages, this version contains stronger results

papers.title: Baxter Q-operators from a Schwinger-Boson construction of the master T-operator and the mKP hierarchy
papers.abstract: The master T-operator is a generating function for transfer matrices and a tau-function of the modified KP (mKP) hierarchy. It is conventionally introduced through a Schur-function expansion whose coefficients are fused transfer matrices satisfying the Cherednik--Bazhanov--Reshetikhin determinant formula. For rational inhomogeneous gl(M) spin chains, we give an alternative definition: we realize gl(M) on an auxiliary Fock space generated by finitely many families of Schwinger bosons, form a monodromy matrix from the resulting L-operator, and define the master T-operator as its trace over the Fock space. Howe duality then reproduces the Schur-function expansion. This realization relates two constructions of Baxter Q-operators. In the construction of [arXiv:1112.3310] (see also [arXiv:1010.4022]), the Q-operators are obtained from residues of the master T-operator with respect to selected Miwa variables. In the construction of [arXiv:1010.3699], they are defined using degenerate Yangian L-operators in oscillator form. When selected Miwa variables approach the inverses of boundary-twist eigenvalues, the defining trace develops poles. After a suitable rescaling of this L-operator, only the terms contributing to the highest-order pole survive in the normalized limit; before the trace is taken, they form the degenerate Yangian L-operator of the second construction. The trace then gives an explicit residue formula for the corresponding Q-operator.
